Unlock these with Subscription Eminent painter Jogen Chowdhury died at a private hospital in Kolkata on Sunday morning (October 25, 2026) following a prolonged battle with a rare blood cancer. He was 87. Watch | Peek into Jogen Chowdhury’s lifetime through his art exhibition in Mumbai Mr. Chowdhury, a former TMC MP, had been suffering from a myeloproliferative neoplasm, a rare type of blood cancer, for the past 14 months and was undergoing chemotherapy, Ruby General Hospital said in a statement. He was admitted to the hospital in southeast Kolkata on October 16 and breathed his last at 10.15 a.m., it said. Also read | In Jogen Chowdhury’s 80th year, an exhibition that celebrates the leading modern artist "It is with profound sadness that we announce the demise of Shri. Jogen Chowdhury, the renowned Indian painter," the hospital said. During the course of his illness, Mr. Chowdhury had also required hospitalisation for urinary tract infections, it added. Condoling his death, Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said Chowdhury's works would remain "immortal through the ages". Describing him as an artist of great stature, Mr. Adhikari said the body of work he had left behind was a treasure for the state and the nation. "Chowdhury's rich contributions are evident in numerous government buildings, including Rashtrapati Bhavan. The works he left behind will remain for centuries," he said. Former CM Mamata Banerjee said Mr. Chowdhury was the pride of Bengal and India. "A great inspiration to artists worldwide, and me personally. My condolences to his family, friends, and admirers all over the world," she said in a social media post. Ms. Banerjee recalled that he was elected to the Rajya Sabha on a Trinamool Congress ticket and served from 2014 to 2020, and that her government conferred the Banga Bibhushan, one of the State's highest civilian honours, on him in 2012. "His passing away will create an irreparable void in the world of art and culture," she said. Painter Samir Aich also mourned Mr. Chowdhury's death, describing it as a "personal loss". His passing marked the death of an art form in the country, including the Bengal School of Art, Aich said. Bengali writer Sirshendu Mukhopadhyay also mourned the painter's death, describing him as a longtime friend and associate. "Jogen was a long-term friend and associate, and I have memories of 'adda' with him. His death is a great loss," he said. Mr. Chowdhury also had a house in Santiniketan, where the region's red earth and distinctive landscape served as inspiration for his artworks. Born on February 16, 1939, in Daharpara village in Faridpur, then part of undivided Bengal, Mr. Chowdhury developed an early interest in art under the influence of his mother, who was skilled in 'alpana', a traditional form of floor art. During Partition, his family moved to Kolkata, where he received formal training in art. Mr. Chowdhury began his career as an art teacher at Howrah Zilla School before joining the Handloom Board in Kolkata as a designer in 1962. In the late 1960s, he went to Paris for higher studies at the Ecole Nationale Superieure des Beaux-Arts. He developed his distinctive artistic style after returning to India. Known for his unique visual language, Mr. Chowdhury drew inspiration from political and social themes as well as Indian and European art movements. 著名画家乔根·乔杜里在与一种罕见血癌长期抗争后，于2026年10月25日星期日上午在加尔各答一家私立医院去世，享年87岁。

观看｜通过在孟买举办的乔根·乔杜里艺术展，回顾他的一生

Ruby General Hospital在一份声明中表示，曾担任TMC国会议员的乔杜里先生过去14个月一直患有骨髓增殖性肿瘤，这是一种罕见的血癌，并接受了化疗。他于10月16日入住加尔各答东南部这家医院，于上午10时15分去世。

另请阅读｜在乔根·乔杜里80岁之际，一场展览向这位杰出的现代艺术家致敬

医院表示：“我们怀着深切的悲痛宣布，著名印度画家乔根·乔杜里先生逝世。”医院补充称，乔杜里先生在患病期间还曾因尿路感染住院。

首席部长苏文杜·阿迪卡里对乔杜里去世表示哀悼，称他的作品将“世代不朽”。阿迪卡里先生称乔杜里是一位成就卓著的艺术家，他留下的作品宝库是邦和国家的财富。他说：“乔杜里丰富的艺术贡献体现在众多政府建筑中，包括Rashtrapati Bhavan。他留下的作品将流传数百年。”

前首席部长马马塔·班纳吉表示，乔杜里先生是孟加拉邦和印度的骄傲。她在社交媒体帖子中写道：“他是世界各地艺术家以及我个人的一位伟大榜样。我向他的家人、朋友和全世界所有仰慕者致以慰问。”班纳吉女士回顾说，他曾以印度人民党候选人的身份当选联邦院议员，任职时间为2014年至2020年；她的政府于2012年授予他该邦最高荣誉之一“Banga Bibhushan”。她说：“他的离世将在艺术和文化领域留下无法弥补的空缺。”

画家萨米尔·艾奇也悼念乔杜里先生，称他的去世对个人而言是“一项损失”。艾奇说，他的离世意味着这个国家的一种艺术形式，包括孟加拉艺术流派，也随之消逝。孟加拉作家西尔申杜·穆克帕德亚也悼念这位画家的离世，称他是自己多年的朋友和伙伴。他说：“乔根是位长期交往的朋友和伙伴，我与他一起‘闲聊’的回忆至今仍历历在目。他的离世是一大损失。”

乔杜里先生在桑蒂尼凯坦也有一处住所，该地区的红土和独特风景曾为他的艺术作品带来灵感。他于1939年2月16日出生在当时仍属 undivided Bengal的法里德普尔县Daharpara村。在母亲的影响下，他 early 对艺术产生了兴趣；他的母亲精通“alpana”，这是一种传统的地面绘画艺术。印巴分治期间，他的家人迁居加尔各答，他在那里接受了正规的艺术训练。

乔杜里先生最初在Howrah Zilla School担任美术教师，1962年加入加尔各答手工艺委员会，担任设计师。20世纪60年代末，他赴巴黎，在Ecole Nationale Superieure des Beaux-Arts深造。回到印度后，他形成了独特的艺术风格。乔杜里先生以独特的视觉语言闻名，从政治和社会主题以及印度和欧洲艺术运动中汲取灵感。

Unlock these with Subscription Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Minister Eshwar Khandre has said that there is no shortage of funds to handle the drought situation in the State. The State government has released ₹306 crore for drinking water supply and other drought-relief works. Speaking to reporters during his visit to Shivamogga on Sunday (October 25, 2026), Mr. Khandre said that, in addition to this amount, the Deputy Commissioners also had sufficient funds at their disposal. “The State government is well prepared to handle the drought. There is no shortage of funds to ensure drinking water supply in rural areas,” he said. Officers have been instructed to ensure drinking water supply either through tankers or by hiring private borewells. “There is no need to worry. If any borewell dries up, an alternative arrangement will be made within 24 hours. We are prepared to handle the situation in rural areas,” he said. On the elections to rural local bodies, Mr. Khandre said that the State government had already issued the draft notification on the delimitation of constituencies and reservation. The elections would be held either at the end of December or in January 2027. “The deadline for filing objections to the draft notification was October 19. The final notification will be issued after the objections are reviewed,” he said. Mr. Khandre took part in a felicitation programme organised by the Veerashaiva-Lingayat Mahasabha in Shivamogga. The Mahasabha had chosen his late father, Bheemanna Khandre, for the Keladi Shivappa Nayaka Award for 2023-24. Mr. Eshwar Khandre received the award on his father’s behalf. Addressing the gathering, Mr. Khandre said that Veerashaiva and Lingayat were two sides of the same coin and that nobody could divide the community. He said he would visit the Anubhava Mantapa being constructed at Basava Kalyana at a cost of ₹750 crore, and that efforts would be made to complete the construction before the next Basava Jayanti. Responding to the Mahasabha’s demand to declare Malnad as “Keladi Karnataka,” the Minister said he would discuss the matter with the Chief Minister. Major Deeksha C. Mudadevannanavar of the Indian Army Medical Corps, who became the first woman officer to receive the Para Special Forces’ Balidaan Badge, was honoured with the Keladi Chennamma Award. Unlock these with Subscription The Congress on Sunday (October 25, 2026) demanded the resignation of Manipur Chief Minister Y. Khemchand Singh, alleging a failure to contain renewed violence in the State. It said no armed group or individual attacking civilians should enjoy “political protection or immunity”. Addressing a press conference, Congress MP and Manipur in-charge Saptagiri Ulaka called for time-bound investigations and prosecution in cases of killings, firing, arson, and destruction of civilian property. Referring to the protests on Friday (October 23), Mr. Ulaka said thousands of people across five districts took to the streets and marched towards Lok Bhavan before police stopped them. They carried out unique “sound protests”, Mr. Ulaka said, using the very technique prescribed by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who had asked Indians to bang utensils during the COVID pandemic. The police, he alleged, used a heavy hand to suppress the protest by using tear gas shells and lathi charge against the people. The Congress leaders cited recent incidents of violence, including the killing of three Meitei civilians collecting firewood on October 19 and clashes in Kamjong district in which Kuki and Naga civilians were killed. Mahila Congress president Alka Lamba, who visited Manipur earlier this month, said women affected by the conflict continued to face hardship. “The BJP government in Manipur has completely failed to stop the violence there,” she said. Mr. Ulaka alleged that armed groups possessed more sophisticated weapons than security forces. He said around 300 people had been killed since May 2023, while nearly 60,000 were displaced, with about 24,000 yet to return home. The Congress leaders called for immediate protection of civilians in vulnerable areas, strict enforcement of the suspension-of-operations ground rules, restoration of free movement across the State, and a credible roadmap for rehabilitation and the return of displaced persons. They demanded dissolution of the Assembly and fresh elections, alongside an intervention by the Union government to end the violence and initiate an inclusive peace process. The ethnic conflict between the Meitei and Kuki communities that began in May 2023 has claimed more than 300 lives and displaced thousands. 国大党领导人列举了近期发生的暴力事件，包括10月19日三名拾取柴火的Meitei平民被杀，以及Kamjong地区发生冲突，Kuki和Naga平民在冲突中丧生。

女国大党主席Alka Lamba本月早些时候访问那普尔邦后表示，受冲突影响的妇女仍面临困境。她说：“那普尔邦的印度人民党政府完全未能阻止当地暴力事件。”

Ulaka先生指称，武装团体拥有的武器比安全部队更加先进。他说，自2023年5月以来，已有约300人死亡，近6万人流离失所，其中约2.4万人尚未返回家园。

国大党领导人呼吁立即保护脆弱地区的平民，严格执行停火基本规则，恢复全邦自由通行，并制定可信的安置方案，让流离失所者返乡。他们要求解散议会并重新举行选举，同时要求中央政府介入，结束暴力事件并启动包容各方的和平进程。

2023年5月爆发的Meitei与Kuki族群冲突已造成300多人死亡，数千人流离失所。近几个月还发生了涉及Kuki和Naga群体的冲突。

Unlock these with Subscription Published - October 25, 2026 04:47 pm IST - THIRUVANANTHAPURAM In an unprecedented move, former Keralam Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar has reportedly recommended to the President the removal of Kerala Public Service Commission (PSC) chairperson M.R. Baiju over alleged irregularities in the running of the recruitment body. The recommendation came out in the public domain hardly a few days after he left the State and was succeeded by Om Prakash Mathur as the Governor . He is learnt to have sent a communication to President Droupadi Murmu in this regard a week before he was relieved of his duties. A Crime Branch investigation into the alleged irregularities in the PSC examination for certain posts in the State Planning Board is currently progressing. Criticising the move, Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan said that the recommendation to remove the PSC chairperson and dissolve the commission is unlawful, a violation of constitutional provisions, and a gross abuse of power. Under Article 317 of the Constitution, the President can remove a PSC chairperson or member on grounds of misbehaviour only after the Supreme Court, following an inquiry, has reported that they should be removed. "No such inquiry has been conducted by the Supreme Court regarding the members of the Kerala PSC. Consequently, the Governor possesses no constitutional authority to make such a recommendation. It appears that the former Governor has made this recommendation as a final act—a continuation of the unlawful interventions he has made in the State throughout his tenure. This is a conspiracy to undermine the credibility of the entire system by alleging irregularities in a single instance of recruitment," he said He further said that Article 163 unequivocally states that the Governor can only act in accordance with the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers. This implies that the Governor possesses no independent authority in this regard. Furthermore, under Article 317, the Council of Ministers cannot take any such decision except on the basis of a report following an inquiry by the Supreme Court. The action taken by the Governor is entirely unconstitutional and unlawful, he said. Mr. Vijayan said that the move raises concerns about the use of Lok Bhavans for the Bharatiya Janata Party’s (BJP) political agenda. There is no precedent in Keralam of approaching the PSC with a motive of political vendetta. The Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) government must clarify its stand and unequivocally oppose any attempt to bypass constitutional procedures or undermine institutional autonomy, he said in a statement. "Does the government intend to use this unlawful act by the Governor as a pretext to dissolve the existing PSC—driven by political partisanship and prejudice—thereby aligning itself with the Governor’s move? Or is it prepared to condemn the Governor’s stance? On the other hand, if the government intends to provide support—whether directly or indirectly—to the unlawful actions of the Governors, it will have to pay a heavy price. Such a move would pave the way for authoritarian tendencies," said Mr.Vijayan. Comments have to be in English, and in full sentences. They cannot be abusive or personal. https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.title: [COVER STORY] Kim Jong-un's China trip reaffirms 'blood ties' as Beijing watches Moscow
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong-un’s trip to the Chinese border city of Dandong, made days before the anniversary of Chinese troops entering the 1950-53 Korean War, was aimed at reaffirming the historic blood ties between the two countries at a moment when Pyongyang’s alignment with Moscow has drawn Beijing’s attention, experts said.
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.summary_zh: experts: 朝鲜领导人金正恩访问中国边境城市丹东的行程安排在1950年至1953年朝鲜战争中国军队参战周年纪念日的前几天。专家表示，此举旨在两国重新确认历史上的血缘联系；此时，平壤与莫斯科的结盟已引起北京的关注。
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.body: North Korean leader Kim Jong-un’s trip to the Chinese border city of Dandong, made days before the anniversary of Chinese troops entering the 1950-53 Korean War, was aimed at reaffirming the historic blood ties between the two countries at a moment when Pyongyang’s alignment with Moscow has drawn Beijing’s attention, experts said. North's state-run Rodong Sinmun on Sunday reported Kim's visit to the Memorial Hall of the War to Resist U.S. Aggression and Aid Korea in Dandong the previous day. The state media repeatedly emphasized Kim's paying tribute to fallen Chinese troops, remembering their shared history of fighting alongside North Korean forces and preserving ties forged in blood. Kang Dong-wan, a professor of North Korean studies at Dong-A University, said the focus on China’s role in the war was deliberate, coming after a period in which the Beijing relationship had weakened relative to Pyongyang’s deepening partnership with Moscow, including the North’s troop deployment to Russia. "Kim's decision to visit the Memorial Hall among other possible destinations appears to intend to highlight the historic blood ties between North Korea and China," Kang said. Hong Min, a senior research fellow at the Korea Institute for National Unification, read the visit as carrying a message beyond the bilateral relationship. "North Korea and China reaffirmed their shared history of fighting against the U.S. and their blood-forged alliance," he said, underlining North Korean media's repeated emphasis on their blood ties. Kim did not meet Chinese President Xi Jinping during the trip. He instead held talks with Wang Huning, China’s fourth-ranking official, who chairs the National Committee of the Chinese People’s Political Consultative Conference and sits on the Standing Committee of the Communist Party’s Political Bureau, along with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi. Kang said the absence of a Xi meeting was unremarkable given the trip’s purpose. "As Kim sought to express gratitude to China and reaffirm bilateral friendship, a meeting with Xi was not the main purpose of the visit in the first place," he explained, pointing to scheduling issues. "Chinese Communist Party's fifth plenum is reportedly scheduled for next week. This could have contributed to the absence of not only Xi but also Chinese Premier Li Qiang, who had originally been reported to welcome Kim," Hong said. Kim’s day trip drew attention for the route he took — the New Amnok River Bridge, which opened on Oct. 15 after more than a decade of delay. The two countries agreed to build it in 2010, and China completed construction in 2014, but the crossing sat unused for years because the North Korean side lacked connecting roads and customs facilities. "This demonstrates that Kim can now visit China for strategic consultations within a single day, allowing for more frequent high-level exchanges between the two countries," Hong said. The route also carries an economic message, signaling Pyongyang's willingness to strengthen trade ties with Beijing. "By personally endorsing the full operation of the New Amnok River Bridge, Kim demonstrated his commitment to expanding cross-border trade and economic cooperation," said Yang Moo-jin, a distinguished professor at the University of North Korean Studies in Seoul. While some experts say the possibility of talks between Kim and U.S. President Donald Trump cannot be ruled out, particularly ahead of the upcoming Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in November, others remain skeptical. With renewed dialogue between Washington and Pyongyang being discussed and given Kim's multiple visits to China during his talks with Trump between 2018 and 2019, it is difficult to rule out a possible link between his latest visit and potential Trump-Kim talks. "Given Wang Huning's close ties to Xi Jinping, indirect communication between Kim and Xi may have taken place through Wang," said Yang. He also did not rule out the possibility of Wang visiting Pyongyang as Xi's special envoy or Kim being invited to China around the APEC summit. However, others evaluated the likelihood of a Trump-Kim meeting low. "It is highly unlikely that Kim discussed a potential meeting with Trump during his visit to China," said Lim Eul-chul, a professor at Kyungnam University's Institute for Far Eastern Studies. "There is little circumstantial evidence suggesting that Kim is acting with a potential U.S.-North Korea summit or his negotiating leverage in mind." Hong also said there was no clear indication linking Kim's latest visit to the possibility of renewed talks with Washington
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.title_zh: 【封面故事】金正恩访华重申“血缘纽带”，北京观望莫斯科
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.body_zh: 专家表示，朝鲜领导人金正恩在中国边境城市丹东的行程安排在中国军队进入1950年至1953年朝鲜战争纪念日前夕，旨在两国与莫斯科的靠拢引发北京关注之际，重新确认两国之间的历史血缘纽带。朝鲜国家经营的《劳动新闻》周日报道称，金正恩前一天参观了丹东的抗美援朝纪念馆。朝鲜官方媒体反复强调，金正恩向阵亡的中国烈士致敬，缅怀双方并肩抗击朝鲜军队的共同历史，维系以鲜血铸就的纽带。东亚大学朝鲜研究所教授姜东万表示，聚焦中国在战争中的作用是经过深思熟虑的。此前，在朝鲜深化与莫斯科伙伴关系（包括向俄罗斯部署朝鲜军队）之际，北京与朝鲜的关系相对减弱。姜东万说：“在众多可选目的地中，金正恩决定参观纪念馆，显然意在突出朝鲜与中国的历史血缘纽带。”韩国统一研究院高级研究员洪民认为，此访除传递双边关系信息外，还含有更深层含义。他说：“朝鲜和中国重申了共同抗击美国的历史以及以鲜血铸成的联盟。”他强调，朝鲜媒体反复突出双方的血缘纽带。此次行程中，金正恩没有会见中国国家主席习近平，而是与中国排名第四的王沪宁以及中国外交部长王毅进行了会谈。王沪宁担任中国人民政治协商会议全国委员会主席，并任中国共产党政治局常务委员会委员。姜东万说，鉴于此访目的，未安排金正恩与习近平会面并不令人意外。他解释道：“金正恩寻求向中国表达感谢并重申双边友好，因此从一开始，与习近平会面就不是此访的主要目的。”他指出，日程安排也是影响因素。洪民说：“据报道，中国共产党第五次全体会议计划于下周举行。这或许不仅导致习近平未能出席，也导致原定欢迎金正恩的中国国务院总理李强未能现身。”金正恩的当日行程因其所经路线而引人关注，即新鸭绿江大桥。该桥于10月15日开放，经历了十多年延误。两国于2010年同意修建该桥，中国于2014年完成建设，但由于朝鲜一侧缺乏连接道路和海关设施，这座跨境大桥多年未能投入使用。洪民说：“这表明金正恩如今可以在一天之内赴中国进行战略磋商，从而为两国之间更频繁的高层交流创造条件。”这条路线还传递出经济层面的信息，显示平壤愿意加强与北京的贸易关系。首尔大学朝鲜研究院特聘教授杨穆镇说：“金正恩亲自支持新鸭绿江大桥全面运营，表明他致力于扩大跨境贸易和经济合作。”一些专家认为，尤其考虑到11月即将举行的亚太经济合作组织（APEC）峰会，金正恩与美国总统唐纳德·特朗普会谈的可能性无法排除；另一些人则持怀疑态度。随着华盛顿与平壤重新展开对话的讨论不断深入，加上金正恩曾在2018年至2019年与特朗普会谈期间多次访问中国，因此很难排除此次最新访问与潜在特朗普—金正恩会谈之间存在联系。杨穆镇说：“鉴于王沪宁与习近平关系密切，金正恩与习近平之间可能通过王沪宁进行了间接沟通。”他也没有排除王沪宁作为习近平特使访问平壤，或金正恩在亚太经济合作组织峰会前后获邀访华的可能性。不过 Others 对特朗普与金正恩会面的可能性评估较低。庆南大学远东研究所教授林日哲说：“金正恩在访华期间讨论与特朗普潜在会面的可能性极低。”“几乎没有间接证据表明，金正恩此次行动考虑了潜在的美朝峰会或他的谈判筹码。”洪民还表示，没有明确迹象将金正恩此次最新访问与恢复同华盛顿对话的可能性联系起来

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/business/te.summary_zh: 韩国智库Rockbridge Network Korea最近发布的一份报告显示，在韩国机构今年1月至8月于Hugging Face发布的1,845个模型中，49.3%以中国模型为基础，35.9%以美国模型为基础，14.9%基于韩国国内模型。近年来，以中国模型为基础构建的新模型占比迅速增长，从2023年的1.2%跃升至2025年的22%，今年又几乎翻了一番。
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/business/te.body: According to a recent report by think tank Rockbridge Network Korea, Sunday, 49.3 percent of the 1,845 models published by Korea-based accounts on Hugging Face between January and August were based on Chinese models, compared with 35.9 percent based on U.S. models and 14.9 percent on domestic models. The share of new models built on Chinese foundations has been rapidly growing in past years, surging from 1.2 percent in 2023 to 22 percent in 2025, before nearly doubling this year. Qwen was the most widely used foundation model, accounting for 46.8 percent of the total, or 864 models. Google's Gemma ranked second with 14.7 percent, followed by Meta's Llama with 13.8 percent. LG AI Research's EXAONE ranked fourth at 9.3 percent, while Kakao's Kanana accounted for 2.7 percent. Popular AI foundation models, such as OpenAI's GPT, Anthropic's Claude and Google's Gemini, are closed models whose underlying weights are not publicly available. In contrast, Alibaba's Qwen and Google's Gemma allow developers to download and modify the models for their own purposes. Such models, known as open-weight models, are easier to adapt for specific applications thanks to their publicly available weights, including through fine-tuning with Korean-language data, without relying on cloud-based AI services. The report noted that low costs and a wide range of available models have made Chinese models attractive to Korean developers. Alibaba's Qwen offers models ranging from small versions to large-scale systems and supports 119 languages. Its extensive ecosystem of derivative models, tools and applications also gives developers greater flexibility in adapting the technology. The report found that Chinese models' output costs were about one-34th those of comparable top-tier models, although the cost advantage narrowed to about fourfold when measured across a full benchmark run. “The rapid adoption of Chinese open-weight models, including Qwen, reflects their growing use in lightweight experiments and day-to-day development work,” an industry official said. The growing use of Chinese models nevertheless raises concerns about technological dependence. Alibaba offers both AI models and cloud infrastructure, potentially making it harder for developers to move away from its ecosystem as Qwen adoption grows. “The biggest concern (in the rapid adoption) is not simply just information leaks, but the risk of technological dependence and supply-chain vulnerabilities,” the official said. Security is another concern. In the report's survey on 102 small and medium-sized companies, 80.2 percent cited potential data leaks as a concern about Chinese AI models, while 67.7 percent pointed to a lack of transparency in personal data handling. Industry officials cautioned that the opaque origins of training data in open-weight models could make it difficult for companies to meet strict requirements for AI safety, reliability and compliance. “Rather than deepening reliance on external models in pursuit of short-term cost efficiency, Korea needs a two-track strategy that builds its own secure and reliable foundation models to safeguard technological sovereignty,” the official said. “Building good models is important, but building a strong ecosystem together is even more important.”

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/opinion/edi.title: Kim's China visit must lead to restraint
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/opinion/edi.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong-un’s surprise visit to China is a reminder that the Korean Peninsula’s future cannot be understood through inter-Korean relations alone. For South Korea, the appropriate response is neither alarmism nor wishful thinking, but rather a clear-eyed assessment of what closer ties between China and North Korea could mean for regional security, sanctions enforcement and diplomacy. The visit carried both historical symbolism and practical economic significance.
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/opinion/edi.summary_zh: 朝鲜领导人金正恩突然访问中国，提醒人们仅凭韩朝关系无法理解朝鲜半岛的未来。对韩国而言，适当的回应既不是危言耸听，也不是一厢情愿，而是清醒评估中朝关系加深将如何影响地区安全、制裁执行和外交。此次访问兼具历史象征意义和实际经济意义。
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/opinion/edi.body: North Korean leader Kim Jong-un’s surprise visit to China is a reminder that the Korean Peninsula’s future cannot be understood through inter-Korean relations alone. Kim's crossing into Dandong via the newly opened New Amnok River Bridge and his meetings with senior Chinese official Wang Huning underscore the strategic importance Pyongyang attaches to Beijing. For South Korea, the appropriate response is neither alarmism nor wishful thinking, but rather a clear-eyed assessment of what closer ties between China and North Korea could mean for regional security, sanctions enforcement and diplomacy. The visit carried both historical symbolism and practical economic significance. Kim paid tribute to China’s participation in the Korean War and toured an automobile factory with Wang, who conveyed greetings from Chinese President Xi Jinping. The itinerary highlighted a relationship grounded in shared history but increasingly shaped by material interests. Notably, however, Kim did not meet Xi. The visit should therefore be judged on what it demonstrably achieved, not inflated into evidence of a diplomatic breakthrough that has yet to materialize. The new bridge merits particular scrutiny. Better transport links can facilitate legitimate trade, sustain livelihoods and ease North Korea’s isolation. Economic engagement is not inherently inimical to peace. Its implications, however, depend on what crosses the border and whether transactions are properly monitored. Beijing must ensure that deeper economic cooperation remains consistent with its international obligations and does not create new channels for prohibited transfers that could advance Pyongyang’s weapons programs. China cannot credibly champion regional stability while treating North Korea’s military provocations as a problem for others to manage. Its renewed access to Kim’s leadership presents an opportunity to discourage escalation, encourage communication and reinforce the costs of confrontation. Beijing need not sever ties with Pyongyang to exercise such influence. On the contrary, it should recognize that an increasingly volatile peninsula threatens the economic and strategic interests that closer bilateral relations are meant to serve. Kim, too, should recognize the limits of a foreign policy built around powerful patrons. Stronger relations with China and Russia may expand his diplomatic options and provide economic or strategic support, but they cannot deliver lasting security or broad-based prosperity on their own. A strategy that seeks external assistance while excluding South Korea from meaningful dialogue would only entrench the peninsula’s division. Sustainable economic development requires predictability, and predictability is impossible when the risk of military conflict remains high. Seoul must respond with equal resolve and strategic discipline. Robust deterrence and close coordination with Washington remain indispensable. But deterrence should create space for diplomacy, not become a substitute for it. South Korea should maintain active channels with Beijing, pursue practical cooperation on crisis prevention and assess closer China-North Korea ties by their actual consequences. A measurable reduction in military threats would be welcome. Any use of enhanced cooperation to embolden coercion would require a firm and coordinated response. Nor should Seoul define diplomatic progress solely by whether Kim meets U.S. President Donald Trump again. Speculation about another summit should not be mistaken for a confirmed diplomatic process. A hastily arranged encounter could produce striking images and short-lived optimism without yielding durable commitments. Any renewed negotiations must include close consultation with Seoul and focus on concrete, verifiable measures to reduce nuclear dangers and prevent miscalculation. The immediate priority should be to restore military communication, prevent incidents along the border and preserve avenues for humanitarian engagement. Such steps would not resolve the nuclear question, but they could address one of the peninsula’s most dangerous vulnerabilities: the absence of reliable mechanisms for managing confrontation. Seoul should advance these proposals without assuming that Pyongyang will accept them readily. An offer of dialogue is a strategic choice, not a guarantee of reciprocity. Kim’s journey across the Amnok River demonstrates that North Korea will open doors when its leadership sees an advantage. The challenge is to turn selective engagement into a broader contribution to regional security. Beijing should use its influence responsibly, Pyongyang should reconsider the costs of sustained hostility and Seoul should pair credible deterrence with sustained diplomatic initiative. A bridge can connect two banks; only prudent policy can make it a passage toward peace
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/opinion/edi.title_zh: 金正恩访华必须带来克制
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/opinion/edi.body_zh: 朝鲜领导人金正恩突然访问中国，再次表明，仅凭韩朝关系无法理解朝鲜半岛的未来。金正恩经新通车的鸭绿江大桥进入丹东，并会见中国高级官员王沪宁，凸显平壤赋予北京的重要战略意义。对韩国而言，适当的回应既不是危言耸听，也不是一厢情愿，而是清醒评估中朝关系走近可能给地区安全、制裁执行和外交带来何种影响。此次访问既具有历史象征意义，也具有实际经济意义。金正恩向中国参加朝鲜战争一事致敬，并与王沪宁一同参观汽车工厂；王沪宁转达了中国国家主席习近平的问候。访问日程凸显了两国关系建立在共同历史之上，但正日益受到现实利益影响。然而，金正恩此次并未与习近平会面。因此，应根据此次访问切实取得的成果来评价它，而不应将其夸大为迄今尚未实现的外交突破。新桥尤其值得审视。更便利的交通连接能够促进合法贸易、维持民生并缓解朝鲜的孤立。经济接触本身并不必然与和平相悖。然而，其影响取决于跨境流通的是什么，以及相关交易是否得到妥善监督。北京必须确保，更深入的经济合作符合其国际义务，不会为被禁止的转让行为开辟新渠道，从而推动平壤的武器计划。中国不能一面标榜维护地区稳定，一面把朝鲜的军事挑衅当成应由他人处理的问题。重新接触金正恩领导层，为中国创造了劝阻局势升级、鼓励沟通并强化对抗代价的机会。北京无须切断与平壤的关系，便能发挥这种影响。相反，中国应当认识到，日益动荡的朝鲜半岛会威胁更密切的双边关系本应服务的经济和战略利益。金正恩也应认识到，围绕强大靠山构建外交政策的局限。改善与中国和俄罗斯的关系或许能扩大他的外交选择，并提供经济或战略支持，但这些关系本身无法带来持久安全或广泛繁荣。寻求外部援助、却将韩国排除在实质性对话之外的战略，只会进一步固化半岛分裂。可持续经济发展需要可预测性，而军事冲突风险依然高企时，可预测性便无从谈起。首尔必须以同等决心和战略纪律作出回应。有效的威慑以及与华盛顿密切协调仍不可或缺。但威慑应当为外交创造空间，而不是取代外交。韩国应保持与北京的活跃沟通渠道，就危机预防开展务实合作，并根据中朝关系走近的实际后果加以评估。若军事威胁得到可量化减少，将是值得欢迎的成果。任何利用加强后的合作来助长胁迫的行为，都将需要坚决且协调一致的回应。首尔也不应仅以金正恩是否再次会见美国总统唐纳德·特朗普来界定外交进展。关于再次举行峰会的猜测，不应被误认为已确认的外交进程。仓促安排会晤可能制造醒目的画面和短暂的乐观情绪，却不会产生持久承诺。任何重启的谈判都必须包括与首尔的密切磋商，并聚焦于降低核危险和防止误判的具体、可核查措施。眼下的优先事项应是恢复军事沟通、防止边境发生意外事件，以及为人道主义接触保留渠道。这些举措无法解决核问题，但可以处理半岛上最危险的脆弱性之一：缺乏管理对抗局势的可靠机制。首尔应推动这些提议，同时不假定平壤会欣然接受。提出对话是一项战略选择，并不保证对方会予以回应。金正恩跨越鸭绿江的行程表明，当朝鲜领导层看到有利条件时，朝鲜愿意打开大门。挑战在于把有选择的接触转化为对地区安全的更广泛贡献。北京应负责任地运用影响力，平壤应重新审视持续敌对的代价，首尔则应把可信的威慑与持续的外交倡议结合起来。桥梁能够连接两岸；只有审慎的政策才能使其成为通往和平的通道

Hyundai Motor's sales plunged 47 percent on-year to around 4,000 units last month, while Kia's dropped 31 percent to 5,000, according to a Hana Securities report based on China Passenger Car Association (CPCA) data. Their combined sales fell 39 percent to approximately 9,000 units, with their market share slipping to just 0.6 percent from more than 10 percent in the mid-2010s. The automakers have struggled to revive sales despite introducing electric vehicles (EVs) tailored to the Chinese market. Hyundai's China-specific electric SUV Elexio sold just 251 units in the first nine months of this year, compared with 1,216 in the final three months of last year. https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/economy/202.body: The number of temporary and daily workers in Korea fell to its lowest third-quarter level in 31 years amid a prolonged construction slump, government data showed Sunday. The combined figure dropped by 95,000 from a year earlier to 5.73 million in the July-September period, the lowest third-quarter level since 1995, according to an analysis of microdata from the Ministry of Data and Statistics. Of the total, the number of daily workers fell by 38,000 to a record third-quarter low of 833,000, largely due to weak employment in the construction sector. Daily construction workers declined by 28,000 to 381,000, accounting for 74.6 percent of the overall drop. Those in their 50s saw the sharpest decline, down 21,000. The number of temporary workers, whose contracts last at least one month but less than a year, fell by 57,000 to 4.89 million in the three-month period. By industry, the accommodation and food services sector recorded the largest decline in temporary workers, down 30,000, followed by construction, and information and communications, which shed 22,000 each

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/southkorea/.summary_zh: 2000年，她随丈夫赴旧金山照顾其工作，后来开始参与韩国历史与文化教育。她联系孩子们就读的韩国学校，并于2007年开始为中学学生开设以讨论为主的历史课程，常常熬夜准备教学材料。“我毕生的使命是传承韩国独立运动的精神。
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/southkorea/.body: At the first Korea Book Festival in Vancouver, Canada, which runs through Oct. 31, a very meaningful book was exhibited: "Jessie’s Diary," reborn as a graphic novel. On Oct. 8, a session was held where readers read the original work and shared their impressions, receiving a great response. The graphic novel has been introduced in French, Chinese and Japanese, and preparations are underway to publish an English edition of the original work as well. "Jessie’s Diary" is a child-rearing journal kept for eight years, beginning in 1938 with the birth of the couple’s eldest daughter, Jessie, by Yang Woo-jo (1897-1964) and Choe Seon-hwa (1911-2003), a husband and wife who participated in the Korean Provisional Government. Alongside their deep love for their family, the diary chronicles the provisional government’s life in exile, the daily lives of independence activists and anecdotes about prominent figures in the independence movement, including Kim Gu and Ahn Chang-ho. It has been recognized for its historical value. The diary came to public attention in 1999 when Kim Hyun-ju, 54, the couple’s granddaughter and the daughter of Jessie Yang, the diary’s namesake, published it as a book. Kim currently lives in the United States and serves on the board of the Fremont Union High School District in California. In a recent telephone interview, she recalled her first encounter with the journal: “When I first saw the diary, written so carefully, one character at a time, it felt as though my maternal grandfather, whom I had never met, had come back to life.” Kim learned of the diary in 1998, when she was pregnant with her first child. Her maternal grandmother, Choe Seon-hwa, entrusted her with an old brown journal she had carefully preserved. The lives and convictions of her grandparents, preserved in its pages, deeply moved her. Having worked as a broadcast writer, Kim modernized archaic expressions and Chinese-derived words and added vivid recollections she had heard directly from her grandmother before compiling the material into a book. The publication celebration was especially meaningful, bringing together four generations of women: Choe, Jessie Yang, Kim and Kim’s first daughter, who was about 100 days old at the time. The diary also changed the course of Kim’s life. After moving to San Francisco in 2000 to accompany her husband for his job, she became involved in Korean history and cultural education. At the time, even finding books about Korea in American libraries was difficult. She approached the Korean school her children attended and began teaching discussion-based history classes for middle school students in 2007, staying up through the night to prepare teaching materials. She eventually became a vice principal and then a principal. Another experience also sparked her interest in history education. She discovered that "So Far from the Bamboo Grove," a book centered on a Japanese girl near the end of World War II that portrays Japanese people as victims and Koreans as aggressors, was being used as instructional material in some California schools. “I was deeply shocked when I heard that a Korean American student who had read the book felt ashamed of being Korean,” Kim said. Working with fellow Korean school teachers and other members of the Korean American community, Kim urged education authorities to remove "So Far from the Bamboo Grove" from the list of instructional materials. In 2008, at the publisher’s request, the school district board finally voted to remove the book. “I sobbed in the bathroom all by myself because I thought of my grandparents. I felt that this was why I had come to America.” Since 2009, Kim has organized seminars on Korean history and culture for American teachers. Around 2012, she and Korean school teachers established the educational organization Echo Korea. She also runs the Young Korean American Academy, a summer camp for young people. “I want to help Korean American students take pride in their roots while growing into members of American society,” she said. Kim was first elected to the school district board in 2018 and won reelection in 2022. She is seeking a third term in the election on Nov. 3. Her dream is to one day meet her maternal grandparents and mother in heaven and proudly tell them about the path she has taken. “My life’s mission is to carry on the spirit of the Korean independence movement. I will continue moving forward, using my grandparents’ lives as my compass.” This article from the Hankook Ilbo, the sister publication of The Korea Times, is translated by a generative AI system and edited by The Korea Times
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/southkorea/.title_zh: 韩国独立运动人士的孙女将韩国历史带入美国学校
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/southkorea/.body_zh: 在加拿大温哥华举行的首届韩国书展将持续至10月31日，展出了一本意义非凡的书：以图像小说形式重新问世的《Jessie的日记》。10月8日，活动现场举办了一场读书会，读者朗读原作并分享感想反响热烈。这本图像小说已推出法语、中文和日语版本，英文版原作也正在筹备出版。《Jessie的日记》是一本育儿日记，记录了8年的家庭生活，从1938年夫妇二人的长女Jessie出生写起。这对夫妇是杨宇柱（1897-1964）和崔孙花（1911-2003），他们曾参加韩国临时政府。除了对家人的深厚感情，日记还记录了临时政府流亡期间的生活、独立活动人士的日常生活，以及金九、安昌浩等独立运动杰出人物的故事，其历史价值已获认可。1999年，这本日记为公众所知，当时夫妇二人的外孙女、日记主人公Jessie Yang之女、54岁的金贤珠将其出版成书。金目前居住在美国，担任加利福尼亚州弗里蒙特联合高中学区董事会成员。最近接受电话采访时，她回忆第一次看到这本日记的情景：“当我第一次看到这本日记时，里面的一字一句都写得那么工整细致，我仿佛觉得从未见过的外祖父又回到了人间。”金是在1998年怀第一个孩子时得知这本日记的。外祖母崔孙花将一本珍藏多年的旧棕色日记交给她。祖辈的人生与信念在日记篇章中得以保存，深深打动了她。金曾从事广播撰稿工作，并为编纂成书 modernize了陈旧表达和源自汉语的词语，还补入了从外祖母本人那里听来的生动回忆。出版庆祝活动尤其意义非凡，因为它让一家四代女性相聚在一起：崔孙花、Jessie Yang、金贤珠，以及当时年仅约100天大的金的第一个女儿。这本日记也改变了金的人生轨迹。2000年，她随丈夫赴旧金山照顾其工作，随后开始参与韩国历史与文化教育。当时，即便是在美国的图书馆里也很难找到有关韩国的书籍。她找到孩子们就读的韩国学校，自2007年起为初中生开设以讨论为主的历史课程，并熬夜准备教学资料。她后来先后担任副校长和校长。另一次经历也激起了她对历史教育的兴趣。她发现，一部以第二次世界大战末期一名日本女孩为中心、把日本人描绘为受害者而把韩国人描绘为侵略者的作品《远方的竹丛》竟被一些加利福尼亚州学校用作教材。“听说一名读过这本书的韩裔美国学生为自己是韩国人感到羞耻时，我深受震撼。”金说。她与韩国学校的其他教师及韩裔美国社群成员共同敦促教育主管部门将《远方的竹丛》从教学材料清单中删除。2008年，应出版方要求，学区董事会终于表决决定移除该书。“我想起祖父母，独自在浴室里放声大哭。我觉得，这正是我来美国的意义。”自2009年起，金一直为美国教师组织韩国历史与文化研讨会。约在2012年，她与韩国学校教师共同成立了教育组织Echo Korea。她还运营青年韩裔美国学院，这是一个面向青少年的夏令营。她说：“我希望帮助韩裔美国学生为自己的根源感到自豪，同时成长为美国社会的一员。”金于2018年首次当选学区董事会成员，并在2022年成功连任。她正在争取11月3日选举中的第三个任期。她的梦想是有一天能在天堂与外祖父母和母亲相见，并自豪地告诉他们自己走过的人生道路。“我的人生使命是延续韩国独立运动的精神。我会以祖辈的人生为指南针，继续向前。”本文来自《韩国时报》的姊妹报《韩国先驱报》，由生成式人工智能系统翻译，并经《韩国时报》编辑。

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.title: Uzbekistan marks independence day in Seoul, citing $8 bil. in Korean investment
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.summary: Uzbekistan's Ambassador to Korea Alisher Abdusalomov emphasized the importance of further expanding bilateral trade and industrial cooperation between Uzbekistan and Korea at a reception marking the country’s 35th Independence Day and the 34th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries.
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.summary_zh: 乌兹别克斯坦驻韩国大使Alisher Abdusalomov在庆祝该国独立35周年及乌韩两国外交关系建立34周年的招待会上强调，进一步扩大乌兹别克斯坦与韩国之间的双边贸易和工业合作十分重要。
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.body: Uzbekistan's Ambassador to Korea Alisher Abdusalomov emphasized the importance of further expanding bilateral trade and industrial cooperation between Uzbekistan and Korea at a reception marking the country’s 35th Independence Day and the 34th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries. "President Shavkat Mirziyoyev's state visit to the Republic of Korea in September this year marked an important milestone in the development of the Special Strategic Partnership between our two countries," Abdusalomov said Wednesday. He also stressed how the inaugural Korea-Central Asia Summit outlined a long-term vision for cooperation across various fields. Highlighting that Korean investment in Uzbekistan has surpassed approximately 11 trillion won ($8 billion), with more than 700 Korean companies operating in the country, the ambassador expressed hope for Korean companies' active participation in the New Tashkent project. The ambassador also stressed the importance of people-to-people ties, noting that around 107,000 Uzbekistan nationals currently reside in Korea, including some 22,000 students, are not just future skilled professionals, but are bridges between the two countries. The reception also featured an award ceremony for winners of the Why I Love Uzbekistan contest. Chung Eui-hae, deputy minister for political affairs at Korea's foreign ministry, also described this year as a turning point in bilateral relations, citing the two major diplomatic events held in September. "Since the establishment of diplomatic relations in 1992, the Republic of Korea and Uzbekistan have grown together as trusted friends and special strategic partners, building on mutual trust," Chung said. Looking ahead to next year's 35th anniversary of Seoul-Tashkent diplomatic relations and the 90th anniversary of ethnic Koreans' settlement in Central Asia, she emphasized the possibility of the two countries creating new growth opportunities by combining Korea's advanced technology with Uzbekistan's rich potential and dynamism
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.title_zh: 乌兹别克斯坦在首尔庆祝独立日，称韩国在乌投资达80亿美元
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.body_zh: 乌兹别克斯坦驻韩国大使阿里希尔·阿卜杜萨洛莫夫在一场纪念该国独立35周年及乌韩建交34周年的招待会上强调，进一步扩大乌兹别克斯坦与韩国之间的双边贸易和工业合作十分重要。阿卜杜萨洛莫夫周三表示：“沙夫卡特·米尔济约耶夫总统今年9月对大韩民国的国事访问，标志着我们两国特殊战略伙伴关系发展过程中的一个重要里程碑。”他还强调，首次举行的韩国—中亚峰会勾勒了双方在各领域合作的长期愿景。大使指出，韩国对乌兹别克斯坦的投资已超过约11万亿韩元（80亿美元），目前有700多家韩国企业在该国经营，并希望韩国企业积极参与“新塔什肯特”项目。大使还强调民间联系的重要性，并指出，目前约有107,000名乌兹别克斯坦国民居住在韩国，其中约22,000人是学生；他们不仅是未来的技术人才，也是两国之间的桥梁。招待会还举行了“我爱乌兹别克斯坦”竞赛获奖者颁奖仪式。韩国外交部政治事务副部长郑义海也将今年称为双边关系的转折点，并提及9月举行的两场重大外交活动。郑义海说：“自1992年建立外交关系以来，大韩民国与乌兹别克斯坦在相互信任的基础上携手成长，成为可信的朋友和特殊战略伙伴。”展望明年首尔—塔什肯特建交35周年以及朝鲜民族迁居中亚90周年，她强调，两国可以将韩国的先进技术与乌兹别克斯坦丰富的潜力和活力结合起来，创造新的增长机遇

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.body_zh: 宾客在首尔南部良才溪畔举行的“瓦茨拉夫·哈维尔长椅聚会”活动上合影。10月20日，韩国捷克大使馆与首尔瑞草区公署联合主办该活动，纪念前捷克总统瓦茨拉夫·哈维尔（1936—2011）诞辰90周年。长椅于2025年5月设立，捷克驻韩大使Ivan Jančárek（右起第三）强调，哈维尔为自由与民主留下的持久遗产；捷克中心首尔主管Michal Emanovský（左起第五）则强调，这张长椅是促进对话与相互理解的场所。瑞草区区长Jun Sung-soo（左起第四）指出，韩国自身也有维护民主的历史，两国共享的价值观将成为深化双边关系的坚实基础。图片来源：瑞草区公署
