https://www.thehindu.com/entertainment/m.summary_zh: 但今年一直让像我这样的人几乎每天都抱着期待、如同“注射快乐剂”般等待的压轴之作，是Studio Trigger备受期待的作品，即曾获“年度动画”的《赛博朋克：边缘行者》的续作。《赛博朋克：边缘行者2》的故事设定在第一季结束3年后、电子游戏事件发生1年后，故事重返夜之城，并采用一组全新角色，他们个个都像会走路的债务人。
https://www.thehindu.com/entertainment/m.body: Account subscription benefits alongside Premium Stories, Editorials, Opinions and more. Unlock these with Subscription Good morning, Night City! Four years since David Martinez and his chromed-out cohort gave Arasaka a run for its eddies, we’re back on the streets, where the body count remains awful and the cost of existing worse! Cyberpunk 2077 has undergone a miraculous rehabilitation, courtesy of enough patch updates and a sprawling Phantom Liberty expansion to make its launch-day catastrophe one of gaming’s great redemption stories! Meanwhile, Ghost in the Shell has returned through Science SARU, Prime Video’s Blade Runner 2099 is touching down next month, and William Gibson’s Neuromancer is finally getting its Apple TV moment in January. The future (daresay the present), ladies and gentlemen, is looking absolutely dystopian, and the entertainment industry has never been more bleak! For the handful of cyberpunk devotees who were impressed by my thoroughly shoddy impression of Cyberpunk 2077 ’s iconic radio jockey intro, and the considerably larger contingent of uninitiated readers wondering whether I’ve suffered a stroke; the genre has been having something of a moment lately, thanks in no small part to the real world making steady attempts to outdo it. But the crown jewel that has had people like me practically mainlining copium in anticipation all year is Studio Trigger’s long-awaited follow-up to its Anime of the Year-winning Cyberpunk: Edgerunners . Born in Mike Pondsmith’s tabletop RPG, immortalised in CD Projekt Red’s sprawling videogame, and subsequently given a spectacularly violent animated makeover by Studio Trigger, Night City has become one of sci-fi’s most recognisable monuments to humanity’s capacity for self-sabotage. It is a dystopian, hypercapitalist hellscape where corporations like Arasaka wield more power than governments and the human body is just another depreciating asset awaiting its next absurd upgrade. The first season followed a gang of rebellious mercenaries AKA ‘Edgerunners’ as they took increasingly suicidal gigs and eventually found themselves on a collision course with Arasaka that could only end in tragedy. After all, there are no happy endings in Night City … or so we were led to believe. Set three years after the first season and a year after the events of the videogame, Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 returns to Night City with an entirely new cast of walking liabilities. Roman Carax is a 12-year-old aspiring filmmaker who prefers his analogue camera to the brain-rotting convenience of Braindances; D is a vengeful netrunner whose Nomad clan was massacred; Talia is a young woman replacing her failing body with disturbing amounts of chrome; and Weak Kingsley, once the celebrated edgerunner King, is attempting to rebuild his life after surviving cyberpsychosis at the cost of the augmentations that made him formidable. Despite the subtitle, Edgerunners 2 couldn’t care less about edgerunning, abandoning its predecessor’s fixer-economy ladder-climbing and doomed pursuit of mercenary immortality for a more incisive autopsy of the psychological inducements and hideously personal costs of chroming. This sequel throws together four protagonists who share neither a crew nor a coherent set of interests, through a bunch of narrative happenstance. Weak Kingsley’s introduction establishes just how close he is to cyberpsychosis, forcing him to chrome down to prevent another episode. The prospect of becoming an obsolete relic without the hardware that furnished his reputation proves so intolerable that he attempts suicide, until a former flame Avida, interrupts his exit strategy by asking for his help. His ensuing arc keeps circling the question that David’s story could never quite afford to entertain: who the hell are you when the chrome comes off? Losing his augmentations does mean losing the very thing that made him somebody, but it eventually gives him the freedom to find his own meaning in life, untethered from the legend he once was. Talia’s predicament is the inverse of Weak’s — while he has to figure out who he is without his chrome, she is unable to imagine herself without hers. She begins augmenting herself to treat her condition, but as more of her flesh gives way to machinery, the distinction between medical necessity and personal compulsion grows murkier by the episode. Chroming becomes her means of coping with trauma, a way of feeling powerful enough to finally be fully herself, even as that pursuit takes a brutal toll on the very body she is trying to reclaim. The season probes this vicious oscillation between chrome as an act of self-preservation and body dysmorphia as a licence for extraordinary acts of self-directed contempt. One of the season’s highlights is the internet’s ‘Cyber Sasuke’ D, a brooding teenage netrunner with unresolved trauma and a blood oath against the people who massacred his Nomad clan. He begins the season chasing vengeance and answers, with enough anguished emo energy to slot comfortably alongside Sasuke Uchiha, Megumi Fushiguro, Shoto Todoroki and Zuko in the prestigious lineage of fictional boys who desperately need somebody to talk to. But D’s story gradually outgrows its revenge complex, becoming an interrogation of what freedom actually means in a city that dictates even the terms of your rebellion. D’s serendipitous encounter with Capri, an experimental digital construct that manifests inside his head, gives the season its most unexpectedly compelling relationship to excavate. Where Cyberpunk 2077 saddled players with Keanu Reeves’ sardonic Johnny Silverhand, a digital squatter who spent much of his tenancy encouraging you to blow up Arasaka; Edgerunners 2 gives us a sprightly, pixelated anime girl whose frolicsome disposition and appetite for chaos make her considerably more fun to have around. The human-machine relationship is one of the season’s more intriguing preoccupations, with Capri offering D the feeling of being understood and seen. There are shades of Samantha in Her and Joi in Blade Runner 2049 in this intimate companionship, along with a rather timely question about the parasocial attachments we are already forming with artificial life. And yet, for all the existential queasiness of watching a traumatised teenager find solace in a being whose inner life remains tantalisingly unknowable, their chemistry is disarmingly tender — I couldn’t help but root for them? I’m still working out whether that makes me naively sentimental or just profoundly stupid; perhaps both. But the beating heart of Edgerunners 2 is unquestionably Roman. The precocious 12-year-old cinephile is a conduit through whom the series articulates some of its most incisive observations on art in the age of AI, with an early piece of writing distilling his entire artistic philosophy very eloquently: “In Braindance, nothing separates the audience from the action. It’s just one layer deep. But film has a screen. It acts like a boundary. One you’re supposed to cross, so you forget it was ever there. Stories transport us. That’s why they matter. That’s why we still need them” Roman Carax Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 Between tailing D to capture Nightcrawler -style LiveLeak carnage, splicing narco-executions into grisly montages, and taking an earnest interest in preserving the spark in his friends’ eyes at their happiest, Roman is a fascinating character study in what the lens does to the person behind it. It’s a question Lance Oppenheim’s Primetime has already probed, and Nathan Fielder’s much-anticipated You Can See Everything will soon revisit, but in Night City, where the line between snuff, Mondo, exploitation and documentary is practically non-existent, Roman remains stubbornly committed to making art for art’s sake. There’s also a lovely streak of analogue-media evangelism running through the season, from Roman’s excitement at the prospect of shooting on 35mm to the early-2000s DVD-era nostalgia baked into its visual grammar, right down to that bouncing DVD screensaver outro. I also refuse to believe the fact that Night City’s three great corpo nightmares — David Martinez (2075), V (2077) and David (2078) — spelling out DVD, isn’t a mere coincidental spit in the face of the streaming economy. Across its ten episodes, I’ve lost count of how many times Studio Trigger left me gawping at the screen, with images I wouldn’t know how to conjure in my most feverishly elaborate dreams. The fluidity, ferocity, obsessive detail and deranged editing are among the finest I’ve witnessed all year, and given the competition 2026 has thrown up, that is no small achievement. But it’s Kai Ikarashi’s direction and shot composition that elevate the spectacle beyond an exercise in technical one-upmanship. Having already established himself with the extraordinary sixth episode of season one, “Girl on Fire”, Ikarashi pushes Trigger’s rendering of Night City to dizzying new heights, marrying ultra-stylised character designs and outrageously kinetic action with the grainy, paranoia-soaked found-footage frames of Roman’s camera. The key frames, production design, background art and sheer audacity of the visual language work in concert to make Edgerunners 2 one of the year’s most astonishingly realised animated productions. Of course, what makes all that visual lacquer unmistakably Cyberpunk is the exquisite misery it’s been applied to conceal, because Night City has never met a gorgeous frame it couldn’t use to make somebody’s suffering look spectacular. D’s slow capitulation to his own fate carries shades of Eren Jaeger’s terminal fatalism , while Roman and Talia’s budding relationship has that Your Lie in April flavour of impending heartbreak. The unfairness of it all made me inconsolable. These are just a bunch of kids trying to decipher their place in a world, but the crippling nihilism of Night City moulds, radicalises, exploits and, all too often, turns them into weapons. And so, if you told me Edgerunners 2 was essentially a brilliantly disguised bildungsroman about a boy learning to love the act of creation in a world drowning in mass-produced cultural landfill; and how that love for the messiness of human experience might yet save something worth saving, I would burst into tears all over again. I think a lot of people miss what this story is getting at, and more broadly, what cyberpunk has always been about beyond the fetishistically rendered hypercapitalism. This is, in many ways, an unbecoming of cyberpunk, and a rejection of the genre’s self-destructive fixations in favour of the almost radical act of choosing to live. If season one was about dying for the people you love, season two is about learning to live for them. The most powerful argument Edgerunners 2 makes is that even in a civilisation drowning in technofascism and algorithmically dispensed slop, the love of art and the need for human connection remain stubbornly irreducible. Its aggressively hopecore sensibilities crystallise in that cheeky final shot, when a piece of airborne rubbish smacks Roman in the face and he simply grins — Night City may do its best to suck the very soul out of you but it cannot quite extinguish the impulse to create, to feel, to find something worth preserving, and to simply, love. The indomitable human spirit is a phrase that has been flogged to death by considerably less deserving stories, but here it earns its keep. It sounds borderline cyberpsychotic to say a series set in Night City restored my faith in humanity. That Edgerunners 2 can wring such tenderness, such an unembarrassed belief in art and human connection, from a world so thoroughly committed to grinding both into dust is precisely what makes it one of the finest things television has given us this year. https://www.thehindu.com/entertainment/m.title_zh: 《赛博朋克：边缘行者2》系列评测：技术法西斯主义时代的爱情与艺术
https://www.thehindu.com/entertainment/m.body_zh: 订阅可解锁高级报道、评论、观点等更多内容。订阅后即可畅读。早上好，夜之城！距离David Martinez和他的镀铬伙伴向Arasaka大展拳脚已过去4年，我们重返街头，这里的死亡人数依旧触目惊心，而生存成本更是糟糕透顶！得益于足够多的补丁更新和内容庞大的《Phantom Liberty》扩展包，《Cyberpunk 2077》经历了奇迹般的重生，把发售日的灾难变成了游戏史上最伟大的救赎故事之一。与此同时，《Ghost in the Shell》通过Science SARU强势回归，Prime Video的《Blade Runner 2099》将于下月登场，William Gibson的《Neuromancer》也终于要在1月迎来Apple TV时刻。女士们、先生们，未来（姑且也可以说是现在）简直赛博朋克到底了，娱乐行业也从未如此令人绝望！少数赛博朋克爱好者或许还记得我那极其拙劣的《Cyberpunk 2077》标志性电台主持人开场白让他们印象深刻；更多的是尚未接触这一类型的读者，可能正怀疑我是不是中风了。近来，这一类型可谓正当风光，而现实世界不断企图超越它，同样大有功劳。但今年最令人期待、让我几乎全年都在畅想“兴奋剂”的压轴之作，是Studio Trigger久违的续集——《Cyberpunk: Edgerunners》。第一季曾获“年度动画”大奖。夜之城诞生于Mike Pondsmith的桌上角色扮演游戏，经CD Projekt Red打造的大型电子游戏而名垂千古，随后又被Studio Trigger改编成一部暴力 spectacular 的动画，成为科幻领域最容易被辨认的人类自我毁灭能力象征之一。这里是一片反乌托邦式的极端资本主义炼狱，Arasaka等企业拥有的权力甚至超过政府，而人的身体不过是另一件等待下一次荒谬升级的贬值资产。第一季讲述了一群被称为“Edgerunners”的反叛佣兵，他们接下越来越自杀式的任务，最终发现自己与Arasaka迎头相撞，结局只能是悲剧。毕竟，夜之城没有圆满结局……至少过去一直是这么告诉我们的。《Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2》的故事设定在第一季3年后、电子游戏事件1年后，全新的角色阵容回到了夜之城。Roman Carax是一名12岁的有志电影人，相较于令人脑腐的Braindances便利，他更钟爱自己的模拟胶片相机；D是一名满心复仇的潜行者，他的Nomad部族惨遭屠杀；Talia是一名年轻女子，正用令人不安的大量铬金属替换日渐衰竭的身体；Weak Kingsley则是一度备受推崇的传奇跑者King，在从cyberpsychosis中生还后，他失去了曾让自己令人闻风丧胆的增强组件，如今试图重建人生。尽管副标题仍叫“Edgerunners 2”，续集却根本不在乎什么跑者行动，抛开了前作那套摆渡人经济、向上攀爬和追求佣兵永生的 doomed 设定，转而更尖锐地剖析铬金属化背后的心理诱因，以及由此带来的骇人个人代价。续集通过一连串叙事偶然，将4名既不属于同一团伙、也没有共同连贯利益的主角凑到了一起。Weak Kingsley的出场揭示了他距离cyberpsychosis究竟有多近，迫使他再次进行铬金属化，以防旧疾复发。失去赖以成名的硬件，意味着他将成为过时的残骸，而这一前景令他难以忍受，于是他试图自杀，直到旧日恋人Avida请求他帮忙，打断了他的计划。此后他的故事始终围绕着一个David的故事因篇幅所限始终无法正视的问题打转：当你身上的铬金属被移除后，你到底是谁？失去增强组件确实也意味着失去让自己成为其人的一切，但最终也让他摆脱了昔日传奇的束缚，在生活中找到属于自己的意义。Talia的处境则与Weak恰好相反——他必须弄清没有铬金属的自己是谁，她却无法想象没有铬金属的自己。她开始对身体进行增强，以治疗自身状况，但随着更多血肉让位于机械，医疗必要与个人强迫之间的界线也逐集变得模糊。铬金属化成了她应对创伤的手段，让她感到自己足够强大，终于能够成为完整的自己，即便这一追求正残酷地损耗着她试图夺回的身体。本季深入探究了这种恶性摆动：铬金属化既是自我保存的行为，也成为身体焦虑障碍为极端自我轻蔑行为提供借口。本季亮点之一是互联网所谓的“Cyber Sasuke”——D。他是一名阴郁的少年潜行者，创伤尚未愈合，并对屠灭自己Nomad部族的人立下血誓。季初，他一心追索复仇，以足以媲美Sasuke Uchiha、Megumi Fushiguro、Shoto Todoroki和Zuko的纠结中二能量，跻身那些迫切需要找人倾诉的虚构男孩的显赫谱系。但D的故事逐渐不再局限于复仇执念，转而拷问自由在一座连反抗方式都由你规定的城市里究竟意味着什么。D与Capri的偶遇构成本季最出人意料、最引人深入挖掘的一段关系。Capri是一个实验性的数字构造体，能够显化在D的脑海中。《Cyberpunk 2077》给玩家安排了Keanu Reeves饰演的冷嘲热讽的Johnny Silverhand，一个在大部分“租期”里都怂恿玩家炸掉Arasaka的数字寄居者；《Edgerunners 2》则带来一个活泼、像素化的动漫女孩，她嬉皮笑脸的性情和制造混乱的欲望，让她成为更有趣的陪伴。人与机器的关系是本季颇引人入胜的主题之一，Capri让D感受到被理解、被看见。这种亲密陪伴中既有《Her》里Samantha的影子，也有《Blade Runner 2049》里Joi的影子，同时还提出了一个格外应时的问题：我们已经在与人工生命形成何种准社会性依恋？然而，眼看一个受创的少年从其内在生命依旧诱人地不可知的存在中寻得慰藉，尽管存在主义式的反胃感挥之不去，两者的化学反应却感人得 disarmingly 温柔——我忍不住希望他们好起来？我仍在琢磨，这究竟说明我天真多情，还是愚蠢透顶；或许两者兼有。不过，《Edgerunners 2》无可争议的核心 unquestionably 是Roman。这个早熟的12岁影迷成为剧中表达其最敏锐艺术观的 conduits：系列借他的一段早期文字，极其流畅地浓缩了他的整个艺术哲学：“在Braindance中，观众与行动之间没有任何隔阂。它只有一层。但电影有银幕。银幕就像一道边界。你本应跨越它，从而忘记它曾经存在。故事带我们抵达别处。这就是故事之所以重要，也是我们至今仍需要故事的原因。”——Roman Carax，《Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2》Roman一面尾随D，拍下Nightcrawler风格的LiveLeak式血腥画面，一面将毒 executions 剪进阴森蒙太奇，同时真挚地关注朋友们最快乐时眼中保有的光芒。他是一个关于镜头如何塑造镜头背后之人的迷人角色研究。这个问题Lance Oppenheim的《Primetime》早已探讨，Nathan Fielder备受期待的《You Can See Everything》也很快会重新审视。但在夜之城， snuff、Mondo、剥削与纪录片之间的界线几乎不存在，Roman仍固执地坚持为艺术而艺术。本季还有一条可爱的模拟媒体布道线：从Roman对使用35mm拍摄兴奋不已，到视觉语法中浸透的21世纪初DVD时代怀旧，直至最后那个弹跳的DVD屏幕保护程序式片尾。我拒绝相信，夜之城的3大企业噩梦——David Martinez（2075年）、V（2077年）和David（2078年）——恰好拼出“DVD”，只是对流媒体经济的偶然吐口水。全剧10集，我已数不清Studio Trigger多少次让我目瞪口呆，那些画面即使在我最狂热的梦境中也不知该如何想象。其流畅性、凶猛感、执迷般的细节和疯狂剪辑，是我今年见过的最佳水准之一；考虑到2026年涌现的竞争作品，这绝非小小的成就。但真正让奇观超越技术炫技的，是Kai Ikarashi的导演手法和镜头构图。第一季第6集“Girls on Fire”已让他凭借卓越表现确立地位，本集又把Trigger对夜之城的呈现推向令人眩晕的新高度，将极度风格化的角色设计、极富动感的动作场面与Roman镜头中颗粒感十足、浸透偏执的伪纪录片画面融为一体。关键帧、制作设计、背景美术以及视觉语言中十足的大胆，共同成就了《Edgerunners 2》，使其成为今年最令人惊叹的动画制作之一。当然，让所有这些视觉外壳 unmistakably 赛博朋克的，正是它被用来遮盖的精致苦难，因为夜之城从未见过一个不能用来让某个人苦难显得 spectacular 的华丽画面。D缓慢向自己的命运屈服，带有Eren Jaeger终局宿命论的味道；Roman与Talia初萌的关系，则有《Your Lie in April》那种即将迎来心碎的气息。整部作品的不公让我悲痛欲绝。这些不过是一群试图在这个世界中找到自身位置的年轻人，但夜之城的致命虚无主义会塑造他们、激进化他们、剥削他们，而且往往还会把他们变成武器。因此，如果你告诉我，《Edgerunners 2》本质上是一部精心伪装的成长小说，讲述一个男孩在批量生产的文化垃圾中学习热爱创作，而对人类经验之混乱的热爱或许仍能拯救某些值得拯救之物，我一定又会泪流满面。我认为很多人错过了这个故事想说出的东西，更广义地说，也错过了赛博朋克除了迷恋式呈现的极端资本主义之外始终关注的本质。从许多方面看，这是一次对赛博朋克的反叛，也是对该类型自我毁灭执念的拒绝，转而选择一项近乎激进的行动：活下去。如果第一季讲的是为你所爱之人赴死，第二季讲的则是学会为他们而活。《Edgerunners 2》最有力量的论点是：即便身处的文明沉没于技术法西斯主义和算法批量炮制的劣质内容，对艺术的热爱以及与人建立联系的需要，依然顽固地不可化约。它咄咄逼人的希望核心，在最后一个镜头中凝结成形：一件飞在半空的垃圾砸中Roman的脸，他只是咧嘴一笑——夜之城或许会竭尽全力吸干你的灵魂，却无法彻底扑灭创造的冲动、感受的冲动、寻找值得守护之物的冲动，以及单纯去爱的冲动。“不屈的人类精神”这句话已经被远不值得如此的故事滥用至死，但在这里，它终于配得上这句评价。说一部以夜之城为背景的剧重新让我相信人类，听起来几乎有些cyberpsychotic。而《Edgerunners 2》竟能从这样一个彻底致力于把艺术与人际联结碾成齑粉的世界中，榨取出如此温柔、如此毫不羞赧地相信艺术与人际联结的信念，这正是它成为今年电视带给我们的最佳作品之一的原因。评论必须使用英语，并以完整句子表述。不得包含辱骂性或针对个人的内容。发布评论时请遵守我们的社区准则。

Unlock these with Subscription I remember Fitbit as a slim tracking device worn on the wrist , from a time when fitness bands were about counting steps and monitoring activity, long before the smartwatch craze took over. Over the years, wearables have evolved into mini smartphones, complete with displays, notifications and apps. With the Fitbit Air, Google brings back some of that original simplicity in a new avatar. Priced at ₹13,999 in India, this screenless tracker focuses on health monitoring, sleep insights and activity tracking, with Google Health and Gemini-powered coaching adding a layer of intelligence. It is designed to stay out of the way while keeping tabs on your health throughout the day. After spending time with it, the question is whether this return to the basics works for today’s fitness-focused users. Let’s find out. The Fitbit Air takes a different approach to wearable design by keeping the hardware compact and unobtrusive. The tracking module weighs just 5.2 grams, while the device weighs around 12 grams with its band. It has a small, pebble-shaped sensor housed inside a woven fabric strap, giving it the appearance of a simple wristband rather than a conventional smartwatch. There is no display or physical button, which keeps the design clean and minimal. Comfort is one of the Fitbit Air’s biggest strengths. Its lightweight construction makes it comfortable to wear throughout the day and while sleeping. The woven band sits gently on the wrist, while its adjustable fastening helps achieve a secure fit for continuous tracking. This matters for a device designed to collect health data around the clock, rather than something you wear only during workouts. The tracker also has a detachable sensor module, allowing you to change bands without replacing the device. The Fitbit Air has a small status LED that responds to a firm double-tap. A white light indicates sufficient battery, while red signals that the charge is low. It also includes a vibration motor for silent alarms and reminders. The tracker offers water resistance up to 50 metres, making it suitable for swimming, although the fabric band needs proper drying after water exposure. Google offers the tracker in Obsidian, Berry, Lavender and Fog, with interchangeable band options. The Fitbit Air relies on the Google Health app for almost everything beyond collecting data. Once paired with a smartphone, it tracks activity and health metrics in the background and syncs them to the app. The dashboard brings together steps, sleep, heart rate, readiness and cardio load, making it possible to review daily activity without needing a screen on the wrist. The app offers plenty of information, although understanding some of the metrics takes time. Its separate sections for Today, Fitness, Sleep and Health make it easier to explore individual readings. You can also connect supported health services and devices. Another useful feature is the ability to keep the Fitbit Air and a Pixel Watch connected to the same account. This works well if you prefer a smartwatch during the day but want a lighter tracker for sleeping. Google Health Coach, powered by Gemini, is one of the more interesting additions. Available through a Google Health Premium subscription, it interprets health data, suggests workouts, explains recovery scores and helps create personalised fitness plans. Instead of simply presenting numbers, it aims to explain what they mean and how you can act on them. However, some recommendations can feel generic, and the feature needs refinement before its guidance consistently feels personal. It should also be treated as a wellness tool, and not a substitute for medical advice. Google includes a three-month Premium trial with the Fitbit Air. After that, the subscription costs ₹499 per month or ₹4,999 annually. Basic activity tracking, sleep information and several recovery metrics remain available without a subscription, which means you can continue using the core features without an ongoing payment. The Fitbit Air’s screenless design makes the experience genuinely distraction-free. You do not have notifications appearing on your wrist or a display encouraging you to check it repeatedly. The tracker collects information quietly, leaving the phone app to handle the analysis. This approach works particularly well for people who want to monitor their health without adding another source of digital interruptions. Sleep tracking is one of the more detailed parts of the experience. The Fitbit Air automatically detects sleep and daytime naps, so you do not have to start a session manually. During testing, it recorded sleep duration and estimated the time spent in deep, REM and light sleep. It also highlighted periods of restlessness and time spent awake. The presentation makes it easy to see how the night unfolded, although sleep stages remain estimates rather than clinical measurements. The app also records resting heart rate, heart-rate variability and readiness scores. These readings can help you follow patterns over time, especially as the tracker builds a baseline from your personal data. During the initial testing period, some recovery metrics did not yet have an established range. This meant the insights were less useful at first, but they became easier to interpret in the context of ongoing tracking. Heart-rate data is presented through graphs that show how readings change during an activity. This makes it easier to understand workout intensity and review a session afterwards. However, automatic workout recognition was less consistent. On some occasions, the app detected movement but labelled it as a possible activity and asked for confirmation. The ability to edit the recorded session helps, but more accurate automatic identification would make the experience smoother. Overall, the Fitbit Air offers a detailed view of activity, sleep and recovery in a compact device. Its tracking information is easy to access, and the app gives you several ways to understand your daily patterns. The main limitation is that some insights need more historical data, while automatic workout recognition and AI coaching still have room to improve. Battery life is another advantage of the Fitbit Air’s screenless design. Google claims up to seven days of use on a single charge, depending on settings and usage. During testing, the tracker lasted around seven days on a full charge, matching the company’s claim. This reduces the need to interrupt daily wear for charging, and makes continuous health monitoring more convenient. The Fitbit Air supports fast charging, with Google claiming that a five-minute charge provides up to a day of use. A full charge takes around 90 minutes. The included charging cable connects to the sensor module through pogo pins, so you need to remove the tracker from your wrist while charging. You can check the exact battery percentage in the Google Health app, while a double-tap on the tracker provides a quick LED indication of the remaining charge. The Google Fitbit Air brings the traditional Fitbit idea into a new avatar, focusing on health tracking rather than smartwatch features. Its lightweight design is comfortable enough for all-day and overnight wear, while its screenless approach creates a distraction-free experience. Detailed sleep tracking, heart-rate monitoring, recovery metrics and a week-long battery life make it a useful companion for people who want to understand their daily activity without constantly interacting with a device. The Google Health app adds depth to the experience, although automatic workout recognition and Gemini-powered coaching still need refinement. The ₹13,999 price also means you are paying for a dedicated screenless tracker rather than a conventional smartwatch with a display and additional features. For users who prioritise comfortable, continuous health monitoring and prefer to check their data on their phone, the Fitbit Air makes a compelling case. It brings the essence of the old Fitbit into a cleaner, more modern form, with the software experience now playing a central role. Comments have to be in English, and in full sentences. https://www.thehindu.com/sci-tech/techno.body_zh: 订阅账户还可解锁 Premium Stories、Editorials、Opinions 等更多内容。订阅即可畅享这些内容。我记得，Fitbit 曾是一款佩戴在手腕上的纤薄追踪设备，那还是健身手环主要用于计算步数、监测活动量的时代，远早于智能手表热潮兴起。多年来，可穿戴设备已经演变成小型智能手机，配备显示屏、通知和应用。借助 Fitbit Air，Google 以新形态重现了最初那份简约。该无屏追踪器在印度售价 ₹13,999，专注于健康监测、睡眠分析和活动追踪，并通过 Google Health 以及由 Gemini 驱动的指导服务增添智能功能。它的设计旨在不打扰用户，同时持续掌握全天的健康状况。使用一段时间后，问题在于这种回归基础的设计是否适合当今注重健身的用户。让我们一探究竟。Fitbit Air 采用不同的可穿戴设备设计思路，将硬件保持得小巧低调。追踪模块仅重 5.2 克，设备连同腕带总重约 12 克。它将一颗小型鹅卵石形传感器置于编织织物表带内，因此看起来更像一条简单的手环，而非传统智能手表。它没有显示屏或实体按钮，整体设计简洁而简约。舒适性是 Fitbit Air 的主要优势之一。其轻量构造让用户全天佩戴乃至睡觉时都能感到舒适。编织腕带轻柔地贴合手腕，可调节扣带则有助于实现稳固贴合，以便持续追踪。这一点对于一款旨在全天候收集健康数据、而非只在锻炼时佩戴的设备尤为重要。该追踪器还配有可拆卸传感器模块，用户更换腕带时无需更换设备本身。Fitbit Air 配备一盏小型状态 LED，用力双击即可触发提示。白色灯光表示电量充足，红色则表示电量偏低。它还内置振动马达，用于无声闹钟和提醒。该追踪器支持最高 50 米防水，适合游泳使用，但织物腕带沾水后需要充分晾干。Google 提供 Obsidian、Berry、Lavender 和 Fog 等配色，并支持更换腕带。除收集数据外，Fitbit Air 的几乎所有功能都依赖 Google Health 应用。与智能手机配对后，它会在后台追踪活动和健康指标，并同步至应用。仪表板汇集步数、睡眠、心率、准备度和心肺负荷等信息，让用户无需在腕上佩戴显示屏也能回顾每日活动。应用提供了丰富的信息，不过理解其中一些指标需要时间。它将 Today、Fitness、Sleep 和 Health 划分为独立板块，便于查看各项读数。用户还可以连接受支持的健康服务和设备。另一项实用功能是，可让 Fitbit Air 与 Pixel Watch 连接到同一账户。如果你白天更喜欢智能手表，同时又想在睡觉时使用更轻便的追踪器，这一功能会非常方便。由 Gemini 驱动的 Google Health Coach 是较为吸引人的新增功能之一。该功能随 Google Health Premium 订阅提供，可解读健康数据、建议锻炼、解释恢复评分，并帮助制定个性化健身计划。它不只是展示数字，而是试图解释这些数字的含义以及用户可以如何据此行动。不过，其中一些建议可能显得千篇一律；在指导内容始终贴合个人情况之前，这项功能仍需改进。它也应当被视为健康管理工具，而不能替代医疗建议。购买 Fitbit Air 时，Google 附带 3 个月 Premium 试用。试用期结束后，订阅价格为每月 ₹499 或每年 ₹4,999。无需订阅也能使用基础活动追踪、睡眠信息和多项恢复指标，因此用户可以持续使用核心功能，而无需持续付费。Fitbit Air 的无屏设计让使用体验真正不受干扰。用户不会在手腕上收到通知，也没有显示屏诱使自己反复查看。追踪器默默收集信息，由手机应用负责分析。这种方式尤其适合希望监测自身健康、又不愿增加数字干扰来源的人。睡眠追踪是整体体验中较为细致的部分之一。Fitbit Air 能够自动识别睡眠和白天小睡，用户无需手动开始记录。测试期间，它记录了睡眠时长，并估算深度睡眠、快速眼动睡眠和浅睡眠各自所占的时间。它还会突出显示躁动时段和清醒时间。呈现方式让用户很容易了解夜间睡眠的经过，不过睡眠阶段仍属于估算值，而非临床测量结果。应用还会记录静息心率、心率变异性以及准备度评分。这些读数有助于用户观察长期趋势，尤其是追踪器根据个人数据建立基准之后。在初始测试阶段，一些恢复指标尚未形成稳定范围，因此相关洞察起初用处有限，但随着持续追踪，它们会更容易结合实际进行解读。心率数据通过图表呈现，显示各项读数在活动期间如何变化。这有助于用户理解锻炼强度，并在训练结束后回顾过程。不过，自动识别锻炼的稳定性稍差。有时应用能够检测到动作，却将其标记为可能的活动并要求用户确认。编辑已记录训练的功能有所帮助，但若能更准确地自动识别活动，体验会更加流畅。总体而言，Fitbit Air 以小巧设备提供有关活动、睡眠和恢复的详细视图。其追踪信息易于获取，应用也通过多种方式帮助用户理解日常规律。主要局限在于，一些洞察需要积累更多历史数据，而自动锻炼识别和人工智能指导仍有改进空间。电池续航是 Fitbit Air 无屏设计的另一项优势。Google 宣称根据设置和使用情况不同，单次充电最长可使用 7 天。测试期间，追踪器充满电后维持了约 7 天，与公司的说法一致。这减少了用户为了充电而中断全天佩戴的必要性，也让持续健康监测更加方便。Fitbit Air 支持快充，Google 宣称充电 5 分钟即可使用最长 1 天。充满电约需 90 分钟。随附的充电线通过 pogo pin 连接传感器模块，因此充电时需要将追踪器从手腕上取下。用户可以在 Google Health 应用中查看准确的电量百分比，双击追踪器则可通过 LED 快速显示剩余电量。Google Fitbit Air 让传统 Fitbit 的理念以新形态回归，重点转向健康追踪，而非智能手表功能。其轻量设计足够舒适，适合全天及夜间佩戴，无屏方式则营造出不受干扰的使用体验。详细的睡眠追踪、心率监测、恢复指标和长达一周的电池续航，使它成为那些希望了解自身日常活动、又不愿频繁与设备交互的人的实用伙伴。Google Health 应用进一步充实了整体体验，尽管自动锻炼识别和 Gemini 驱动的指导服务仍需改进。₹13,999 的价格也意味着，用户购买的是一款专用无屏追踪器，而不是配有显示屏和更多功能的传统智能手表。对于优先考虑舒适、持续健康监测，并习惯在手机上查看数据的用户而言，Fitbit Air 极具吸引力。它以更简洁、更现代的形式呈现了旧款 Fitbit https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new.summary_zh: 警方表示，周四凌晨，德里一处Kalkaji立交桥附近，一辆超速卡车撞上两人的电动滑板车，造成一名28岁男子死亡，另一人受重伤。警方称，伤者被确认为30岁的Raju Kumar Yadav，目前正在接受治疗。报警者称，一辆卡车撞上了驶往Kalkaji寺庙道路上的滑板车。
https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new.body: A 28-year-old man was killed and another seriously injured after a speeding truck hit their electric scooter near the Kalkaji flyover in Delhi early Thursday, police said. Aditya Kumar, a native of Bihar , died after being taken to the AIIMS Trauma Centre. The injured man, identified as Raju Kumar Yadav, 30, is undergoing treatment, police said. Police received a call about the accident at around 2:28 am on Thursday. The caller reported that a truck had hit a scooter on the road leading towards the Kalkaji temple . A police team reached the spot and found one of the men injured on the roadside. A damaged black electric scooter was also found nearby. Both men were taken to the AIIMS Trauma Centre in an ambulance. Doctors declared Kumar dead on arrival. Yadav was admitted for treatment. The Okhla Industrial Area police station team called the crime team to examine the scene. The team collected two pieces of evidence. Police also seized the damaged scooter. Police searched for eyewitnesses at the accident site and the hospital but found none. A case has been registered against the unidentified truck driver under relevant sections of the law, including those related to rash and negligent driving. Investigators are scanning CCTV footage from cameras installed around the accident site to identify the truck and its driver, police said

https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new.body_zh: 警方称，周四凌晨，一辆超速行驶的卡车在德里卡尔卡吉立交桥附近撞上一辆电动滑板车，造成一名28岁男子死亡，另一名男子受重伤。比哈尔邦人阿迪蒂亚·库马尔被送往AIIMS创伤中心后死亡。警方称，伤者确认为30岁的拉朱·库马尔·亚达夫，目前正在接受治疗。警方于周四凌晨2:28左右接到事故报案。报案人称，一辆卡车撞上了驶往卡尔卡吉神庙方向道路上的滑板车。警察赶赴现场，发现其中一名男子受伤倒在路边。附近还发现一辆损坏的黑色电动滑板车。两人均被救护车送往AIIMS创伤中心。医生宣布库马尔到达医院时死亡。亚达夫则被收治接受治疗。奥克拉工业区警察站团队召集刑事调查组检查现场。该团队收集了两件物证。警方还扣押了受损的滑板车。警方在事故现场和医院寻找目击者，但未找到。警方已依据法律相关规定（包括危险驾驶和过失驾驶相关条款）对身份不明的卡车司机立案。警方称，调查人员正在调取事故现场周边摄像机的监控录像，以查明该卡车及其司机身份。

Khemchand Singh on Sunday (October 25, 2026) said the State could not achieve lasting peace as long as "gun culture" persisted, appealing to people to surrender illegal arms. Mr. Singh made the remarks during a visit to Sinai Camp, a designated camp for militants under the Suspension of Operations (SoO) agreement in Kangpokpi district, according to an official statement. The camp was recently taken over by the CRPF following joint operations involving its CoBRA unit, police and other security forces in the aftermath of the killing of three firewood collectors near Nongshum in Imphal East district. During the operation, 17 people allegedly impersonating SoO cadres using false identities were found at the camp. The facility was supposed to accommodate around 150 cadres, the statement said. Sinai Camp was a designated camp of the Kuki National Army (KNA) and the Kuki Liberation Army (KLA), both signatories to the SoO agreement. The statement described Mr. Singh's visit as the first by a sitting chief minister to a designated SoO camp. Upon his arrival, Mr. Singh inspected the camp premises and was briefed by CRPF and Assam Rifles officers on the operations and the prevailing law and order situation in the area. Interacting with senior security officers and personnel, the chief minister commended the CRPF's CoBRA battalion for its role in the operation that led to the camp coming under the security forces' control. He stressed that adequate care must be taken to ensure that innocent civilians were not affected during combing operations. Security personnel were there to protect people's lives and property, he said. Mr. Singh stressed that Manipur could not progress or achieve lasting peace as long as gun culture prevailed. He appealed to people to renounce violence, surrender illegal weapons and work together to restore peace and harmony in the state. 曼邦首席部长Y. Khemchand Singh于2026年10月25日星期日表示，只要“枪支文化”依然存在，该邦就不可能实现持久和平，并呼吁民众交出非法武器。据官方声明，Singh先生是在参观Sinai Camp时发表上述言论的。该营地位于坎普基地区，是根据停火行动协议（SoO）指定的武装分子营地。

据声明，在东因帕尔地区Nongshum附近3名拾柴者遇害后，中央武装警察部队（CRPF）与警方及其他安全部队开展联合行动，最近接管了该营地。行动期间，执法人员在营地发现17名涉嫌使用虚假身份冒充停火行动协议成员的武装分子。声明称，该设施原计划容纳约150名武装分子。

Sinai Camp是库基民族 Army（KNA）和库基解放军（KLA）的指定营地，两者均为停火行动协议的签署方。声明称，这是曼邦现任首席部长首次访问停火行动协议指定营地。

抵达后，Singh先生视察了营地，并听取中央武装警察部队和阿萨姆步枪队军官关于行动及当地治安状况的汇报。他与高级安全官员及人员交流时，高度评价了中央武装警察部队CoBRA营在促成营地由安全部队接管这次行动中的作用。他强调，搜捕行动必须采取充分措施，确保无辜平民不受影响。他说，安全人员的职责是保护民众的生命和财产。

Singh先生强调，只要枪支文化继续盛行，曼邦就无法发展或实现持久和平。他呼吁民众放弃暴力、交出非法武器，并携手恢复邦内的和平与 harmony。

首席部长随后与当地民间社会组织的代表和村民交流。

https://www.thehindu.com/sci-tech/techno.body: Account subscription benefits alongside Premium Stories, Editorials, Opinions and more. Unlock these with Subscription Sales of Apple’s first folding phone, the iPhone Duo, began on Friday, with market watchers betting on whether the device can reinvent the small foldables market just like the iPhone did for smartphones. The Duo’s reception could prove an early test for new CEO John Ternus, the former hardware chief who unveiled the phone barely a week after taking charge in September. It could also have large implications for a niche category in which rivals such as Samsung Electronics and Huawei Technologies have sold premium offerings for several years. Within minutes of pre-orders opening last Friday, Apple’s estimated delivery dates for the Duo had slipped to late January as demand outpaced supply. The US company called the response from customers “nothing short of extraordinary.” In Sydney, the first Apple store to sell the phones on Friday, a queue of customers formed outside before opening at 8 a.m. local time (2100 GMT). Simon Krishnan, a 48-year-old engineer, paid A$3,899 ($2,734) for a Duo with 512GB memory. “This is a bit of a luxury item for me, because it’s so expensive, but I just think, you know what? Life’s too short,” he said. Early reviews have praised the Duo’s design as well as its sturdy and barely visible hinge, a major feat for phones whose prominent creased screen has long been a drawback and potential deterrent for buyers. But reviewers have said camera compromises including the absence of a telephoto lens and third-party apps that still need to be reworked for the new display size could disappoint some buyers. They have also said the Duo in its smaller, folded state is less handy for the litany of quick tasks that most users carry out each day on standard iPhones, with several prominent reviewers recommending against the Duo for many Apple customers. “It’s been a lot of fun trying the Duo out for a week, but it feels like I’ve gotten to use an extraordinarily polished prototype — not a finished product that I’d want to buy and carry,” longtime Apple commentator John Gruber, author of the blog Daring Fireball, wrote in a review. The limited supplies could disappoint Apple fans lining up in front of stores to buy the Duo. Apple told Reuters that walk-in availability would vary by country, with limited stocks in the US, Australia, Canada, Mexico and much of Britain and Europe. In China, France, Hong Kong, India and Japan, units would be available only for customers who had ordered online. In the China-governed territory of Macau, where the iPhone Duo will be available for walk-in customers only, fans lined up hours in advance of the store opening, social media posts and media reports showed. “Foldables have been an established category for years, but adoption has remained relatively limited compared with conventional smartphones. Apple’s entry could bring the format to a much broader audience,” said Francisco Jeronimo, vice president at market researcher IDC. IDC expects Apple will take 44% of the foldable value in 2026 on 31% of foldable units. By 2027, it will become the market leader in the category both in value and units shipped, IDC forecast. “Apple has made a convincing case for this form factor,” Jeronimo said after spending a week with the passport-shaped Duo. “Now comes the next test: turning excitement into availability, adoption and a lasting new chapter for the smartphone market,” Jeronimo said. https://www.thehindu.com/sci-tech/techno.body_zh:

苹果首款折叠手机iPhone Duo于周五开始销售，市场观察人士押注这款设备能否像iPhone重新定义智能手机那样，开创小型折叠屏手机市场。Duo的市场反响可能是对苹果新任CEO John Ternus的一次早期考验。这位前硬件业务负责人于9月接任后不到一周便发布了这款手机。Duo还可能对这一细分品类产生重大影响；Samsung Electronics和Huawei Technologies等竞争对手已推出高端产品多年。

上周五预购开启仅几分钟后，由于需求超过供应，苹果预估的Duo交付日期已推迟至1月下旬。这家美国公司称，客户的反响“堪称非凡”。在悉尼，首家于周五销售这款手机的苹果门店尚未于当地时间上午8时（格林尼治时间21时）开门，门外就已排起长队。48岁的工程师Simon Krishnan花费3,899澳元（2,734美元）购买了一款配备512GB内存的Duo。他说：“对我来说，这算是有点奢侈，因为价格太昂贵了，但我就想，你知道吗？人生苦短。”

早期评测对Duo的设计以及坚固、几乎看不见的铰链赞不绝口。对许多手机而言，明显的折痕屏幕一直是一大缺点，也可能让消费者望而却步，而苹果在这项技术上取得了重大突破。不过，评测人士表示，取消长焦镜头等相机方面的妥协，以及仍需针对新显示尺寸重新开发的第三方应用，都可能让一些买家失望。他们还指出，Duo处于体积较小的折叠状态时，不如标准iPhone便于处理大多数用户每天都要完成的各种快捷任务；多位知名评测人士因此不建议许多苹果用户购买Duo。

长期评论苹果的作者、博客Daring Fireball的作者John Gruber在评测中写道：“试用Duo一周非常有趣，但它给我的感觉更像是在使用一款打磨得出奇精细的原型，而不是一款我愿意购买并随身携带的成品。”供应有限可能会让排队在苹果门店前购买Duo的苹果粉丝失望。苹果对Reuters表示，到店现货供应情况将因国家而异，美国、澳大利亚、加拿大、墨西哥以及英国和欧洲大部分地区的库存有限。在中国、法国、香港、印度和日本，设备仅向已经在线下单的客户提供。在中国管辖的澳门，iPhone Duo也仅向到店购买者销售；社交媒体帖子和媒体报道显示，粉丝们提前数小时便到门店排队。

市场研究机构IDC副总裁Francisco Jeronimo表示：“折叠屏手机多年来一直是一个成熟的品类，但与conventional智能手机相比，其普及程度仍然相对有限。苹果的进入可能让这种形态触达更广泛的受众。”IDC预计，到2026年，苹果将占折叠屏市场价值的44%，出货量占折叠屏设备总量的31%。IDC预测，到2027年，苹果将成为这一品类在价值和出货量两项指标上的市场领导者。Jeronimo在使用护照大小的Duo一周后表示：“苹果已经为这种外形形态给出了令人信服的理由。”“接下来的考验是，把热度转化为供应、普及，以及智能手机市场持久的新篇章。”Jeronimo说。

Unlock these with Subscription Published - October 25, 2026 04:12 pm IST - THIRUVANANTHAPURAM Left employees’ organisations in the Kerala State Electricity Board (KSEB) have expressed deep concern over an alleged delay in issuing the work order for Phase II roll-out of smart electricity meters in Keralam. The Electricity Employees’ Federation of India (EEFI), an umbrella organisation of Left-backed organisations, has now written to Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan, saying that the financial bids were opened on September 5 this year. Any further delay in issuing the work order would lead to Keralam losing Central grants under the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS) as well as an opportunity for securing additional borrowing space. The delay would also deny electricity consumers in Keralam the opportunity for low-cost smart meter services, the EEFI said. EEFI leaders have urged the Chief Minister to issue a direction to the KSEB to promptly issue the work order as the tender period expires on November 11. The EEFI represents the Centre of Indian Trade Unions (CITU) -backed KSEB Workers’ Association (KSEBWA), the KSEB Officers’ Association (KSEBOA) and the CITU-backed KSEB Contract Workers’ Association (KSEBCWA). The issue pertains to the Phase II roll-out of smart meters wherein up to 50 lakh smart meters are meant to be installed. In its letter to the Chief Minister, the EEFI leaders said that the director board of the KSEB and the State Cabinet had cleared Phase II with a total outlay of ₹2,813.59 crore earlier this year. Of the 11 firms that bid, GridCrest Technologies had quoted ₹1651.75 crore, which was lower by 41.29% than the outlay, opening up a possibility for the people of Keralam to be equipped with smart electricity meters at the lowest available rate, according to the EEFI leaders. However, the KSEB is yet to issue the work order. In February this year, when the CPI(M)-led LDF government was still in power, the KSEB had cleared a proposal for Phase II implementation of smart meters covering around 35 Lakh consumers (extendable up to 50 Lakhs with annual on-boarding of new consumers) under CAPEX mode. “Delays would lead to the tender being cancelled. It is also to be suspected that a move is on to undermine the CAPEX model which enables the people of Keralam to secure smart meter services at a lower cost,” the EEFI said, alleging that certain corporate majors, which had quoted higher amounts in the bidding process, were keen on this project. Smart metering project had been in the news during the LDF government’s term when KSEB unions opposed the TOTEX model of implementation prescribed under RDSS. Consequently, the State government had decided to adopt the CAPEX model with the KSEB as the implementing agency. The (KSEB) director board meeting held on September 29 decided to seek government approval for issuing the work order. But the EEFI leaders said that further government nod is not required for a work that was tendered with government approval and attracted a financial bid that was way lower than the original outlay. https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/k.body_zh:
订阅还可享受 Premium Stories、Editorials、Opinions 等内容。解锁这些内容需订阅。发布于——2026年10月25日，印度标准时间下午4:12——蒂鲁瓦南塔普拉姆

喀拉拉邦电力委员会（KSEB）的左翼雇员组织对据称延迟为喀拉拉邦第二阶段智能电表部署签发工作令表示深切担忧。印度电力雇员联合会（EEFI）是一个由左翼支持组织组成的联合机构，该机构现已致函首席部长V.D.萨特希桑，称相关财务投标已于今年9月5日开标。EEFI表示，如果签发工作令继续延迟，喀拉拉邦不仅会失去《改造型配电部门计划》（RDSS）项下的中央补助，也会失去争取额外借款空间的机会。

EEFI还表示，延迟还将使喀拉拉邦的电力消费者无法享受低成本的智能电表服务。EEFI领导人敦促首席部长指示KSEB尽快签发工作令，因为招标有效期将于11月11日届满。

EEFI代表获得印度工会中心（CITU）支持的KSEB工人协会（KSEBWA）、KSEB官员协会（KSEBOA）以及获得CITU支持的KSEB合同工协会（KSEBCWA）。

此事涉及第二阶段智能电表部署，计划安装最多500万只智能电表。EEFI领导人在致首席部长的信中表示，KSEB董事会和邦内阁已于今年早些时候批准第二阶段计划，总预算为₹2,813.59 crore。11家投标企业中，GridCrest Technologies报价₹1651.75 crore，比预算低41.29%。EEFI领导人称，这使喀拉拉邦民众有机会以现有最低费率安装智能电表。

然而，KSEB仍未签发工作令。今年2月，在由印度共产党（马克思主义）主导的左翼民主阵线（LDF）政府仍在执政时，KSEB已经批准了第二阶段智能电表实施计划。该计划在资本支出模式下覆盖约3500万名消费者，并可随着新消费者每年接入而扩展至最多5000万名。

EEFI表示：“延迟将导致招标被取消。还应怀疑有人正试图破坏资本支出模式，因为该模式能让喀拉拉邦民众以更低成本获得智能电表服务。”该机构指控称，某些在投标过程中报价较高的企业巨头有意承接该项目。

LDF政府执政期间，KSEB工会反对按照RDSS规定采用授予运营转移模式（TOTEX）实施智能计量项目，因此智能计量项目曾成为新闻焦点。随后，邦政府决定采用资本支出模式，并由KSEB担任实施机构。

9月29日举行的KSEB董事会会议决定，请求政府批准签发工作令。但EEFI领导人表示，这项工作已在获得政府批准的情况下完成招标，并吸引了远低于原预算的财务报价，因此无需政府进一步批准。

https://leadership.ng/no-master-design-f.summary: So there is no one single design that the 750 kilometres of Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway is holding. https://leadership.ng/no-master-design-f.summary_zh: 因此，拉各斯至卡巴沿海公路全长750公里，并不存在一套统一的设计方案。他提到拉各斯至卡巴沿海公路的47公里路段，以及贝宁共和国的47.47公里沿海公路，称这些项目耗资1.06万亿奈拉。乌马希表示，连接线段的设计工作仍在进行，并强调不应将其与原有的750公里拉各斯至卡巴沿海公路混为一谈。
https://leadership.ng/no-master-design-f.body: Umahi made the disclosure during a one-hour-30-minute interview on Arise Television monitored by our correspondent on Friday, explaining that the project was being designed and costed section by section. The admission comes amid persistent questions over the highway’s total cost, construction process, environmental approvals and the federal government’s capacity to complete the project, which is one of President Bola Tinubu’s flagship infrastructure initiatives. “There is no single design of any road project that came out, you know, in reality, at the end of the project, the way it was designed,” Umahi said. Asked directly whether an engineering design covered the entire highway, the minister replied, “So these are the procedures. So there is no one single design that the 750 kilometres of Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway is holding. There’s no one single design.” Umahi said the highway had been conceived as far back as 1955, while the concept was gazetted in 2006. However, he maintained that he had not found a complete engineering design, subsoil investigation or other detailed technical documents covering the entire route in the ministry’s archives. According to him, engineering designs are developed for individual sections after environmental assessments and soil investigations establish the route, terrain and technical requirements. He said the procurement arrangement approved by the Federal Executive Council required the project to be procured section by section, arguing that differences in terrain, bridges and engineering requirements made it inappropriate to calculate the overall cost by multiplying an estimated average cost by 750 kilometres. “Who fixed this N15tn that people are just, you know, brandishing everywhere? Who fixed it? And let me also clarify that nobody has the right to do an average cost and multiply by 750,” he said. The absence of a single engineering design and a comprehensive project cost raises questions about how the government intends to establish the highway’s total financial commitment, assess its overall value and communicate its eventual cost to Nigerians. Defending the cost of the first section, Umahi said a standard two-lane carriageway would cost about $5.5 million (N7.3 billion) per kilometre, based on his comparison with a coastal highway project in neighbouring Benin Republic. He referred to a 47-kilometre section of the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway and a 47.47-kilometre coastal road in Benin Republic, which he said cost N1.06 trillion. The minister cited a cost of about N7.5 billion per kilometre for a three-carriageway configuration before adjusting the estimate to reflect a standard two-lane carriageway. He put the adjusted cost at approximately $5.5 million per kilometre, using an exchange rate of N1,330 to the dollar. He said differences in road configurations and project specifications must be considered before comparing the costs of the two projects. On environmental approvals, Umahi confirmed that construction began after the ministry obtained a provisional Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) certificate. “Every project has provisional ESIA,” he said, adding that environmental issues, resettlement and other associated programmes were being considered during implementation. He explained that a final certificate would follow as the project progressed and outstanding requirements were addressed. He also maintained that environmental assessments were being conducted section by section rather than through a single assessment covering the entire route. Umahi said the ministry had obtained final environmental approval for the first 47-kilometre section. The highway has attracted criticism over its cost, route and environmental implications since construction began. The federal government has defended it as a major transport corridor intended to improve connectivity along Nigeria’s coastline. Umahi also clarified his remarks about an additional 400 kilometres linked to the project, following questions about whether President Tinubu had ordered a diversion from the original route. He said the additional stretch involved connecting the coastal highway to the existing East-West Road through Edo State, rather than abandoning the original alignment. “The alignment is intact,” he said, insisting that Edo remained part of the route, which traverses Lagos, Ogun, Ondo, Edo, Delta, Bayelsa, Rivers, Akwa Ibom and Cross River states. The minister acknowledged that describing the connection as a diversion was inaccurate, explaining that the plan was to provide a spur linking the coastal highway to the East-West Road. “It’s to also put a spur. The word divert, if I used that then it’s a slip of the tongue. We are talking about the connection of the Lagos-Calabar coastal highway, we are connecting it also to have a spur on the East-West Road,” Umahi said. He added that the connection would provide an alternative route and support the reconstruction of the East-West Road, parts of which he said had deteriorated and fallen below flood levels. Umahi said design work on the connection was ongoing, stressing that it should not be confused with the original 750-kilometre Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway. We’ve got the edge. https://leadership.ng/no-master-design-f.title_zh: 乌马希承认，拉各斯至卡拉巴尔750公里高速公路尚无总体设计
https://leadership.ng/no-master-design-f.body_zh: 乌马希周五在 Arise Television 接受了长达一个半小时的采访，本次采访由本社记者监督。他解释道，该项目正在按路段逐一进行设计和成本核算。就在他作出这一披露之际，外界对该公路的总成本、施工流程、环境审批以及联邦政府完成这一项目的能力持续存在疑问；该项目是总统博拉·蒂努布的旗舰基础设施项目之一。乌马希说：“事实上，任何道路项目都不存在一份最终成型的单一设计方案，不会按照最初设计的样子建成。”当被直接问及是否有一份覆盖整条公路的工程设计时，这位部长答复道：“流程就是这样。因此，拉各斯至卡拉巴尔沿海公路这750公里并不存在一份统一的设计，也不存在一份单一的设计。”乌马希称，该公路的构想早在1955年就已提出，相关概念于2006年正式公布。然而，他坚持表示，在该部档案中并未找到覆盖整条路线的完整工程设计、地下土壤调查或其他详细技术文件。据他介绍，工程设计需在环境评估和土壤调查确定路线、地形及技术要求后，针对各个路段分别编制。他说，联邦执行委员会批准的采购安排要求该项目按路段分别采购，并认为地形、桥梁和工程要求各不相同，因此不宜用估算的平均成本乘以750公里来计算项目总成本。乌马希说：“这个15万亿奈拉是谁算出来的？人们到处都在引用。这个数字是谁定的？我还要澄清，任何人都无权计算平均成本后再乘以750。”缺乏统一工程设计和全面项目成本估算，引发了外界对政府如何确定该公路总财政投入、评估整体价值以及向尼日利亚民众公布最终成本的疑问。为首段公路的成本辩护时，乌马希称，根据他与邻国贝宁共和国一项沿海公路项目的比较，标准双车道车行道每公里成本约为550万美元（73亿奈拉）。他提到了拉各斯至卡拉巴尔沿海公路的47公里路段，以及贝宁共和国一条47.47公里的沿海公路，并称后者耗资1.06万亿奈拉。部长援引的数据是，三车道配置每公里成本约为75亿奈拉，之后他调整了估算，以反映标准双车道车行道。按照1美元兑换1,330奈拉的汇率，他估算调整后的成本约为每公里550万美元。他说，在比较两个项目的成本之前，必须考虑道路配置和项目规格方面的差异。在环境审批方面，乌马希确认，该部取得临时《环境与社会影响评估》（ESIA）证书后，施工便已启动。他说：“每个项目都有临时ESIA。”他补充称，环境问题、移民安置及其他相关方案正在实施过程中予以考虑。他解释说，随着项目推进、各项尚未满足的要求得到处理，将随后颁发最终证书。他还坚持表示，环境评估是按路段分别进行，而非通过一次评估覆盖整条路线。乌马希称，该部已经为首个47公里路段取得最终环境批准。自施工启动以来，该公路因成本、路线及其对环境的影响而一直受到批评。联邦政府则为其辩护，称这是一条旨在改善尼日利亚沿海地区交通联系的主要运输走廊。针对有关总统蒂努布是否下令将公路改离原路线的问题，乌马希还澄清了自己此前关于项目将延伸400公里的说法。他说，新增路段是要通过埃多州将沿海公路与现有东西路连接起来，而不是放弃原有路线。乌马希说：“原有路线保持不变。”他坚称，埃多州仍是路线的一部分；该路线途经拉各斯、奥贡、奥恩多、埃多、德尔塔、巴耶尔萨、河流、阿夸伊博姆和十字河州。部长承认，将这一连接称为“改道”并不准确，并解释说，相关计划是修建一条支线，将沿海公路与东西路连接起来。乌马希说：“同时还要修建一条支线。如果我用了‘改道’这个词，那就是口误。我们说的是拉各斯至卡拉巴尔沿海公路的连接问题，也就是让它通过一条支线接入东西路。”他补充称，这一连接将提供一条替代路线，并支持东西路的重建；他称东西路部分路段已经恶化，路面高度甚至低于洪水水位。乌马希表示，连接段的设计工作仍在进行，并强调不应将其与原有的750公里拉各斯至卡拉巴尔沿海公路混为一谈。掌握独家动态。获取实时报道、突发独家消息和独家视角，直接推送到您的手机。不要满足于过时新闻。加入 LEADERSHIP NEWS WhatsApp 频道，随时随地掌握最新动态 →

Unlock these with Subscription Former Minister and BJP State vice-president Harathalu Halappa has urged the State government to supply electricity to agricultural pump sets for at least seven to eight hours during the day, as farmers are struggling to save their crops amid severe drought. He warned that the party would intensify its agitation if the demand was not met. In a press conference in Shivamogga on Saturday (October 24, 2026) Mr. Halappa said farmers in Hosanagara, Sagar, Sorab, Shivamogga Rural and Ripponpet, among other places in the district, were facing disruptions in power supply. Owing to the weak monsoon, standing crops such as paddy and maize are drying up, and areca plantations also faced the threat of damage due to water shortage. “Earlier, farmers received seven hours of power a day. Officers now say they have received instructions from senior officials to supply six hours. In reality, however, even this is not supplied continuously, as power is cut for 30 to 45 minutes at a time, so farmers do not get the full supply.” Officers have not responded to requests to provide the lost hours later, he alleged. Since pump sets receive power only at night, farmers around Ripponpet in Hosanagara taluk have to go to their farms after dark to irrigate their plantations, despite the threat from wild elephants in the area. There have been fatalities in elephant attacks in the past, he said. Farmers in the area had staged protests demanding daytime power for their safety. Mr. Halappa also pointed out that vacancies in the Mangalore Electricity Supply Company (MESCOM) were contributing to the problem. The shortage of officers and linemen was affecting the maintenance and repair of power lines. He called for steps to ensure adequate power supply before the situation worsens in the coming summer, and warned that the party would intensify its protests across the district if the government did not respond. A man holds a 'Vote Blue' sign while sitting in a golf cart during a Democratic rally in The Villages, Florida, US, October 17, 2026. WASHINGTON, USA – Nonpartisan analysts say Democrats stand a good chance of winning the US House of Representatives and possibly the Senate in the November 3 midterm elections , which would give them a slice of power in Washington after two years of Republican control. Democrats argue that Republicans have allowed President Donald Trump ‘s administration to declare war and control spending, even though the US Constitution reserves those powers for lawmakers. Here are some ways a Democratic Congress could hem in Trump’s foreign policy. Trump did not secure approval from Congress before he launched the war with Iran on February 28 , and Democrats have voted repeatedly to end the fighting unless he does so. One of these resolutions passed with support from a handful of Republicans, but Trump’s administration ignored it. With control of the House or the Senate, Democrats could cut defense spending to pressure Trump to obtain permission from Congress to continue the war. They could also require administration officials to testify publicly about their plans. Trump has largely halted direct US financial and military aid to Ukraine, despite broad support from Democratic and Republican lawmakers as it fights a Russian invasion . Most recently, he has angered members of Congress, including many Republicans, by lifting sanctions on Russian diesel and waiving sanctions on Russian energy only weeks after signing them into law. With a victory in both chambers in November, Democrats would be able to decide what gets voted on and when. That could allow them to approve new aid to Ukraine, which likely would pass with the two-thirds majorities needed to overcome a Trump veto. They could also target other Trump activities. For example, Representative Gregory Meeks of New York, who could head the House Foreign Affairs Committee if Democrats win control, has introduced bipartisan legislation to block Trump’s plan to bring Russian diesel back into the global market. Support for Israel has plummeted among Democrats over its conduct in the Gaza war, which has killed tens of thousands of Palestinian civilians. The ongoing violence in the Israeli-occupied West Bank and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s close alliance with Republicans have also been factors. Democrats could limit or end military aid to Israel, which amounted to $3.8 billion in the most recent fiscal year. That is more than was provided to any other country. Nearly half of House Democrats voted this summer to cut off aid to Israel. Some of those who voted against that effort, such as Meeks, have backed limits on providing weapons like heavy bombs to Israel. Democrats are far more likely than Trump’s Republicans to limit military spending. Trump asked for an unprecedented 67% increase in the military budget this year, to $1.5 trillion, but Democrats blocked it in the Senate, citing his refusal to consult Congress about the Iran war and his steep cuts to social programs. Trump has also withheld or canceled billions of dollars in foreign aid approved by Congress. Many Democrats have been angered by the cuts and say they will try to restore funding. https://leadership.ng/federal-government.body: “Gas has been a priority within that reform agenda because Nigeria is, as you all know, even more gas-rich than it is oil-rich, and the gas is arguably the most important physical resource for industrialisation,” special adviser to the President on Oil and Gas, Olu Verheijen said. According to her, government is now promoting gas production activities to secure firm energy security which will at the same create value in its industrialization efforts. Verheijen, disclosed this at the Africa Interviews Sustainability Forum 2026 in Lagos. She also said government has settled more than ₦100 billion in outstanding gas debts since January 2026, in a move aimed at strengthening the gas-to-power value chain and improving electricity supply. The payments were made under the Presidential Power Sector Financial Reform Programme and comes as Nigeria continues to grapple with electricity supply challenges, with gas supply and payments to producers remaining important to the performance of the power sector. Clearing outstanding obligations is expected to support confidence across the gas-to-power chain, although sustained improvement will also depend on regular payments, reliable gas delivery and the financial health of electricity market participants. Verheijen also highlighted government measures introduced since 2023 to encourage the use of liquefied petroleum gas, LPG, for household cooking. These include import duty waivers and zero-rated value-added tax measures for LPG and gas cylinders, intended to make cleaner cooking alternatives more accessible and reduce dependence on firewood. “A gas-rich nation cannot be comfortable while families remain stuck in the age of firewood,” she said. According to the presidential adviser, reforms under President Bola Tinubu’s administration are designed to remove barriers to investment and unlock Nigeria’s gas resources for industrialisation, electricity generation and economic growth. She disclosed that Nigeria had recorded four final investment decisions, FIDs, on gas projects in less than two years, while average daily gas production had increased from about seven billion cubic feet to eight billion cubic feet. Nigeria holds more than 200 trillion cubic feet of proven gas reserves, Verheijen said, but stressed that the country must attract sustained investment to convert its resource base into economic value. “A country can sit on enormous natural wealth and fail to turn it into energy to power industry, industries that create jobs and jobs that help us grow incomes,” she said. “What turns resources into prosperity is investment, consistent investment that responds to predictable incentives and a stable environment,” she added. Verheijen said Tinubu had directed his administration to identify and address the factors preventing investment from keeping pace with Nigeria’s economic potential. “When President Bola Tinubu assumed office in 2023, he gave us a very clear mandate: understand why investment has not moved at the pace of Nigeria’s potential and fix it,” she said. The four gas project investment decisions, including the Ima project in September 2026, reflect growing activity in the sector, Verheijen said. She also noted the increasing contribution of indigenous producers to domestic gas supply. Addressing Africa’s energy transition, she argued that governments across the continent should balance environmental sustainability with energy security, industrial development and job creation. “For Africa, the energy transition must mean transformation, molecules converted into megawatts, fertilizer, petrochemicals, cleaner mobility, manufacturing, jobs and exports,” she said. Verheijen also maintained that African countries should determine the pace of their energy transitions according to their development priorities and economic circumstances, rather than have those decisions imposed externally. “The energy transition must also mean agency. Africa is right to decide for itself how fast it decarbonises, rather than having those choices made for us by others. It is about affirming our right to be the authors of our own energy transition,” she said. She further emphasised the need to measure and reduce methane emissions from gas operations while ensuring that host communities benefit meaningfully from resource development. The settlement of the outstanding gas debts represents a step towards addressing financial constraints within Nigeria’s gas-to-power chain. However, the broader test will be whether improved payment discipline and investment translate into more reliable gas supplies, stronger electricity generation and better power delivery to homes and businesses. Meanwhile, Renaissance Africa Energy (RAE) says it’s growing its oil production to 500,000 barrels a day by 2030. The indigenous firm also said it will alongside this projection expand gas supply as part of broader efforts to improve Nigeria’s energy security and accelerate industrial development. The company also plans to grow its production portfolio to one million barrels of oil equivalent per day by 2030, supported by additional gas production and investments in exploration, development and infrastructure-led opportunities. The Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of RAE, Engr. Tony Attah, disclosed this in a keynote address delivered on his behalf by the company’s Vice President, Exploration, Dr. John Bosco Uche, at a pre-conference workshop organised by the Nigerian Association of Petroleum Explorationists (NAPE). The workshop, themed: “Navigating Nigeria’s Upstream Future: Exploration and Development Approaches vs. Energy Security Demand,” examined strategies for increasing petroleum reserves, accelerating project delivery and meeting the country’s growing energy needs. Attah said Nigeria’s energy security depended not merely on its abundant oil and gas resources but on its ability to convert those resources into reliable energy supply, industrial growth, employment and improved living standards. The Renaissance helmsman noted that despite the country’s substantial hydrocarbon resources, millions of Nigerians still lacked reliable access to energy, stressing that the real measure of energy security was the extent to which resources powered homes, industries, hospitals and schools. According to him, exploration, development and production must operate as an integrated value chain to ensure that Nigeria meets its current energy requirements while sustaining supply for future generations. “Exploration creates options. Development transforms options into projects. Production converts projects into energy, and energy security exists only when all these three operate as an integrated value chain,” he said. The Renaissance CEO emphasised the need for continuous investment in exploration to replenish reserves, warning that failure to discover new resources would undermine future production and threaten long-term energy security. He explained that every barrel produced today depended on discoveries and investments made in previous years, making reserve replacement essential to sustaining Nigeria’s petroleum industry. Attah also stressed the importance of accelerating the journey from discovery to first production, arguing that the speed of project delivery had become as important as the volume of resources available. “Energy security is not only about volume; it is about velocity,” he said, adding that discoveries that take decades to reach production could fail to address the immediate energy needs of a growing economy. He identified infrastructure-led exploration as a key strategy for shortening project timelines and improving the commercial value of discoveries, noting that Renaissance had adopted the approach as a central pillar of its near-term strategy. According to him, leveraging existing infrastructure, data and technical knowledge could help unlock additional value from mature assets while reducing the time and cost required to bring resources to market. The company’s strategy, he said, was anchored on three principles: safely receiving inherited assets, stabilising operations and growing production. Attah disclosed that within its first 100 days of assuming operatorship of the assets in March 2025, Renaissance added approximately 100,000 barrels of oil to its portfolio and Nigeria’s production. He added that the company had sustained gas exports while increasing domestic gas supply, with further expansion planned to support the country’s industrialisation and energy needs. On the role of natural gas, Attah described the resource as a major driver of Nigeria’s economic transformation, noting its potential to strengthen manufacturing, improve industrial competitiveness, create jobs and stimulate economic growth. “Gas is not merely a transition fuel for Nigeria; it is our transformation fuel,” he said. He maintained that Nigeria could achieve greater economic benefits by deploying its gas resources to support industrial development and expand access to reliable energy. The Renaissance CEO further highlighted the importance of indigenous capabilities, technology and human capital development in building a sustainable upstream industry. He said the growing participation of indigenous operators represented not just a transfer of assets but also a transfer of responsibility for developing the country’s resources and creating long-term value. Attah also identified artificial intelligence, digital technologies and advanced software as tools for improving exploration decisions, maturing prospects and enhancing operational performance. He said Renaissance had tested several digital solutions and planned to deploy additional technologies to improve the identification and development of exploration opportunities. On workforce development, he announced that the company planned to recruit more than 100 young graduates by November 2026 to strengthen its workforce and contribute to building local technical capacity. He added that sustainable development required the industry to balance environmental responsibility with the need to provide affordable and reliable energy for economic progress. Attah urged industry stakeholders to focus on execution, investment and collaboration, stressing that Nigeria’s petroleum wealth would deliver lasting benefits only when resources were continuously discovered, developed and produced at a pace that matched the country’s energy demand. He concluded that effective leadership with a clear vision and disciplined project execution would be essential to converting the country’s oil and gas potential into energy security, industrialisation and shared prosperity. https://leadership.ng/federal-government.title_zh: 联邦政府制定更广泛的天然气转型战略，以确保稳固的能源安全
https://leadership.ng/federal-government.body_zh: “在这一改革议程中，天然气一直是优先事项，因为各位都知道，尼日利亚的天然气储量甚至比石油储量更加丰富，而天然气可以说是推动工业化最重要的实体资源，”总统石油与天然气特别顾问 Olu Verheijen 表示。她表示，政府目前正在推动天然气生产活动，以保障稳健的能源安全，同时为工业化努力创造价值。Verheijen 在拉各斯举行的 2026 年非洲访谈可持续发展论坛上披露了这些情况。她还表示，自 2026 年 1 月以来，政府已结清超过 ₦100 billion 的天然气欠款，旨在加强天然气发电价值链并改善电力供应。这些付款根据总统电力部门金融改革计划执行；与此同时，尼日利亚继续应对电力供应挑战，天然气供应及向生产商付款仍是电力部门表现的重要因素。清偿拖欠款项预计将增强天然气发电产业链各方的信心，但要实现持续改善，还取决于定期付款、可靠的天然气输送以及电力市场参与者的财务健康状况。Verheijen 还重点介绍了政府自 2023 年以来为鼓励家庭使用液化石油气（LPG）而采取的措施，其中包括对 LPG 和气瓶免征进口关税并实行零税率增值税，以使更清洁的烹饪燃料更容易获得，并减少家庭对柴火的依赖。“一个天然气资源丰富的国家，如果家庭仍然停留在使用柴火的时代，就不可能感到安心，”她说。总统顾问表示，博拉· Tinubu 总统领导下的政府推行改革，旨在消除投资障碍，释放尼日利亚的天然气资源，为工业化、发电和经济增长赋能。她透露，在不到两年的时间里，尼日利亚已有 4 个天然气项目作出最终投资决定（FIDs），日均天然气产量也从约 70 亿立方英尺增至 80 亿立方英尺。Verheijen 表示，尼日利亚拥有超过 200 万亿立方英尺的探明天然气储量，但强调该国必须吸引持续投资，才能将资源基础转化为经济价值。“一个国家可能坐拥巨额自然资源，却未能将其转化为为工业提供动力的能源，无法创造就业，而就业又帮助我们提高收入，”她说。“将资源转化为繁荣的是投资，是回应可预期激励措施和稳定环境的持续投资，”她补充道。Verheijen 表示，Tinubu 已指示政府找出并解决阻碍投资进度未能匹配尼日利亚经济潜力的因素。“博拉· Tinubu 总统于 2023 年就任时，给了我们一项非常明确的指示：查明投资为何未能按照尼日利亚的潜力同步推进，并解决这个问题，”她说。Verheijen 表示，包括 2026 年 9 月 Ima 项目在内的 4 个天然气项目投资决定，反映出该行业活动日益增加。她还指出，本土生产商对国内天然气供应的贡献正在增加。在谈及非洲能源转型时，她认为，非洲各国政府都应在环境可持续性与能源安全、工业发展和创造就业之间实现平衡。“对非洲而言，能源转型必须意味着转型，把分子转化为兆瓦、化肥、石化产品、更清洁的交通、制造业、就业和出口，”她说。Verheijen 还坚持认为，非洲国家应根据自身发展重点和经济状况决定能源转型速度，而不应由外部强加这些决定。“能源转型还必须意味着自主权。非洲有权自行决定以多快速度实现脱碳，而不是让别人替我们作出选择。这关乎确认我们有权书写自己的能源转型篇章，”她说。她进一步强调，需要衡量并减少天然气运营产生的甲烷排放，同时确保东道社区从资源开发中获得切实利益。清偿拖欠的天然气债务，是解决尼日利亚天然气发电价值链内资金限制的一步。然而，更广泛的考验在于，改善后的付款纪律和投资能否带来更可靠的天然气供应、更强的发电能力，以及向家庭和企业更好的供电。与此同时，Renaissance Africa Energy（RAE）表示，正将石油产量提高至 2030 年每天 500,000 桶。这家本土企业还表示，将在实现这一目标的同时扩大天然气供应，作为改善尼日利亚能源安全和加快工业发展的更广泛努力的一部分。公司还计划在勘探、开发和基础设施主导机会方面的投资及新增天然气产量支持下，将生产组合扩大至 2030 年每天 100 万桶油当量。RAE 董事总经理兼首席执行官 Tony Attah 工程博士，在尼日利亚石油勘探家协会（NAPE）组织的会前研讨会上，通过公司勘探副总裁 John Bosco Uche 博士代其发表主旨演讲时披露了上述情况。研讨会的主题为：“把握尼日利亚上游行业的未来：勘探与开发方式对能源安全需求”，会议探讨了增加石油储量、加快项目交付和满足国家日益增长的能源需求等战略。Attah 表示，尼日利亚的能源安全不仅依赖其丰富的石油和天然气资源，也取决于能否将这些资源转化为可靠能源供应、工业增长、就业和更高生活水平。Renaissance 掌舵者指出，尽管该国拥有大量碳氢化合物资源，但数百万尼日利亚人仍无法稳定获得能源，因此真正的能源安全衡量标准，是资源能否为家庭、工业、医院和学校供电。他表示，勘探、开发和生产必须作为整合的价值链运行，以确保尼日利亚满足当前能源需求，同时为后代维持供应。“勘探创造选择，开发把选择转化为项目，生产把项目转化为能源，而只有这三者作为整合价值链运转时，能源安全才存在，”他说。Renaissance 首席执行官强调，需要持续投资勘探以补充储量，并警告未能发现新资源将削弱未来产量，威胁长期能源安全。他解释道，如今产出的每一桶石油都依赖往年取得的发现和投资，因此必须以储量替代来维持尼日利亚石油工业的持续发展。Attah 还强调，加快从发现到首次生产的进程至关重要，认为项目交付速度已与可用资源量同等重要。“能源安全不仅关乎数量，也关乎速度，”他说，并补充称，需要数十年才能投产的新发现，可能无法满足不断增长经济的即时能源需求。他把基础设施主导型勘探列为缩短项目周期和提高发现商业价值的关键战略，并指出 Renaissance 已将这一做法作为近期战略的支柱。他认为，利用现有基础设施、数据和技术知识，有助于从成熟资产中释放更多价值，同时减少将资源推向市场所需的时间和成本。他说，公司的战略以三项原则为基础：安全接收遗留资产、稳定运营以及扩大产量。Attah 透露，自 2025 年 3 月接管这些资产的运营商职责后的前 100 天内，Renaissance 为其生产组合及尼日利亚产量增加了约 100,000 桶石油。他补充说，公司在维持天然气出口的同时增加了国内天然气供应，并计划进一步扩大供应，以支持国家工业化和能源需求。在谈及天然气的作用时，Attah 称其是推动尼日利亚经济转型的重要动力，指出天然气有望强化制造业、提高工业竞争力、创造就业并刺激经济增长。“天然气对尼日利亚而言不仅是过渡燃料，更是我们的转型燃料，”他说。他坚持认为，尼日利亚可以通过利用天然气资源支持工业发展并扩大可靠能源的可及性，获得更大的经济收益。Renaissance 首席执行官还强调，在建设可持续的上游行业时，本土能力、技术和人力资本开发至关重要。他说，本土运营商参与度日益提高，不仅意味着资产转移，也意味着开发国家资源和创造长期价值的责任转移。Attah 还把人工智能、数字技术和先进软件列为改善勘探决策、推进资产成熟及提升运营表现的工具。他说，Renaissance 已测试多种数字解决方案，并计划部署更多技术，以改善勘探机会的识别和开发。在人才队伍建设方面，他宣布，公司计划在 2026 年 11 月前招聘 100 多名年轻毕业生，以加强人才队伍，并为建设本地技术能力作出贡献。他补充称，可持续发展要求行业在环境责任与为经济进步提供价格可承受且可靠的能源之间实现平衡。Attah 敦促行业相关方把重点放在执行、投资与合作上，强调只有以符合国家能源需求的速度持续发现、开发和生产资源，尼日利亚的石油财富才能带来持久利益。他最后表示，有效的领导、清晰的愿景和有纪律的项目执行，将是把该国油气潜力转化为能源安全、工业化和共同繁荣的关键。我们掌握独家优势。订阅 LEADERSHIP NEWS 的 WhatsApp https://leadership.ng/nigeria-gas-associ.summary_zh: 安全问题是尼日利亚液化石油气营销商协会最近一次会议中利益相关方讨论的主要议题之一。该协会还呼吁行业经营者优先重视安全、监管合规和数字化，以推动尼日利亚液化石油气行业实现可持续增长。
https://leadership.ng/nigeria-gas-associ.body: Safety concerns were among major considers among stakeholders at the Nigerian Association of Liquefied Petroleum Gas Marketers (NALPGAM), recent meeting. The association also called on industry operators to prioritise safety, regulatory compliance and digitalisation to drive sustainable growth in Nigeria’s LPG sector. The call followed its 2026 webinar with the theme: “Downstream LPG Operational Excellence and Compliance,” which brought together industry operators, regulators and other stakeholders to address safety risks, market volatility, operational losses and regulatory requirements. Barrister Edu Inyang, National President, NALPGAM, said that “the future of Nigeria’s LPG industry cannot be achieved by increasing volumes alone. We must grow safely, responsibly, efficiently and sustainably. Safety is not an occasional campaign; it must become a continuous industry culture.” A key outcome was the adoption of the aspiration for a “NALPGAM Standard of Operational Excellence,” built on four principles: safe and well-maintained facilities, competent and trained operators, compliant processes, and customer protection. Participants urged operators to embed safety in daily operations, strengthen preventive maintenance, comply with licensing and incident-reporting requirements, and eliminate unsafe practices, including unauthorised propane blending and illegal decanting. “Compliance is not merely a regulatory burden; it is a business advantage. Well-managed LPG operations reduce accidents, improve efficiency, protect investments and strengthen public confidence in our industry,” Inyang said. The webinar also highlighted digital technologies including smart filling systems, automated tank gauges, load cells, flow meters and vehicle tracking as practical tools to reduce product losses, improve accountability and strengthen operational efficiency. With Nigeria targeting LPG consumption of approximately five million tonnes annually by 2030, stakeholders called for increased industry participation in the Decade of Gas LPG penetration programme and stronger collaboration to expand access, improve cylinder traceability and promote certified local manufacturing. NALPGAM further called on regulators and programme coordinators to involve its members in implementing LPG penetration and cylinder recirculation initiatives, leveraging their nationwide reach and proximity to consumers. “Our aspiration is clear: every LPG facility must be safe and properly maintained, every operator competent and adequately trained, every process compliant, and every customer protected. This is the standard of operational excellence we must collectively pursue,” Inyang said. The Association reaffirmed its commitment to constructive engagement with government, regulators and industry stakeholders to build a safer, more efficient and competitive LPG market. NALPGAM’s message is clear: safety must be the industry’s culture, compliance its character, technology its catalyst, and operational excellence its competitive advantage. The association’s push is also coming as the Special Adviser to the President on Oil and Gas, Olu Verheijen, recently highlighted government measures introduced since 2023 to encourage the use of liquefied petroleum gas, LPG, for household cooking. These include import duty waivers and zero-rated value-added tax measures for LPG and gas cylinders, intended to make cleaner cooking alternatives more accessible and reduce dependence on firewood. “A gas-rich nation cannot be comfortable while families remain stuck in the age of firewood,” she told the Africa Interviews Sustainability Forum 2026 in Lagos. https://leadership.ng/nigeria-gas-associ.title_zh: 尼日利亚天然气协会采用标准运营模板，推动尼日利亚液化石油气安全
https://leadership.ng/nigeria-gas-associ.body_zh:
在尼日利亚液化石油气销售商协会最近一次会议上，安全问题是各利益相关方重点考虑的事项之一。该协会还呼吁行业运营商优先重视安全、监管合规和数字化，以推动尼日利亚液化石油气行业实现可持续增长。此次呼吁紧随协会2026年网络研讨会举行，研讨会主题为“液化石油气下游运营卓越与合规”，汇聚行业运营商、监管机构及其他利益相关方，共同应对安全风险、市场波动、运营损失和监管要求。NALPGAM全国主席、律师埃杜·因扬格表示：“尼日利亚液化石油气行业的未来不能仅靠扩大销量来实现。我们必须安全、负责任、高效且可持续地发展。安全不是偶尔开展的宣传活动，而必须成为行业持续不变的文化。”

此次会议的一项主要成果，是通过以四项原则为基础的“NALPGAM运营卓越标准”倡议：设施安全并得到良好维护，运营商具备胜任能力并接受充分培训，流程符合监管要求，以及客户得到保护。参会者敦促运营商将安全融入日常运营，加强预防性维护，遵守许可和事故报告要求，并消除不安全做法，包括未经授权的丙烷混装和非法罐装倒卖。

因扬格说：“合规不仅是监管负担，更是商业优势。管理良好的液化石油气运营可以减少事故、提高效率、保护投资，并增强公众对本行业的信心。”

网络研讨会还重点介绍了智能灌装系统、自动储罐计量仪、称重传感器、流量计和车辆追踪等数字技术，将其视为减少产品损失、提高问责度和增强运营效率的实用工具。尼日利亚的目标是到2030年将液化石油气年消费量提高至约500万吨，各利益相关方呼吁更多行业运营商参与“天然气十年液化石油气普及计划”，并加强合作，以扩大供应可及性、改善气瓶可追溯性并推动获得认证的本地制造。NALPGAM还呼吁监管机构和计划协调方，在实施液化石油气普及和气瓶循环使用计划时让协会成员参与其中，发挥其全国覆盖网络以及贴近消费者的优势。

因扬格说：“我们的目标很明确：每一处液化石油气设施都必须安全并得到适当维护，每一名运营商都必须具备胜任能力并接受充分培训，每一道流程都必须合规，每一位客户都必须受到保护。这就是我们必须共同追求的运营卓越标准。”

该协会重申，将继续与政府、监管机构和行业利益相关方开展建设性合作，以打造更安全、更高效且更具竞争力的液化石油气市场。NALPGAM传达的信息十分明确：安全必须成为行业文化，合规必须成为行业品格，技术必须成为行业催化剂，而运营卓越必须成为行业竞争优势。

就在该协会推动这些工作的同时，总统石油与天然气特别顾问奥卢·弗赫伊恩最近介绍了政府自2023年以来为鼓励家庭烹饪使用液化石油气而出台的措施。这些措施包括对液化石油气和燃气瓶实行进口关税豁免及零税率增值税，旨在让更清洁的烹饪选择更加容易获得，并减少家庭对柴火的依赖。她在拉各斯举行的“非洲访谈可持续论坛2026”上表示：“一个天然气资源丰富的国家，不能在家庭仍被困于柴火时代的情况下感到安心。”

https://leadership.ng/kingibe-taps-into-.summary: Senator Kingibe’s warning that Nigeria’s new tax laws will compel citizens to surrender 25 per cent of their earnings to the government has ignited a debate extending beyond taxation. During an election period, the factual basis of the senator’s assertion may prove secondary as she taps into the sentiments Nigerians generally feel about the new tax laws and economic reforms of the president’s administration. Kingibe’s position as a senator gives her claims institutional visibility.
https://leadership.ng/kingibe-taps-into-.summary_zh: 参议员金吉比警告称，尼日利亚新税法将迫使公民把收入的25%交给政府，由此引发了一场超出税收本身的讨论。在选举时期，这位参议员言论的事实依据可能显得次要，因为她利用了尼日利亚民众对新税法以及总统政府经济改革的普遍情绪。金吉比担任参议员，使其主张获得了制度层面的关注。
https://leadership.ng/kingibe-taps-into-.body: It can be seen in the ease with which laws are passed, from the tax reform bills to the 2026 Electoral Act. That only changes when lawmakers are faced with defending their seats from outside the ruling party. And a lot is going on in the economy for opposition lawmakers to focus on. Senator Ireti Kingine, an opposition lawmaker representing the FCT, chose one of the most contentious laws passed by the National Assembly to strike at the ruling party, its newly introduced tax laws. Senator Kingibe’s warning that Nigeria’s new tax laws will compel citizens to surrender 25 per cent of their earnings to the government has ignited a debate extending beyond taxation. The reality is that only the highest-income earners pay that level of personal tax, while the lowest-income earners are expected to pay between 0 and 18 per cent. Regardless of accuracy, its rapid circulation reflects the declining public confidence in economic policies introduced under President Bola Tinubu’s government. It also exposes how economic anxiety can amplify political messaging and become a handy weapon to turn voters against the ruling party. During an election period, the factual basis of the senator’s assertion may prove secondary as she taps into the sentiments Nigerians generally feel about the new tax laws and economic reforms of the president’s administration. Here is why her warning resonates. Nigerians are confronting the cumulative consequences of petrol subsidy removal, currency depreciation, rising living costs, and electricity tariffs. Against this backdrop, taxation can appear less like an instrument of public finance and more like another demand on already strained household incomes. Kingibe’s position as a senator gives her claims institutional visibility. Nevertheless, even a claim made for political ends can intensify perceptions of hardship. Many Nigerians, small business owners, and manufacturers already distrust government assurances, while the tweaking of facts and interpretations can reinforce existing fears. For the opposition, particularly the ADC to which Senator Kingibe belongs and is seeking reelection, these issues offer legitimate grounds for scrutinising the government. Fuel subsidy removal, taxation, foreign borrowing, and monetary policy all deserve rigorous examination. The challenge is to connect them to verifiable evidence, measurable outcomes, and credible alternatives. Ultimately, Kingibe’s intervention highlights both the opportunity and danger facing Nigeria’s opposition. The decisive question is not whether Nigerians are angry. It is whether political leaders can translate that anger into informed debate about who bears economic costs, how government spends public resources, and what realistic alternatives exist. Then there is an even bigger issue. The fact that many Nigerian voters don’t see the contradiction in the economic hardship they are going through, and their willingness to sell their votes to the same political party that has engineered their suffering.
