https://www.myjoyonline.com/mahama-touts.body: President John Dramani Mahama has touted his administration’s $10 billion Big Push Infrastructure Programme, saying the initiative will accelerate infrastructure development, create hundreds of thousands of jobs and complete stalled legacy projects across the country. Speaking at the 13th Financial Times (FT) Africa Summit in London, President Mahama said the programme would be implemented over five years, with $2 billion allocated annually. “We are building infrastructure through the Big Push Programme. It is a $10 billion programme over five years, with $2 billion allocated each year,” he said. He explained that the programme, which began with road infrastructure, would expand to cover schools, hospitals, irrigation schemes, and other projects to support national development. President Mahama also announced plans for a new economy plan involving $10 billion in self-financed investment over four years. He said the funds would go to nine job-rich sectors, including tourism, energy, agriculture, agro-processing, pharmaceuticals, and textiles and garments. He attributed the planned investments to fiscal adjustments his administration is undertaking, including reducing the primary balance target agreed with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) from 1.5 per cent to 0.5 per cent. The President said the adjustment would create an additional fiscal space equivalent to one percentage point, which would be channelled into the targeted sectors to stimulate economic activity and employment. “However, the economy is holding steadily. Our currency is stable, and interest rates are still falling. I think there is a lot we can do for ourselves, even as we call for reform of the global order,” he said. The two-day summit, held under the theme “Mobilising Growth in a New Global Order”, brought together global business leaders, policymakers and heads of state to discuss economic growth and development. Addressing Africa’s debt burden and the global financial system, President Mahama argued that the international economic order placed the continent at a disadvantage, particularly in accessing financing to respond to climate change. “We contribute just four per cent of greenhouse gas emissions, yet we borrow at eight times the cost to deal with the effects of flooding, forest fires and other climate-related challenges,” he said. He further cited the financial resources leaving the continent through debt servicing and illicit financial flows, saying about $80 billion went out annually in interest and debt repayments, while another $90 billion was lost through illicit financial flows, transfer pricing and related practices. The President also expressed concern about declining Overseas Development Assistance (ODA), noting that it fell by 23.5 per cent in 2025 and was expected to decline further in 2026. Despite these challenges, he described Africa as resilient, arguing that the continent continued to endure substantial financial outflows even as development assistance dwindled. “More than $200 billion goes out every year while ODA continues to dwindle,” he said, questioning how Europe would have coped under similar circumstances
https://www.myjoyonline.com/mahama-touts.title_zh: 马哈马宣传价值100亿美元的“大推进”计划，以推动基础设施建设和就业
https://www.myjoyonline.com/mahama-touts.body_zh: 约翰·德拉马尼·马哈马总统赞扬了本届政府规模为100亿美元的“大推进”基础设施计划，称该计划将加快基础设施建设，创造数十万个就业岗位，并完成全国各处停滞的遗留项目。马哈马总统在伦敦举行的第13届《金融时报》非洲峰会上表示，该计划将在5年内实施，每年拨款20亿美元。他说：“我们正通过‘大推进’计划建设基础设施。这是一个为期5年、总额100亿美元的计划，每年拨款20亿美元。”他解释道，该计划将从道路基础设施开始，随后扩展至学校、医院、灌溉设施及其他支持国家发展的项目。马哈马总统还宣布制定一项新经济计划，计划在4年内投入100亿美元的自筹资金。他说，这些资金将投向9个就业密集型部门，包括旅游、能源、农业、农产品加工、制药、纺织和服装业。他表示，拟议中的投资得益于本届政府正在进行的财政调整，包括将与国际货币基金组织（IMF）商定的基本盈余目标从1.5%降至0.5%。总统说，这一调整将额外释放相当于国内生产总值1个百分点的财政空间，并将其投入重点部门，以刺激经济活动和就业。他说：“不过，经济保持稳定。我们的货币保持稳定，利率仍在下降。我认为，即使我们呼吁改革全球秩序，我们仍然可以在很多事情上依靠自己。”这场为期两天的峰会以“新全球秩序下调动增长”为主题，汇聚全球商界领袖、政策制定者和国家元首，讨论经济增长与发展问题。谈及非洲债务负担和全球金融体系时，马哈马总统认为，国际经济秩序使非洲处于不利地位，尤其是在获得应对气候变化所需的融资方面。他说：“我们的温室气体排放量只占4%，然而，为应对洪水、森林火灾和其他气候相关挑战而借款，我们支付的利率却是其他借款的8倍。”他还提到，因偿债和非法资金流动而离开非洲的金融资源，称非洲每年为利息和债务偿还流出约800亿美元，另有900亿美元因非法资金流动、转让定价及相关做法而流失。总统还对海外发展援助（ODA）减少表示关切，指出其2025年下降了23.5%，预计2026年还会进一步下降。尽管面临这些挑战，他仍认为非洲具有韧性，并指出，即使发展援助日益减少，非洲仍在承受大量资金外流。他说：“每年有超过2000亿美元流出，而海外发展援助却持续萎缩。”他质疑，在类似情况下，欧洲将如何应对。

https://dailytrust.com/fg-giz-push-skill.summary: The Federal Government and the German development agency, GIZ, have called for stronger links between skills development and employment opportunities to help Nigerian youths secure jobs and enable businesses to find qualified workers. He said the country’s youthful population could contribute significantly to national development if young people acquired relevant skills and had access to meaningful economic opportunities.
https://dailytrust.com/fg-giz-push-skill.summary_zh: 联邦政府和德国发展机构GIZ呼吁加强技能培养与就业机会之间的衔接，帮助尼日利亚青年获得工作，也让企业能够找到合格劳动力。他表示，如果年轻人掌握相关技能并获得有意义的经济机会，该国庞大的青年人口就能为国家发展作出重大贡献。
https://dailytrust.com/fg-giz-push-skill.body: The Federal Government and the German development agency, GIZ, have called for stronger links between skills development and employment opportunities to help Nigerian youths secure jobs and enable businesses to find qualified workers. They made the call at the Abuja Job and Career Fair 2026, where government officials and development partners stressed the need for improved career guidance, effective job-matching services and closer cooperation with employers. The Minister of Labour and Employment, Dr Muhammad Maigari Dingyadi, said the government was committed to expanding access to employment through public job centres and the National Electronic Labour Exchange (NELEX), a digital platform designed to connect job seekers with employers. He said the country’s youthful population could contribute significantly to national development if young people acquired relevant skills and had access to meaningful economic opportunities. Dingyadi, who declared the fair open, identified skills mismatches, informal employment and difficulties connecting job seekers with employers as challenges requiring coordinated action. He said the fair provided opportunities for recruitment, career counselling, professional networking and skills development, with sessions covering workplace readiness, entrepreneurship, digitalisation and migration pathways. The minister called on employers to look beyond academic qualifications when assessing candidates and consider their abilities, potential and willingness to learn. Mrs Oladoyin Olayi, Organisational Development Coordinator at GIZ Nigeria, said the organisation had worked with the Ministry of Labour and Employment for eight years to strengthen employment services in the country. Representing GIZ Country Director Dr Marcus Wagner, she said the partnership had supported job centres, vocational training, labour migration advice, business digitalisation and entrepreneurship. Olayi disclosed that 11 job centres had been established across five states under the Skills Development for Youth Programme, with four additional centres planned. She said the centres had served more than 65,000 people, over half of them women, by providing career guidance, connecting job seekers with vacancies and referring them to training opportunities. On labour migration, Olayi said more than 31,000 people had received advice on regular migration since 2023, while over 14,000 had been referred to qualification programmes in sectors including hospitality, information and communications technology, construction, renewable energy and fashion. She said more than 3,600 Nigerians returning from abroad had also received support to review their livelihoods. Olamide Adeyeye, Country Head of Programme at Jobberman Nigeria, said physical career fairs remained important despite the increasing use of digital recruitment platforms. He said many young people continued to face barriers to accessing online employment opportunities because of their location, gender, financial circumstances and limited access to digital resources. He said bringing employers and job seekers together physically allowed candidates to demonstrate their capabilities, ask questions and establish professional relationships. Adeyeye disclosed that more than 150,000 people had secured jobs through job fairs, career events and job centres in the past year, describing direct engagement as an important way to connect qualified candidates with employers. He said employment initiatives must focus not only on preparing young people for work but also on ensuring that suitable opportunities were available to them. Adeyeye urged participants to engage actively with recruiters and make the most of the training sessions, while encouraging employers to recognise the potential of candidates beyond their CVs. https://dailytrust.com/fg-giz-push-skill.title_zh: 尼日利亚联邦政府和德国国际合作机构推动技能与就业衔接，应对青年失业问题
https://dailytrust.com/fg-giz-push-skill.body_zh:
尼日利亚联邦政府与德国发展机构GIZ呼吁加强技能培养与就业机会之间的衔接，帮助尼日利亚青年获得就业机会，也让企业找到合格的劳动者。他们在2026年阿布jobs职业博览会上发出这一呼吁。会上，政府官员和发展伙伴强调，需要改善职业指导、提供有效的职位匹配服务，并与雇主加强合作。

劳工与就业部长Muhammad Maigari Dingyadi博士表示，政府致力于通过公共就业中心和国家电子劳动力交易所（NELEX）扩大就业获取渠道。国家电子劳动力交易所是一个连接求职者与雇主的数字平台。他说，如果年轻人掌握相关技能并获得有意义的经济机会，尼日利亚庞大而年轻的劳动力人口就能为国家发展作出重大贡献。Dingyadi宣布博览会开幕，并指出技能错配、非正规就业以及求职者与雇主之间难以建立联系等问题，这些问题需要协调应对。

他说，本次博览会为招聘、职业咨询、专业 networking 和技能发展提供了机会，议程涵盖职场准备、创业、数字化和移民 pathways。部长呼吁雇主在评估求职者时超越学历要求，考虑他们的能力、潜力和学习意愿。

GIZ Nigeria组织发展协调员Oladoyin Olayi女士表示，该机构已与劳工与就业部合作8年，旨在加强尼日利亚的就业服务。她代表GIZ国家主任Marcus Wagner博士表示，双方合作支持了就业中心、职业培训、劳务移民咨询、企业数字化和创业发展。

Olayi透露，“青年技能发展计划”已在5个州建立11个就业中心，并计划再增设4个。她表示，这些中心已通过提供职业指导、连接求职者与职位空缺、将求职者转介至培训机会等方式，为超过65,000人提供服务，其中超过一半是女性。

谈及劳务移民，Olayi表示，自2023年以来，已有超过31,000人获得正规移民方面的咨询，超过14,000人被转介至酒店业、信息通信技术、建筑、可再生能源和时尚等行业资格培训项目。她表示，还有超过3,600名从海外返回的尼日利亚人获得了支持，以重新评估自己的生计方式。

Jobberman Nigeria项目负责人Olamide Adeyeye表示，尽管数字招聘平台的使用日益增加，实体职业博览会仍然十分重要。他说，许多年轻人因所在地、性别、经济状况以及数字资源获取能力有限等因素，仍然难以获得线上就业机会。

Adeyeye说，在实体场所把雇主和求职者聚集在一起，可以让求职者展示能力、提出问题并建立职业关系。他透露，过去一年，超过150,000人通过职业博览会、职业活动和就业中心获得了工作；他将与合格求职者和雇主直接接触视为实现匹配的重要途径。

Adeyeye表示，就业举措不仅要让年轻人为工作做好准备，还要确保他们能够获得合适的就业机会。他敦促参与者积极参与招聘人员互动，充分利用培训课程，同时鼓励雇主不要只依据求职者简历，而应认识到他们的潜力。

Unlock these with Subscription A U.S. judge on Thursday (October 22, 2026) issued President Donald Trump a December 11 deadline to testify under oath in his $10 billion defamation lawsuit against the BBC . Judge Enjolique Lett in Miami gave the order in response to complaints by the British broadcaster that Mr. Trump has refused to sit for a deposition, including canceling a previously agreed date of October 16. If Mr. Trump fails to attend the deposition by then, he risks sanctions, including dismissal of his lawsuit, the court said. Mr. Trump has accused the BBC of deceptively editing its documentary "Trump: A Second Chance" to make it seem as if he was inciting violence when he told supporters to march on the U.S. Capitol on January 6, 2021, after losing the presidential election. The crowd proceeded to storm Congress in an attempt to stop the formal certification of Democrat Joe Biden's victory. While the BBC has apologised for the incident, which prompted the resignation of multiple senior executives, the broadcaster has denied it caused Mr. Trump any real injury and moved for the case to be dismissed. Mr. Trump filed his suit against the BBC in December 2025 and is seeking at least $5 billion on each of two counts. Charles Tobin, a lawyer for the BBC , said in court that Mr. Trump had no real excuse not to testify and that on October 16, he had only been campaigning, "participating in party politics." In a court filing Wednesday (October 21), Mr. Trump's legal team argued that he was not seeking to avoid a deposition but had been constrained by "matters of national importance." The lawyers said Mr. Trump would be able to give a deposition between January 11 and 22. Mr. Trump has made attacks on the media a signature of his two presidential terms, insulting reporters who ask questions he doesn't like and seeking to ban outlets airing critical reports from the White House. Most recently, the administration has plunged into a legal dispute with CNN, MSNOW and Politico over attempts to bar them from the White House. With his approval ratings in the low 30% range and polls showing his Republican Party likely to lose control of the House of Representatives in the November 3 midterm elections, Mr. Trump faces increasing headwinds as he approaches his final years in power. https://punchng.com/umahi-urges-states-t.body: The Minister of Works, David Umahi, has urged state governments to emulate Kano State’s environmental sanitation efforts, commending Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf for initiatives aimed at keeping the state clean. Umahi made the commendation on Tuesday, at an All Progressives Congress caucus meeting, held at the Coronation Hall in Kano, where he praised the state government’s sanitation programmes, including Operation Kano Tsaf-Tsaf. According to a statement issued on Wednesday by the Public Relations Officer of the Refuse Management and Sanitation Board, Abubakar Ahmad, the minister was in Kano ahead of the official commissioning of the Kaduna-Kano Road. “I urge other states to emulate Kano’s efforts, as environmental cleanliness is essential for public health and the well-being of residents,” Umahi said. “Kano State has demonstrated a strong commitment to environmental cleanliness. Other states across Nigeria should learn from its efforts and adopt similar measures to promote a cleaner and healthier environment for their citizens,” the minister was quoted as saying. Kano Pilgrims Board refunds excess 2027 Hajj deposits Yobe youths hail Buni for appointing new Attorney-General Ogun communities demand improved infrastructure from Yayi The statement noted that the commendation reflected the state government’s efforts to promote a clean and sustainable environment through regular sanitation activities and public participation. “The Operation Kano Tsaf-Tsaf programme encourages residents to maintain clean surroundings, dispose of waste properly and support government efforts to protect public health,” the statement added. The board urged the state government to sustain the sanitation initiatives, stressing the importance of cooperation among government agencies, sanitation workers and residents in maintaining a cleaner environment. https://punchng.com/umahi-urges-states-t.body_zh: 工程部长David Umahi敦促各州政府效仿卡诺州在环境卫生方面开展的工作，并赞扬州长Abba Kabir Yusuf为保持该州清洁而采取的各项举措。Umahi于周二在卡诺州王冠厅举行的一次全进步大会党团会议上作出上述赞扬。他在会上称赞了州政府的环境卫生项目，包括“卡诺清洁行动”（Operation Kano Tsaf-Tsaf）。据垃圾管理与卫生委员会公共关系官Abubakar Ahmad周三发布的声明，这位部长在卡诺公路—卡诺公路正式启用仪式抵达卡诺。“我敦促其他州效仿卡诺州的工作，因为环境清洁对公共健康和居民福祉至关重要，”Umahi说。“卡诺州展现了致力于环境清洁的坚定决心。尼日利亚其他州应从卡诺州的工作中汲取经验，采取类似措施，为本国公民营造更清洁、更健康的环境，”部长援引其讲话称。卡诺朝觐委员会退还2027年朝觐多缴押金；约博州青年称赞Buni任命新任总检察长；奥贡州社区要求Yayi改善基础设施。声明指出，此次赞扬体现了州政府通过定期开展卫生活动和鼓励公众参与，推动营造清洁、可持续环境的努力。声明补充称：“‘卡诺清洁行动’鼓励居民保持周边环境清洁、妥善处置废弃物，并支持政府保护公共健康的工作。”该委员会敦促州政府持续推进环境卫生举措，强调政府机构、卫生工作人员和居民之间相互合作对于维护更清洁环境的重要性。Hussaini Ibrahim

https://leadership.ng/senate-moves-to-st.title: Senate Moves To Strengthen NUC Powers, Targets Universities Violating Regulations
https://leadership.ng/senate-moves-to-st.summary: The proposed legislation, sponsored by Senate Leader Opeyemi Bamidele, representing Ekiti Central Senatorial District, seeks to establish a modern legal framework for the establishment, regulation, monitoring and management of universities and other degree-awarding institutions across the country. He said the proposed legislation would strengthen the commission’s ability to enforce regulations, penalise violations, improve quality assurance and promote internationally recognised academic standards.
https://leadership.ng/senate-moves-to-st.summary_zh: 由代表埃基蒂州中部选区的参议院领袖奥佩耶米·巴米德莱提出的法案，旨在为全国高校及其他学位授予机构的设立、监管、监测和管理建立现代法律框架。他说，拟议法案将加强委员会执行规定、惩处违规行为、改进质量保证以及推广国际认可学术标准的能力。
https://leadership.ng/senate-moves-to-st.body: The proposed legislation, sponsored by Senate Leader Opeyemi Bamidele, representing Ekiti Central Senatorial District, seeks to establish a modern legal framework for the establishment, regulation, monitoring and management of universities and other degree-awarding institutions across the country. The bill, titled National Universities Commission Act (Repeal and Re-enactment) Bill, 2026 (SB. 1056), was presented on behalf of Bamidele by Senate Chief Whip Tahir Monguno, representing Borno North Senatorial District. Leading the debate, Monguno said the existing NUC Act had become outdated in view of changes in Nigeria’s higher education landscape, including the proliferation of private universities, technological advancements, internationalisation of education and evolving national development priorities. He said the proposed legislation would strengthen the commission’s ability to enforce regulations, penalise violations, improve quality assurance and promote internationally recognised academic standards. According to Monguno, the bill also seeks to balance regulatory oversight with institutional autonomy, modernise the commission’s governance structure, encourage international partnerships and address funding challenges affecting university education. “These reforms have become necessary to reposition the NUC as a dynamic catalyst for positive change and innovation in the delivery of quality university education,” he said. He urged senators to support the bill, arguing that a stronger regulatory framework would enable the commission to discharge its statutory responsibilities more effectively. Contributing to the debate, Senator Victor Umeh, representing Anambra Central Senatorial District, called for stronger enforcement powers for the NUC, alleging that some private universities had adopted management structures inconsistent with the existing legal framework. Umeh said that while the commission had initially focused on public universities, the growth of private institutions had created additional regulatory challenges. He alleged that some private universities registered as limited liability companies or companies limited by guarantee had introduced management arrangements involving managing directors and executive directors instead of adhering to governance structures prescribed by law. “The NUC, when it was established, was managing public universities, and at some point, private universities came into being. The private universities that we have in Nigeria today are being run by people who do not keep to the standards as prescribed by the National Universities Commission,” he said. According to Umeh, the commission sometimes struggled to enforce compliance when institutions ignored its directives or challenged its authority. He said the proposed legislation presented an opportunity to strengthen the NUC’s powers and ensure that universities complied with regulations governing their establishment and administration. “When you are told that you are not doing the right thing, that the way and the structure of governance in that private university is not in accordance with the law, you go to court and continue to vacillate,” he said. Umeh recalled that the commission had previously exercised considerable influence over university management by ensuring that institutions complied with its directives. He argued that stronger enforcement provisions were necessary to prevent institutions from disregarding regulatory orders. “Any university that is operating anywhere in Nigeria must align itself with the governance directives of the National Universities Commission. Otherwise, such universities should be proscribed,” he said. He added that the primary objective should be to protect academic standards and ensure that private universities operated within the law. During the debate, senators also discussed allegations of irregular management practices at Tansian University in Anambra State. Umeh cited the institution as an example of what he described as concerns over governance structures and compliance with NUC directives. He alleged that the university’s management arrangements allowed a managing director to exercise powers over appointments and administrative decisions in ways he considered inconsistent with established university governance practices. The allegations were raised during the Senate debate as lawmakers considered whether the proposed legislation would provide the commission with more effective tools to enforce compliance. The discussion also prompted calls for clearer procedures to address institutions that fail to comply with regulatory directives. The Senate President indicated that stronger legislation could help the National Assembly support the commission’s oversight responsibilities and address persistent cases of non-compliance. He also raised the possibility of recommending the proscription of institutions that failed to meet the required standards, subject to the appropriate legal and executive procedures. Beyond enforcement, the proposed legislation seeks to update the NUC’s regulatory framework to reflect developments in higher education. The bill aims to strengthen programme accreditation, update minimum academic standards, improve monitoring mechanisms and promote research and innovation. It also proposes changes to the composition and functions of the commission’s governing board to improve operational efficiency and accountability. Other objectives include providing a clearer framework for international partnerships, foreign investment in university education and the attraction of international faculty and students. The proposed reforms are also intended to encourage greater institutional autonomy while maintaining effective regulatory oversight. Monguno said the changes would help position Nigeria’s university system to respond to emerging challenges and compete more effectively internationally. Following the debate, the Senate passed the bill for second reading through a voice vote. The legislation was subsequently referred to the Senate Committee on Tertiary Institutions and TETFund for further legislative consideration, with the committee directed to report back to the Senate within four weeks. https://leadership.ng/senate-moves-to-st.title_zh: 参议院推动加强国家大学委员会权力，针对违反规定的高校采取行动
https://leadership.ng/senate-moves-to-st.body_zh:
由代表埃基蒂州中部选区的参议院领袖奥佩米·巴米德莱提出的法案，拟为全国大学及其他学位授予机构的设立、监管、监督和管理建立现代法律框架。该法案名为《2026年国家大学委员会法（废止并重新制定）法案》（SB. 1056），由代表博尔诺州北部选区的参议院首席党鞭 Tahir Monguno 代表巴米德莱提交。主持辩论时，Monguno表示，鉴于尼日利亚高等教育格局发生变化，包括私立大学激增、技术进步、教育国际化以及国家发展重点不断演变，现行《国家大学委员会法》已经过时。他说，拟议立法将增强委员会执行规定、惩处违规行为、改善质量保证以及推广国际认可学术标准的能力。

据Monguno介绍，该法案还寻求在监管与机构自主权之间取得平衡，推进委员会治理结构现代化，鼓励国际合作，并解决影响大学教育的资金难题。他说：“为了将国家大学委员会重新定位为提供优质大学教育和推动积极变革与创新的充满活力的催化剂，这些改革已成为必要。”他敦促参议员支持该法案，认为更有力的监管框架将使委员会更有效地履行法定职责。

代表阿南布拉州中部选区的参议员 Victor Umeh 参与辩论时，呼吁赋予国家大学委员会更强的执法权，并指称一些私立大学采用了与现行法律框架不一致的管理结构。Umeh表示，尽管委员会最初主要关注公立大学，但私立机构的发展带来了更多监管挑战。他指称，一些以有限责任公司或担保有限公司形式注册的私立大学引入了由常务董事和执行董事参与的管理安排，而没有遵循法律规定的治理结构。

他说：“国家大学委员会成立之初负责管理公立大学，后来私立大学也开始出现。如今尼日利亚的私立大学由一些人经营，他们没有遵守国家大学委员会规定的标准。”据Umeh介绍，当一些机构无视委员会指示或对其权威提出质疑时，委员会有时难以确保其遵守规定。他说，拟议立法为加强国家大学委员会的权力，并确保大学遵守有关设立和管理的规定提供了机会。

他说：“当你被告知没有正确履行职责，告知那所私立大学的治理方式和结构不符合法律时，你却仍然起诉并继续摇摆不定。”Umeh回顾称，委员会过去曾通过确保各机构遵守其指示，对大学管理施加了相当大的影响。他认为，必须设置更有力的执法条款，以防止机构无视监管命令。

他说：“任何在尼日利亚境内运营的大学都必须遵守国家大学委员会的治理指令，否则就应禁止其办学。”他还补充说，首要目标应是保护学术标准，确保私立大学依法运营。

辩论期间，参议员还讨论了关于阿南布拉州 Tansian University 管理做法不规范的指控。Umeh将该院校列为一个例子，用以说明他所称的治理结构问题以及不遵守国家大学委员会指示的问题。他指称，该大学的管理安排允许常务董事对任命和行政决定行使权力，而他认为这种做法与既定大学治理惯例不符。

这些指控是在参议院辩论期间提出的，当时议员正在审议拟议立法能否为委员会提供更有效的工具以执行合规要求。相关讨论还促使各方呼吁建立更明确的程序，以处理不遵守监管指示的机构。参议院议长表示，更强有力的立法能够帮助国民议会支持委员会的监督职责，并解决长期存在的不合规问题。他还提出，可以建议禁止未能达到规定标准的机构，但须遵守适当的法律和行政程序。

除执法外，拟议立法还旨在更新国家大学委员会的监管框架，使其反映高等教育领域的发展。该法案力求加强专业认证、更新最低学术标准、改善监督机制，并促进研究与创新。法案还提议调整委员会理事会的组成和职能，以提高运营效率和问责水平。其他目标包括为国际合作、大学教育领域的外国投资以及吸引国际教师和学生建立更清晰的框架。

拟议改革还旨在鼓励更大程度的机构自主权，同时保持有效的监管监督。Monguno表示，这些变化将帮助尼日利亚大学体系做好应对新挑战的准备，并在国际市场上具备更强的竞争力。辩论结束后，参议院以口头表决方式通过该法案，进入二读程序。随后，该法案被移交参议院高等教育机构及 TETFund 委员会作进一步立法审议，并指示该委员会在4周内向参议院提交报告。

https://leadership.ng/senate-orders-prob.summary_zh: 他认为，涉嫌无视既定监管程序的行为可能破坏大学治理、削弱学术标准，并损害尼日利亚毕业生的国际声誉。参议院经过审议后，批准了一项动议，要求调查Tansian University的运营和管理，并指示相关委员会在两周内提交报告。
https://leadership.ng/senate-orders-prob.body: The directive followed concerns raised by Senator Victor Umeh, representing Anambra Central Senatorial District, during deliberations on a bill seeking to repeal and re-enact the National Universities Commission Act. Umeh called for an immediate investigation into the university’s governance structure, particularly allegations concerning the appointment and removal of university officials and the exercise of management powers. He argued that alleged disregard for established regulatory procedures could undermine university governance, weaken academic standards and damage the international reputation of Nigerian graduates. Responding to the concerns, Senate President Godswill Akpabio emphasised the need to strengthen the regulatory authority of the NUC to ensure that public and private universities operated within the confines of the law. Akpabio noted that the National Assembly had an oversight responsibility to support the commission in enforcing standards across the university system. He added that where an institution was found to have violated applicable laws, the National Assembly could recommend appropriate action to the President, including its proscription, subject to the relevant legal procedures. Following the deliberations, the Senate approved a motion for an investigation into Tansian University’s operations and management and directed the relevant committee to report back within two weeks. Umeh had expressed concern that some private universities allegedly operated management structures inconsistent with established regulatory requirements. He warned that allowing university operators to disregard the NUC’s directives could weaken accountability and undermine confidence in the country’s higher education system. The senator called on the Senate to take action against any institution found to be operating outside the approved regulatory framework, stressing that enforcement should not wait for the proposed amendment to the NUC Act to become law. He also warned that failure to address alleged irregularities could have wider implications for the credibility of Nigerian university qualifications. The investigation is expected to establish whether Tansian University’s governance arrangements comply with applicable regulations and determine whether further action is warranted. The allegations against the institution have yet to be established by the investigation. The probe comes as the Senate considers a bill seeking to repeal and re-enact the National Universities Commission Act to strengthen the commission’s regulatory powers and improve oversight of university education in Nigeria. The bill, sponsored by Senate Leader Opeyemi Bamidele and presented by Senate Chief Whip Tahir Monguno, seeks to establish an updated legal framework for the regulation, monitoring and management of universities and other degree-awarding institutions. The proposed legislation aims to strengthen enforcement mechanisms, update minimum academic standards, improve accreditation processes and ensure that Nigerian universities align with international best practices. It also seeks to provide appropriate sanctions for regulatory violations and reinforce the NUC’s position as the apex regulatory authority for academic programme accreditation. During the debate, lawmakers argued that the existing legal framework needed to be updated to address changes in the university sector, particularly the expansion of private institutions and emerging challenges in university administration. They maintained that stronger regulation was necessary to improve quality assurance, promote research and innovation, and ensure that Nigerian universities remained competitive internationally. The Senate subsequently referred the investigation into Tansian University to the relevant committee for further consideration, with a directive to report back within two weeks. The committee is expected to examine the institution’s governance arrangements and determine whether they comply with the regulatory guidelines governing university administration in Nigeria. The development signals the Senate’s intention to strengthen oversight of university management as lawmakers consider broader reforms to the legal framework governing higher education. https://leadership.ng/senate-orders-prob.title_zh: 参议院下令调查坦桑大学涉嫌违反监管规定一事
https://leadership.ng/senate-orders-prob.body_zh: 该指令源于参议员维克托·乌梅赫在审议一项寻求废除并重新制定《国家 Universities Commission Act》的法案时提出的关切。乌梅赫代表阿南布拉中部选区，他呼吁立即调查该大学的治理结构，重点调查有关大学官员任免和管理权力行使的指控。他认为，无视既定监管程序的行为可能削弱大学治理、降低学术标准，并损害尼日利亚毕业生的国际声誉。针对这些关切，参议院议长戈德斯威尔·阿克帕比奥强调，需要加强国家 Universities Commission（NUC）的监管权，确保公立和私立大学依法运营。阿克帕比奥指出，国民议会负有监督责任，应支持该委员会在整个大学体系中执行标准。他补充说，如果发现某机构违反适用法律，国民议会可建议总统采取适当行动，包括依法关闭该机构。经过审议，参议院批准了一项动议，对 Tansian University 的运营和管理展开调查，并指示相关委员会在两周内提交报告。乌梅赫此前表示担忧，一些私立大学据称采用与既定监管要求不一致的管理结构。他警告说，如果允许大学运营方无视 NUC 的指令，可能削弱问责制并损害外界对尼日利亚高等教育体系的信心。乌梅赫呼吁参议院对任何被发现脱离既定监管框架运营的机构采取行动，并强调执法不应等待拟议中的 NUC Act 修正案生效。他还警告称，未能处理涉嫌违规行为，可能对尼日利亚大学学历的可信度带来更广泛影响。此次调查预计将确定 Tansian University 的治理安排是否符合适用法规，并判断是否有必要采取进一步行动。针对该机构的指控尚未通过调查得到证实。调查之际，参议院正在审议一项寻求废除并重新制定《国家 Universities Commission Act》的法案，以加强该委员会的监管权力并加强对尼日利亚大学教育的监督。该法案由参议院领袖奥佩耶米·巴米德莱提出，并由参议院首席党鞭塔希尔·蒙努诺提交，旨在为大学及其他学位授予机构的监管、监测和管理建立更新后的法律框架。拟议立法旨在加强执法机制、更新最低学术标准、改善认证流程，并确保尼日利亚大学符合国际最佳实践。法案还 seeks 对监管违规行为规定适当制裁，并强化 NUC 作为学术项目认证最高监管机构的地位。辩论期间，议员们认为，现有法律框架需要更新，以应对大学领域的变化，尤其是私立机构的扩张以及大学管理中 emerging 的挑战。他们坚持认为，加强监管对于改善质量保障、促进研究与创新，以及确保尼日利亚大学保持国际竞争力都是必要的。参议院随后将对 Tansian University 的调查移交相关委员会进一步审议，并指示其在两周内提交报告。预计该委员会将审查该机构的治理安排，确定其是否符合尼日利亚大学管理的监管指引。这一进展表明，参议院有意加强对大学管理的监督，同时议员们正在考虑对高等教育法律框架进行更广泛的改革。拟议中的 NUC 修正案已通过二读，目前正在进行进一步立法审议。我们掌握最新动态。获取实时报道、独家爆料和独家角度，直接发送到您的手机。不要满足于过时新闻。加入 LEADERSHIP NEWS WhatsApp 频道，随时获取全天候更新 → 加入我们的 WhatsApp 频道 --> --> Samson Elijah 是一名就职于 Leadership Newspaper 的记者，专门从事政治报道和公共事务分析。他以深入的事实分析而闻名，这些分析超越表面报道，使他成为该领域值得信赖且权威的声音

https://www.myjoyonline.com/trump-ordere.summary_zh: 美国一名法官已命令总统唐纳德·特朗普于12月11日前在其针对英国广播公司的诽谤诉讼中宣誓回答问题。根据美国法律，宣誓取证是当事人在法庭外宣誓后就提问作出的陈述，该陈述会被记录，供后续诉讼程序使用。特朗普在佛罗里达州提起的诉讼指控英国广播公司“故意、恶意且欺骗性地篡改”了他于2021年1月6日在国会大厦外发表的讲话。
https://www.myjoyonline.com/trump-ordere.body: A US judge has ordered President Donald Trump to answer questions under oath in his defamation lawsuit against the BBC by 11 December. Trump is suing the BBC over an episode of Panorama that edited together two different sections of a speech he gave before the riot at the US Capitol in 2021. Charles Tobin, a lawyer representing the BBC, said in court that "we still haven't been able to depose the plaintiff" with two months left in the discovery period, during which both sides are legally required to exchange information with each other on their case. Trump cancelled a previous deposition on 16 October, citing "matters of national importance" while he was campaigning in Georgia. In US law, a deposition is an out-of-court statement made under oath in response to questions, which is recorded for use in later proceedings. The judge in the case, US Magistrate Judge Enjoliqué Lett, said that Trump must sit for the deposition by 11 December, unless the discovery period is extended. Last week, attorneys asked that Lett compel Trump to face deposition after the last scheduled meeting did not take place. On that day, Trump attended a midterms campaign rally in Dalton, Georgia and a fundraiser at his property in Mar-a-Lago in Florida. Trump's lawsuit - filed in Florida - accuses the BBC of "intentionally, maliciously, and deceptively doctoring" the speech he gave outside the Capitol on 6 January 2021. The BBC apologised for the error and said that the broadcast gave "the mistaken impression that President Trump made a direct call for violent action". The broadcaster has since asked that the court dismiss the lawsuit, arguing that the programme does not meet the legal criteria for defamation and was not available in the US. In July, Trump's lawyers conceded that they had no evidence that the documentary was available in the US on the BBC's BritBox subscription service - as they originally claimed - or on the BBC's website, BBC select or through US broadcasters. Trump ultimately agreed to drop the lawsuit against BBC Studios, its commercial arm, after the BBC argued that it had "no role in creating or producing the documentary". Typically, depositions take place in a lawyer's office - rather than a courtroom - without a judge physically present. Depositions, however, carry legal weight and take place under oath. They are recorded verbatim by a court reporter, and the transcripts can later be used as evidence during trials. In defamation cases, lawyers for both sides are normally present for depositions
https://www.myjoyonline.com/trump-ordere.title_zh: 特朗普须在BBC诉讼案中宣誓回答问题
https://www.myjoyonline.com/trump-ordere.body_zh: 美国法官已命令总统唐纳德·特朗普在12月11日前，就他针对BBC提起的诽谤诉讼宣誓回答问题。特朗普起诉BBC，原因是《全景》节目的一期内容将他在2021年美国国会大厦发生骚乱前发表的一次演讲中两个不同的片段剪辑到了一起。代表BBC的律师查尔斯·托宾在法庭上表示，在证据开示期还剩两个月的情况下，“我们仍未能够让原告接受宣誓取证”，而在此期间，双方依法都必须交换与各自案件有关的信息。特朗普此前取消了10月16日的一次宣誓取证，理由是他正在佐治亚州竞选，声称存在“具有全国重要性的事务”。在美国法律中，宣誓取证是指在法庭外宣誓后回答问题所作的陈述，并会被记录下来，供后续诉讼程序使用。本案法官、美国治安法官恩乔利凯·莱特表示，除非证据开示期获准延长，否则特朗普必须在12月11日前接受宣誓取证。上周，律师请求莱特强迫特朗普接受宣誓取证，因为原定进行的最后一次会面未能举行。当天，特朗普出席了佐治亚州多尔顿市举行的中期选举竞选集会，以及佛罗里达州海湖庄园内的一场筹款活动。特朗普在佛罗里达州提起的诉讼指控BBC“故意、恶意且欺骗性地篡改”了他于2021年1月6日在国会大厦外发表的演讲。BBC为这一错误道歉，并称该节目“使人误以为特朗普总统直接呼吁采取暴力行动”。此后，该媒体请求法院驳回诉讼，理由是该节目不符合诽谤罪的法律标准，而且在美国无法收看。7月，特朗普的律师承认，他们没有证据证明该纪录片可通过BBC的BritBox订阅服务——正如他们最初所称——或通过BBC网站、BBC Select或美国各广播机构在美国收看。最终，在BBC主张其“在制作或创作该纪录片方面没有任何作用”后，特朗普同意放弃对BBC商业部门BBC Studios提起的诉讼。宣誓取证通常在律师事务所而非法庭内进行，法官不会亲自到场。不过，宣誓取证具有法律效力，并以宣誓方式进行。法庭记录员会逐字录制整个过程，记录文本之后可在审判中作为证据。在诽谤案件中，双方律师通常都会出席宣誓取证……

https://www.chicagotribune.com/2026/10/2.summary: WASHINGTON — The U.S. Treasury Department proposed a rule Thursday to crack down on American high-tech investments such as supercomputing and artificial intelligence in China, Russia, North Korea and other “countries of concern.’’ The U.S. government has been working for years to deny China and other adversaries investments that could help them boost their military power.
https://www.chicagotribune.com/2026/10/2.summary_zh: 华盛顿——美国财政部周四提出一项规则，旨在打击美国对中国、俄罗斯、朝鲜及其他“受关注国家”的高科技投资，例如超级计算和人工智能投资。多年来，美国政府一直设法阻止中国及其他对手获得能够增强其军事力量的投资。
https://www.chicagotribune.com/2026/10/2.body: WASHINGTON — The U.S. Treasury Department proposed a rule Thursday to crack down on American high-tech investments such as supercomputing and artificial intelligence in China, Russia, North Korea and other “countries of concern.’’ The U.S. government has been working for years to deny China and other adversaries investments that could help them boost their military power. That program began in 2023 when then-President Joe Biden signed an executive order putting restrictions on outbound U.S. investments in sectors such as semiconductors, quantum computing and artificial intelligence going into China. Treasury later established the Outbound Investment Security Program. In December 2025, Congress passed a law that codified and expanded the program to target more technologies and more foreign countries, including Cuba, Iran, North Korea and Russia. The inclusion of Russia in the proposed rule has come days after President Donald Trump waived sanctions on Russia following a diesel deal with President Vladimir Putin. The rule announced Thursday would expand the restrictions to cover investments in hypersonic systems (capable of traveling at five times the speed of sound), supercomputing, biotechnology and artificial intelligence, though Treasury used Trump’s favored term for AI, “superintelligence” or SI. The proposed rule “sends an important signal to markets that Washington is tracking where U.S. capital is flowing and what capabilities it is helping build,” said Craig Singleton, a senior fellow at the think tank Foundation for Defense of Democracies. The screening of outbound investments “recognizes that capital can accelerate military-relevant capabilities just as surely as technology transfer can,” Singleton said. Treasury’s rule to implement the 2025 law — the Comprehensive Outbound Investment National Security Act — would only apply to investments that exceed $50,000 and would exclude many financial investments, including stock purchases. Treasury will hear public comments on the proposal before issuing a final rule. “It’s just the first step in a fairly long process to get to changes which presumably will be more enforcement-minded, to put more teeth behind the outbound investment program,” said former U.S. trade official Ryan Majerus, now a partner at King & Spalding law firm. Since Trump’s first term, the United States and China — the world’s two biggest economies — have been locked in an economic and tech rivalry. They’ve restricted the export of sensitive technology and critical products (China’s rare earth minerals, America’s advanced computer chips) to each other and slapped tariffs on each other’s products. Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping agreed last year to ease tensions while they engaged in talks, a temporary truce they last month extended into January. But the sparring continues. https://www.chicagotribune.com/2026/10/2.title_zh: 美国财政部提议制定规则，打击对中国及其他“受关注国家”的高科技投资
https://www.chicagotribune.com/2026/10/2.body_zh: 华盛顿——美国财政部周四提议制定一项规则，严厉限制美国对中国、俄罗斯、朝鲜及其他“受关注国家”的高科技投资，例如超级计算和人工智能。美国政府多年来一直致力于阻止中国及其他对手获得可能提升其军事力量的投资。该计划始于2023年，时任总统乔·拜登签署行政命令，限制美国对华 semiconductors、量子计算和人工智能等领域的对外投资。此后，财政部设立了对外投资安全计划。2025年12月，国会通过一项法律，将该计划成文化并予以扩大，将更多技术和更多外国国家列为目标，包括古巴、伊朗、朝鲜和俄罗斯。就在拟议规则发布前几天，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普在与俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京达成柴油交易后，豁免了对俄罗斯的制裁。周四公布的规则将扩大限制范围，涵盖对高超音速系统（飞行速度可达音速5倍）、超级计算、生物技术和人工智能的投资，不过财政部采用了特朗普偏好的人工智能称谓“超级智能”或SI。民主国防基金会高级研究员克雷格·辛格顿表示，拟议规则“向市场发出一个重要信号，表明华盛顿正在追踪美国资本流向何处，以及这些资本正在帮助构建什么能力”。辛格顿说，对对外投资进行审查，“承认资本与技术转让一样，能够加速与军事相关的能力发展”。财政部为落实2025年法律——《综合对外投资国家安全法》——而制定的规则，仅适用于金额超过50,000美元的投资，并将排除许多金融投资，包括购买股票。财政部将在发布最终规则前听取公众对该提案的意见。现任King & Spalding律师事务所合伙人、美国前贸易官员瑞安·马杰鲁斯说：“这只是推动对外投资计划发生改变的一个初步步骤，而这一过程相当漫长；最终出台的规定大概会更加注重执法，使该计划拥有更强的约束力。”自特朗普首个任期开始以来，世界两大经济体美国和中国一直陷于经济与科技竞争。双方相互限制敏感技术和关键产品的出口，其中包括稀土矿产（中国）和先进计算机芯片（美国），并对彼此产品加征关税。去年，特朗普和中国国家主席习近平同意在会谈期间缓和紧张局势，双方达成的临时休战上月又延长至1月。但双方仍不断交锋。今年7月，财政部对一家美国公司处以200,000美元罚款，原因是该公司未向财政部报告其一家子公司对一家中国人工智能和机器人公司进行的92,500美元投资

https://punchng.com/yobe-assembly-approv.body: The Yobe State House of Assembly has approved the establishment of a state police service as part of its consideration of proposed amendments to the 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria. The approval followed deliberations by lawmakers on proposed constitutional amendment bills transmitted by the National Assembly to state Houses of Assembly for consideration and voting. The resolution was reached on Thursday, according to the proceedings of the House. The Speaker, Rt. Hon. Chiroma Buba Mashio, said the bills were forwarded to state legislatures to consider and vote on the proposed alterations in line with constitutional requirements. Mashio said the House’s position on state police was aimed at providing a constitutional framework that would allow states to establish their own police services alongside the existing Nigeria Police Force. He said, “The proposed establishment of state police is aimed at providing a constitutional framework that will enable states to maintain their own police services alongside the existing Nigeria Police Force.” The Speaker added that the proposal was part of ongoing national discussions on security sector reform aimed at strengthening Nigeria’s capacity to address emerging security challenges. “The establishment of state police is a key component of ongoing national discussions on security sector reform aimed at strengthening the country’s capacity to address emerging security challenges,” he said. https://leadership.ng/state-police-gombe.body: The bill, comprising 26 clauses, was transmitted to the state assembly by the National Assembly on October 6, 2026, for concurrence in line with Section 9(2) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended. The proposed legislation seeks to amend the Constitution to establish a legal framework for a State Police Service, distinct from the Nigeria Police Force and under federal control. LEADERSHIP reports that the assembly passed the bill on Thursday after considering the report of its Ad-hoc Committee on the Review of the 1999 Constitution. Upon receipt of the bill, the House constituted a seven-member ad hoc committee, chaired by the Deputy Speaker, Hon. Sadam Bello Sale, to examine the proposed amendments. Presenting the committee’s report, Sale said members had consulted relevant stakeholders as part of their review of the bill. He added that the report received the support of a two-thirds majority of members, in accordance with Order 17, Rule 3 of the Gombe State House of Assembly Standing Orders, 2020. During Thursday’s plenary, lawmakers considered the report at the Committee of the Whole. They adopted recommendations to amend various provisions of the Constitution, including those relating to the establishment and operation of state police services separate from the federal police. The passage places Gombe among the states whose legislatures have endorsed the proposed constitutional changes to establish state police as part of efforts to address Nigeria’s security challenges. Commenting on the bill, the Speaker of the House, Abubakar Muhammad Luggerewo, said members unanimously supported the proposed legal framework for establishing state police, noting that it would strengthen security in the country. He commended the lawmakers for their commitment and resilience. Barr. Hauwa Abdullahi and Barr. Babadidi J. Mele served as secretaries to the committee. We’ve got the edge. https://www.myjoyonline.com/ministry-of-.summary: The Ministry of Education is creating direct reporting channels, including a hotline, to allow students, parents, teachers and community members to report sexual abuse in schools without having to go through head teachers or other local authorities who may be implicated. He cited the Obuasi SHTS case as an example of how complaints could remain unresolved when people who become aware of alleged abuse cannot secure an effective response through existing channels.
https://www.myjoyonline.com/ministry-of-.summary_zh: 教育部正在建立包括热线在内的直接报告渠道，让学生、家长、教师和社区成员无需经过校长或其他可能涉案的当地 authorities，即可举报学校内的性虐待。他以Obuasi SHTS案件为例，说明当知悉涉嫌虐待行为的人无法通过现有渠道获得有效回应时，相关投诉可能长期得不到解决。
https://www.myjoyonline.com/ministry-of-.body: The Ministry of Education is creating direct reporting channels, including a hotline, to allow students, parents, teachers and community members to report sexual abuse in schools without having to go through head teachers or other local authorities who may be implicated. Deputy Education Minister Dr Clement Apaak disclosed this on JoyNews’ News Night on Thursday, October 22, 2026, saying the allegations involving the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS) had exposed weaknesses in the existing reporting structure. “In the wake of this issue, we became aware that there was a challenge within the reporting structure as far as GES is concerned,” he said. Dr Apaak said the proposed channels would provide an alternative route for complaints to reach the Ministry of Education, enabling authorities to respond to allegations more promptly. “We believe that if we were to provide a bypass that would allow victims, parents of victims, teaching and non-teaching staff in the schools where some of these despicable occurrences take place, or even community members and leaders, it will make it easier for such complaints to get to the ministry so that we can act tenaciously,” he said. Dr Apaak stressed that a hotline was one of several reporting options under consideration, acknowledging that students are generally not permitted to carry mobile phones in school. “The concept of the hotline is one among many other options,” he said. He cited the Obuasi SHTS case as an example of how complaints could remain unresolved when people who become aware of alleged abuse cannot secure an effective response through existing channels. “From the documentary, we saw pieces of evidence to suggest that other teachers, a housemistress, and even parents had become aware, and because the structure did not allow them to get the needed response in terms of action, this dragged on,” he said. The Deputy Minister said the delay may have created opportunities for the alleged abuse to continue and affect other students. “That may have then given an opportunity to the accused individual to even engage in this conduct and perpetrate this crime against other female students,” he said. The proposed reporting channels follow allegations of sexual abuse involving the suspended headmaster of Obuasi SHTS, Zakaria Abdulai. An investigative documentary by journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni examined allegations involving multiple students and raised questions about whether concerns brought to the attention of some school authorities and parents received an adequate response. The case has prompted calls for stronger safeguarding measures and more effective systems for reporting suspected abuse in schools. The proposed channels are intended to allow complaints to reach education authorities directly, particularly where school-level officials may be implicated or fail to act. Dr Apaak did not provide a timeline for the introduction of the new reporting options
https://www.myjoyonline.com/ministry-of-.title_zh: 奥布阿西SHTS案件发生后，教育部设立性侵投诉直接报告渠道
https://www.myjoyonline.com/ministry-of-.body_zh: 教育部正在建立直接举报渠道，包括设立热线电话，让学生、家长、教师和社区成员可以直接举报校园性侵，而无需经过可能涉案的校长或其他地方 authorities。2026年10月22日，教育部副部长克莱门特·阿帕克博士在 JoyNews 的《夜间新闻》节目中透露了此事。他说，涉及奥布亚西高级技术学校（SHTS）校长的指控暴露了现有举报机制的薄弱之处。他说：“在这一事件发生后，我们意识到，就GES而言，举报机制存在一个问题。”阿帕克博士表示，拟议中的渠道将为投诉直接传达至教育部提供另一条途径，使有关部门能够更迅速地回应指控。他说：“我们认为，如果设置一条旁路举报渠道，让受害者、受害者的家长、发生这些卑劣事件的学校的教职员工，甚至社区成员和社区领袖，都能更方便地向教育部反映投诉，我们就可以坚决采取行动。”阿帕克博士强调，热线电话只是目前正在考虑的多种举报方式之一，并承认学校通常不允许学生携带手机。他说：“热线电话只是众多选项中的一个。”他以奥布亚西SHTS案件为例，说明当知情者无法通过现有渠道获得有效回应时，投诉可能长期得不到解决。他说：“从纪录片中，我们看到了一些证据，表明其他教师、一名宿舍女管理员，甚至一些家长早已知情，但由于现有机制无法让他们获得所需的行动回应，这件事便一直拖着。”副部长表示，拖延可能为涉嫌的虐待行为继续发生并影响其他学生创造了机会。他说：“这样一来，可能就给了被指控者机会，让他们继续实施这种行为，对其他女学生犯下罪行。”拟议中的直接举报渠道是在奥布亚西SHTS被停职校长扎卡里亚·阿卜杜拉伊涉嫌性侵学生的指控之后提出的。记者曼纳塞·阿祖尔·阿武尼制作的一部调查纪录片审查了涉及多名学生的指控，并质疑向部分学校管理人员和家长反映的情况是否得到了充分回应。此案引发了加强保护措施和完善校园疑似虐待行为举报制度的呼声。拟议中的举报渠道旨在让投诉直接传达给教育主管部门，尤其是在学校层面官员可能涉案或未能采取行动的情况下。阿帕克博士没有就推出这些新举报方式的时间表作出说明

The command disclosed this in a statement shared on its Facebook page on Thursday, saying the vehicle was intercepted at about 8 pm on October 20 in Maitama, Abuja. The statement was signed by the command’s Public Relations Officer, Josephine Adeh. According to the police, preliminary investigations revealed that the number plate bore the registration number 10B218 FG, but the documents presented for its registration were forged. The police said the suspect claimed to be the legitimate holder of the number plate, but further investigations allegedly uncovered that he was impersonating a permanent secretary attached to the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation. https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/sena.body: Layer 1 — Bill seeks to boost science education, skilled manpower Akpabio stresses sustainable funding, research and infrastructure ABUJA — The Senate has held a public hearing on a bill seeking to establish the Federal University of Science and Technology, Korokorosei, in Bayelsa State, as part of efforts to expand science education, strengthen research and address Nigeria’s skilled manpower needs. The hearing was organised on Thursday by the Senate Committee on Tertiary Institutions and TETFund, chaired by Senator Muntari Dandutse (APC, Katsina South). The proposed university is expected to expand access to science and technology education, promote indigenous research and innovation, and train skilled professionals to support industrialisation and technological advancement. Declaring the hearing open, Senate President Godswill Akpabio said the proposed institution should be assessed not only on the merits of its establishment but also on the availability of sustainable funding, adequate facilities and effective administration. Akpabio, who was represented by the Deputy Minority Whip, Senator Ibrahim Mustapha, said Nigeria needed institutions capable of translating research into industrial production, reducing dependence on imported technologies and equipping young people with skills to compete globally. He described human potential as the Niger Delta’s greatest resource, saying the proposed university could help address environmental degradation and develop solutions to challenges facing the region’s riverine communities. Akpabio identified cleaner energy, environmental protection, agriculture and fisheries as areas where the institution could make significant contributions through research and innovation. He said the university should produce graduates whose knowledge and innovations would support national development. The Senate president cautioned, however, that expanding the number of universities should not be the sole objective of higher education policy, stressing that access must be matched by academic excellence, adequate funding and long-term sustainability. He urged stakeholders to examine the bill critically and make recommendations that would assist the National Assembly in reaching an informed decision in the national interest. Earlier, Dandutse said the public hearing provided an inclusive platform for stakeholders to contribute to the proposed legislation. He said the committee would scrutinise the proposed university’s governance structure, funding arrangements, academic focus, staffing requirements, infrastructure and compliance with existing laws governing tertiary education. The committee chairman added that particular attention would be paid to the institution’s long-term viability to ensure that, if approved, it delivered meaningful benefits to students and the country. The bill’s sponsor, Senator Benson Konbowei (Bayelsa Central), said the proposed university would help address shortages of skilled manpower, particularly in science, technology and other specialised fields. Konbowei argued that Nigeria needed to train more professionals locally rather than rely on foreign sources to meet critical technological and industrial manpower requirements. He said establishing the institution in the Niger Delta would give young people greater opportunities to study science-related courses and acquire skills relevant to their communities and the wider country. The lawmaker thanked the Senate leadership and committee members for considering the proposal, describing it as an opportunity to strengthen science and technology education in the region. Also speaking, Mr Timidi Wariowei, technical adviser to Bayelsa State Governor Douye Diri, said Korokorosei, in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area, had existing infrastructure that could support the proposed university. He listed a secondary school with several buildings, a health facility, hotels and a landing jetty among the facilities available in the riverine community. Wariowei added that road construction towards the community was ongoing, expressing optimism that improved accessibility would support the development of the proposed institution. He also said the state government had established technical colleges across its eight local government areas to develop practical skills in science and technology. According to him, the proposed university could provide graduates of those colleges with opportunities for further education, advanced training and specialised knowledge. https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/sena.title_zh: 尼日利亚参议院就拟议中的巴耶尔萨科技大学举行听证会
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/sena.body_zh: 第一层——参议院法案寻求促进科学教育和 skilled manpower；阿卡比奥强调可持续资金、研究与基础设施。阿布贾——参议院举行公开听证会，审议一项拟在巴耶尔萨州设立科罗科罗塞联邦科技大学 的法案，以扩大科学教育、加强研究并应对尼日利亚的技术人才需求。听证会于周四举行，由参议院高等教育机构及TETFund委员会组织，委员会主席为卡塔萨州南区参议员蒙塔里·丹杜塞（全体进步大会党）。拟议大学有望扩大科学和技术教育的入学渠道，推动本土研究与创新，并培养技术专业人才，以支持工业化和技术进步。参议院议长戈德斯威尔·阿卡比奥宣布听证会开幕时表示，对拟议机构的评估不应只看设立该机构的合理性，还应考虑能否获得可持续资金、充足设施和有效管理。阿卡比奥由少数党副党鞭、易卜拉欣·穆斯塔法参议员代表出席。他表示，尼日利亚需要能够将研究成果转化为工业生产、减少对进口技术依赖，并使年轻人获得技能、参与全球竞争的机构。他把人力资源称为尼日尔三角洲最大的财富，并表示，拟议大学有助于应对环境退化和为当地沿河社区面临的挑战开发解决方案。阿卡比奥指出，清洁能源、环境保护、农业和渔业将是该校通过研究与创新作出重大贡献的领域。他说，该大学应培养拥有知识和创新能力的毕业生，以支持国家发展。不过，参议院议长提醒，增加大学数量不应成为高等教育政策的唯一目标，并强调教育机会必须与学术卓越、充足资金和长期可持续性相匹配。他敦促各方认真审议该法案，并提出有助于国民议会基于国家利益作出明智决定 的建议。此前，丹杜塞表示，公开听证会为利益相关方参与拟议立法提供了包容性平台。他说，委员会将审查拟议大学的治理结构、资金安排、学术重点、人员配置、基础设施，以及其遵守现行高等教育法律的情况。委员会主席补充说，将特别关注该机构的长期生存能力，以确保该大学一旦获批，便能为学生和国家带来切实利益。法案发起人、巴耶尔萨州中部选区参议员本森·孔博韦表示，拟议大学将有助于缓解技术人才短缺，尤其是在科学、技术和其他专业领域。孔博韦认为，尼日利亚需要在国内培养更多专业人员，而不是依赖外国人才来满足关键技术和工业领域的人力需求。他说，在尼日尔三角洲设立该大学，将为年轻人提供更多学习科学相关课程、获取与所在社区及全国相关技能的机会。这位议员感谢参议院领导层和委员会成员考虑该提案，并称这是加强该地区科学和技术教育的机会。巴耶尔萨州州长杜耶·迪里的技术顾问蒂米迪·瓦里奥韦先生也出席听证会。他说，位于南伊贾奥地方政府区域的科罗科罗塞已有可支持拟议大学建设的基础设施。他列举了这个沿河社区现有的设施，包括一所拥有数栋建筑的中学、一处医疗设施、酒店和一个登陆码头。瓦里奥韦补充说，通往该社区的道路正在施工，并对改善交通条件将支持拟议机构发展表示乐观。他还表示，州政府已在全州8个地方政府区域设立技术学院，以培养科学和技术领域的实用技能。据他介绍，拟议大学将为这些学院的毕业生提供接受继续教育、 advanced training和获得专业知识的机会。本文所述评论仅代表发言者观点，不代表《Vanguard》报及其任何员工的意见。

https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/us-s.body: Layer 1 The United States government has revoked the citizenship of a Nigerian-born woman, Vivian Chike Obichere, for concealing her previous fraudulent passport activities during her naturalisation process. The US Department of Justice announced that the US District Court for the Northern District of California revoked Obichere’s citizenship on October 13, after determining that she had illegally obtained naturalisation by lying to immigration authorities. According to the department, Obichere fraudulently used the identity of a US citizen to obtain an American passport and later concealed the scheme while applying for citizenship. In 1992, Obichere allegedly used the name, Social Security number, birthplace and date of birth of a US citizen identified as “C.C.O.” to obtain a US passport illegally. In 2003, Obichere became a lawful permanent resident of the United States under her real identity. However, in 2012, she again attempted to renew the fraudulent passport issued under the alias C.C.O., while simultaneously applying for US citizenship under her real name. During her naturalisation interview, Obichere testified under oath that she had never used the name C.C.O., despite knowing the statement was false, the Justice Department said. She became a naturalised US citizen in 2013, even as the authorities’ investigation into her activities was unfolding. In 2015, Obichere was convicted of making a false statement in an application and using a passport by the US District Court for the Northern District of California. As part of the criminal proceedings, she admitted to making the false statements and other lies to the US government over several years. The Department of Justice filed a civil complaint seeking to revoke her citizenship on July 30. On October 7, both parties filed a joint motion requesting a consent judgment to revoke her naturalisation. The court subsequently issued the judgment on October 13, formally stripping Obichere of her US citizenship. Commenting on the cases, Assistant Attorney General Brett A. Shumate of the Justice Department’s Civil Division said denaturalisation was a measure against individuals who concealed criminal activities or defrauded the American people. “Securing denaturalization is the final step to strip citizenship from those who conceal crimes or defraud the American people,” Shumate said. “This administration will continue its historic denaturalization campaign to protect the value of U.S. citizenship.” The department also announced the revocation of the citizenship of Milagros Marileisis Acosta Torres, a Cuban-born woman convicted of conspiring to commit money laundering. Acosta Torres obtained US citizenship in 2015 but was later convicted in 2020 over her involvement in a scheme to defraud a tribal casino in Florida. She was sentenced to six months in prison and ordered to pay nearly $150,000 in restitution. Her citizenship was revoked by the US District Court for the Southern District of Florida on October 14. https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/us-s.title_zh: 美国在尼日利亚女子通过欺诈取得公民身份13年后剥夺其公民身份
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/us-s.body_zh: 第一层 美国政府撤销了一名出生于尼日利亚的 woman's citizenship，她叫 Vivien Chike Obichere，原因是在归化过程中隐瞒了自己此前使用欺诈护照的活动。美国司法部宣布，加利福尼亚州北区联邦地区法院于10月13日撤销了 Obichere 的公民身份，原因是认定她通过向移民当局撒谎而非法取得了归化身份。司法部称，Obichere 冒用一名美国公民的身份获取美国护照，后来在申请公民身份时隐瞒了这一骗局。1992年，Obichere 据称冒用一名代号为“C.C.O.”的美国公民的姓名、社会安全号码、出生地和出生日期，非法取得美国护照。2003年，Obichere 以真实身份成为美国合法永久居民。然而，2012年，她再次试图以 C.C.O. 的别名更新那本欺诈签发的护照，同时又以真实姓名申请美国公民身份。在归化面谈中，司法部称，Obichere 宣誓作证称自己从未使用过 C.C.O. 这个姓名，尽管她知道该陈述是虚假的。尽管当局正在调查她的活动，她仍于2013年成为归化美国公民。2015年，加利福尼亚州北区联邦地区法院判定 Obichere 在申请中作出虚假陈述并使用护照，构成犯罪。作为刑事诉讼的一部分，她承认多年来曾向美国政府作出虚假陈述并编造其他谎言。司法部于7月30日提起民事诉讼，寻求撤销她的公民身份。10月7日，双方共同提交动议，请求法院作出撤销其归化身份的合意判决。法院随后于10月13日作出判决，正式剥夺了 Obichere 的美国公民身份。司法部民事部门助理总检察长 Brett A. Shumate 在评论这些案件时表示，取消归化身份是针对隐瞒犯罪活动或欺骗美国民众人士的措施。Shumate 说：“确保取消归化身份，是剥夺那些隐瞒罪行或欺骗美国民众者公民身份的最后一步。本届政府将继续推进历史性的取消归化行动，以维护美国公民身份的价值。”司法部还宣布撤销了 Milagros Marileisis Acosta Torres 的公民身份。她是一名出生于古巴的女子，曾因共谋洗钱被判罪。Acosta Torres 于2015年取得美国公民身份，但后来因参与诈骗佛罗里达州一家部落赌场而被判有罪，判决时间为2020年。她被判处6个月监禁，并被要求支付近$150,000的赔偿金。佛罗里达州南区联邦地区法院于10月14日撤销了她的公民身份。本文所载评论不代表 Vanguard 各报或任何员工的观点

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/22/e.body: The Minister of Information and National Orientation, Alhaji Mohammed Idris, has directed agencies under his ministry to intensify public education on Ebola Virus Disease (EVD). According to a statement issued by the minister’s Media Aide, Rabiu Ibrahim, the agencies include the National Orientation Agency (NOA), Nigerian Television Authority (NTA) and Federal Radio Corporation of Nigeria (FRCN). Others are the Voice of Nigeria (VON) and the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN ). The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) had confirmed a case of Ebola involving a woman who recently travelled to Abuja from Uganda. The woman is in isolation and receiving treatment, while health authorities have identified her contacts and are monitoring them. The minister said: “The Federal Government is taking every necessary step to contain this case and protect Nigerians. Accurate and timely information is one of our strongest defences. Idris directed the agencies to collaborate with the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare and the NCDC to ensure all public information is verified and evidence-based. He also tasked the NOA with deploying its nationwide offices for grassroots sensitisation, in collaboration with traditional and religious leaders, community groups and the media. The minister urged Nigerians to remain calm, rely on official information and avoid spreading unverified claims on social media. He advised members of the public to report suspected cases immediately by calling the NCDC’s toll-free, 24-hour emergency line on 6232. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/22/s.body: *Moves to check alleged illegal management structures in public, private institutions The Senate on Thursday moved to investigate the governing structures of public and private universities across Nigeria over alleged violations of statutory requirements, as it intensified efforts to strengthen regulatory oversight, improve research funding and protect vulnerable coastal communities from environmental devastation. The upper chamber resolved to constitute an ad hoc committee to investigate Tansian University, Umunya, Anambra State, and other tertiary institutions following allegations that some universities had adopted management structures inconsistent with established governance regulations. The decision followed a motion by Senator Victor Umeh (Anambra Central), who raised concerns about the alleged operation of corporate-style management structures, including managing directors and executive directors, in some private universities. The development came during consideration of the National Universities Commission Act, 2026 (SB. 1056), sponsored by Senate Leader Opeyemi Bamidele, which seeks to strengthen the regulatory authority of the National Universities Commission (NUC) over the establishment, administration, monitoring and management of universities and other degree-awarding institutions. Umeh alleged that Tansian University had failed to comply with existing regulatory provisions despite sanctions imposed by the NUC. According to him, rather than operate a board of trustees as required, the institution was allegedly headed by an executive director who exercised powers to appoint and dismiss vice-chancellors at will. He argued that such practices undermined established university governance standards and weakened the commission’s capacity to enforce compliance. Responding, Senate President Godswill Akpabio called for a comprehensive investigation to establish whether the university and other institutions had violated applicable laws. “This consideration of the bill does not preclude our committees on Basic and Tertiary Education from bringing to the Senate the university so named for necessary action,” he said. Akpabio specifically called for an ad hoc committee to “investigate where it got its powers from to have directors”. He warned against allowing alleged regulatory breaches to persist until the proposed legislation came into force. “Even before the law takes effect, we must bring erring private and public universities to order so that we don’t end up degrading the standards of education this country,” the Senate President said. He further warned that weaknesses in university administration could undermine public confidence in Nigerian academic qualifications and the credibility of certificates awarded by the institutions. The proposed legislation seeks to modernise the legal framework for university regulation, strengthen accreditation and enforcement mechanisms, improve institutional governance and update the composition and functions of the NUC governing board. Presenting the bill on behalf of Bamidele, Senate Chief Whip Tahir Monguno said the existing law required an overhaul to reflect the expansion of private universities, technological advancement, globalisation and changing national development priorities. The bill was referred to the Senate Committee on Tertiary Institutions and TETFund, which was given four weeks to report back. In a related development, the Senate passed for second reading a bill seeking to establish a National Research and Innovation Development Fund, with a proposed annual allocation of 20 per cent of the Nigerian Content Development Fund. Monguno said Nigeria possessed the universities, polytechnics, research institutes and technology entrepreneurs needed to drive innovation but lacked a sustainable framework to coordinate research activities and translate discoveries into commercially viable products. “The importance of research and innovation to national development cannot be overemphasised. In a rapidly evolving global economy driven by science, technology, industrial advancement and the application of knowledge, the capacity of a nation to generate ideas, develop indigenous technologies and translate research findings into practical solutions is critical to its economic competitiveness and prosperity,” he said. He added that the proposed fund would ensure that research extended beyond academic publications and laboratory experiments. “It recognises that research should not remain confined to academic publications or institutional laboratories, but should be translated, where viable, into goods, services, technologies and practical solutions capable of improving the lives of Nigerians,” Monguno said. Under the bill, the fund would receive 20 per cent of the Nigerian Content Development Fund annually, alongside government appropriations, grants, donations, investment income and proceeds from patents and commercialisation. Its resources would support research grants, infrastructure, product development, indigenous technology, intellectual property protection and technology transfer. Administrative expenditure would be capped at 25 per cent of the annual contribution from the Nigerian Content Development Fund. Contributing, Senator Samson Ekong lamented the country’s neglect of research and innovation. “Research and innovation, we would have gone far in this country if we had taken these two aspects of education seriously,” he said. He asked: “How do we catch up when we ignore research, when we ignore innovation?” The bill was also referred to the Committee on Tertiary Institutions and TETFund for consideration and a report within four weeks. Meanwhile, the Senate has urged the Federal Government to urgently intervene to prevent further destruction of Aiyetoro community in Ilaje Local Government Area of Ondo State by Atlantic Ocean surges. The resolution followed a motion sponsored by Senator Dayo Faduyile, who raised concerns over the destruction of homes, schools, healthcare facilities and other public infrastructure. Lawmakers noted reports indicating that approximately 80 per cent of buildings in the coastal community had been lost to sea incursion, threatening residents’ livelihoods, cultural heritage and continued habitation. The Senate called on the Federal Ministry of Environment, the Niger Delta Development Commission, the Ondo State Government and the Ondo State Oil Producing Areas Development Commission to collaborate on a comprehensive shoreline protection programme. It also demanded a transparent review of previous and ongoing shoreline protection contracts to establish their funding, implementation status, outstanding obligations and completion timelines. The chamber further urged the National Emergency Management Agency and relevant state authorities to provide the affected residents with safe water, healthcare assistance and temporary shelter. Amending the motion’s prayers, Ekong called for the inclusion of affected communities in Akwa Ibom South in the proposed federal intervention. Supporting the amendment, Akpabio stressed the need for a broader national approach to shoreline protection. “Some of these things are above the resources of the state, and that is why these issues are being brought here to the Senate,” he said. The Senate mandated its Committees on Environment, Niger Delta Development Commission and Special Duties to monitor implementation and report back within four weeks. The Committee on Legislative Compliance was also directed to monitor adherence to the resolutions. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/22/s.title_zh: 参议院调查高校管理机构，并寻求改革国家大学委员会
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/22/s.body_zh:
参议院着手调查公立、私立机构涉嫌违法的管理架构

参议院周四着手调查尼日利亚公立和私立大学的治理架构，原因是这些大学被指控违反法定要求。参议院正加大力度强化监管监督、改善科研经费保障，并保护脆弱的沿海社区，使其免遭环境灾难。

上院决定成立一个特设委员会，调查位于阿南布拉州乌穆尼亚的Tansian University以及其他高等教育机构。此前有指控称，一些大学采用了与现行治理规章不一致的管理架构。

这项决定源于参议员Victor Umeh（阿南布拉中选区）提出的一项动议。他对一些私立大学涉嫌实行公司式管理架构提出关切，包括设置董事总经理和执行董事等职位。

此事发生在参议院审议《2026年国家大学委员会法》（SB. 1056）之际。该法案由参议院领袖Opeyemi Bamidele发起，旨在加强国家大学委员会（NUC）对大学及其他学位授予机构的设立、运营、监督和管理等方面的监管权力。

Umeh指控，尽管国家大学委员会已经实施制裁，Tansian University仍未遵守现行监管规定。据他称，该校没有按照要求设立受托人董事会，而是由一名执行董事负责校务，并可任意任命和撤换副校长。他认为，此类做法破坏大学既定治理标准，并削弱委员会执行合规要求的能力。

参议院议长Godswill Akpabio回应称，应开展全面调查，查明该大学及其他机构是否违反适用法律。

他说：“现在审议这项法案，并不妨碍我们基础教育委员会和高等教育委员会将上述大学提交参议院采取必要行动。”

Akpabio特别要求成立特设委员会，“调查该校设立董事职位的权力来源”。他警告，不能任由涉嫌违反监管规定的行为持续到拟议法律生效为止。

参议院议长说：“即使法律尚未生效，我们也必须惩治违规的私立和公立大学，不能让这个国家的教育标准因此下降。”

他还警告，大学管理中的薄弱环节可能损害公众对尼日利亚学历的信任，以及高校所颁发证书的可信度。

拟议法律旨在更新大学监管法律框架，强化认证和执法机制，改善机构治理，并更新国家大学委员会理事会的组成和职能。

参议院党鞭Tahir Monguno代表Bamidele介绍法案时表示，现行法律需要全面改革，以反映私立大学扩张、技术进步、全球化以及国家发展重点的变化。

法案已提交参议院高等教育机构与TETFund委员会审议，该委员会须在四周内提交报告。

与此同时，参议院通过一项法案的二读阶段。该法案拟设立国家研究与创新发展基金，建议每年从尼日利亚本土内容发展基金中划拨20 per cent。

Monguno表示，尼日利亚拥有推动创新所需的大学、理工学院、研究机构和技术创业者，但缺乏协调研究活动、将研究发现转化为具有商业可行性产品的可持续框架。

他说：“研究创新对国家发展的重要性怎么强调都不为过。在由科学、技术、工业进步和知识应用驱动的快速演变全球经济中，一个国家产生创意、开发本土技术并将研究成果转化为实际解决方案的能力，对其经济竞争力和繁荣至关重要。”

他补充说，拟议基金将确保研究超越学术出版物和实验室试验的范畴。

Monguno说：“该基金承认，研究不应局限于学术出版物或机构实验室；在具备商业可行性的情况下，还应将其转化为商品、服务、技术和能够改善尼日利亚人民生活的实际解决方案。”

根据法案，该基金每年将获得尼日利亚本土内容发展基金20 per cent的资金，同时还可获得政府拨款、赠款、捐赠、投资收益以及专利和商业化所得。其资源将用于支持研究资助、基础设施建设、产品开发、本土技术、知识产权保护和技术转让。行政支出上限为尼日利亚本土内容发展基金年度出资的25 per cent。

参议员Samson Ekong在发言时，对国家忽视研究与创新表示遗憾。

他说：“如果我们认真对待教育和科研创新的这两个方面，这个国家本可以走得更远。”

他问道：“当我们忽视研究、忽视创新时，又怎能追赶上来？”

该法案也已提交高等教育机构与TETFund委员会审议，并要求在四周内提交报告。

另一方面，参议院敦促联邦政府紧急干预，防止大西洋海浪继续破坏奥多州Ilaje地方政府辖区Aiyetoro社区。

这项决议源于参议员Dayo Faduyile提出的一项动议。他对住宅、学校、医疗设施及其他公共基础设施遭到破坏表示关切。

议员们注意到相关报告称，这个沿海社区约80 per cent的建筑物已被海水侵袭摧毁，居民的生计、文化遗产和持续居住均受到威胁。

参议院呼吁联邦环境部、尼日尔河三角洲发展委员会、奥多州政府和奥多州产油地区发展委员会协作，制定全面的海岸线保护计划。

参议院还要求对以往及正在执行的海岸线保护合同进行透明审查，查明其资金来源、实施进展、尚未履行的义务以及完工时间表。

上院进一步敦促国家紧急事务管理局和州内相关当局向受灾居民提供安全饮用水、医疗援助和临时住所。

Ekong对动议中的请求提出修正，要求将阿夸伊博姆南部的受灾社区纳入拟议的联邦干预措施。

Akpabio支持这项修正，并强调海岸线保护需要采取覆盖全国范围的更广泛举措。

他说：“其中一些事务超出了州政府的资源能力，因此这些问题才会被带到参议院。”

参议院授权其环境委员会、尼日尔河三角洲发展委员会和特别事务委员会监督执行情况，并在四周内提交报告。立法合规委员会也被要求监督各项决议的遵守情况。

Roy Vincent Trinidad told reporters at Camp Aguinaldo in Quezon City. “We need not seek the clearance nor the approval of any foreign power to perform our mandate,” he added. READ: Teodoro: Ayungin resupply to push through despite China interference In a statement published on China’s Ministry of National Defense website on Wednesday, China Coast Guard (CCG) spokesperson Jiang Lue claimed that Beijing had permitted the Philippines to deliver supplies to the BRP Sierra Madre at Ayungin Shoal, which China calls Ren’ai Jiao. Jiang also claimed that the CCG had questioned and verified the Philippine vessel involved in the delivery and monitored the entire operation. “On October 21, with China’s permission, the Philippines transported supplies to its vessel illegally grounded on Ren’ai Reef,” the CCG statement read. “The China Coast Guard questioned and confirmed the incident with the Philippine vessel and monitored the entire process.” Trinidad confirmed that the AFP successfully completed the rotation and reprovisioning (RoRe) mission but declined to disclose whether Chinese vessels had attempted to interfere with the operation. “It was successfully concluded,” he said when pressed on possible Chinese interference. The latest mission followed an unsuccessful resupply attempt in September, when Philippine forces suspended their operation over safety concerns amid the presence of Chinese vessels. Asked what had changed between the two missions, Trinidad replied: “Last September, hindi natuloy. This time natuloy (Last September, it did not push through. This time, it did).” He declined to elaborate, citing operational considerations. Trinidad also accused Beijing of repeatedly inventing narratives to justify its territorial and maritime claims, citing its assertions over Panatag (Scarborough) Shoal and Batanes. “Nag-i-imbento lamang sila ng naratibo at wala namang naniniwala sa kanila (They are merely inventing narratives, and nobody believes them),” he said. “Wag tayo mabigla, baka pati Pluto e angkinin na rin nila (Don’t be surprised if they eventually claim even Pluto),” he quipped. “These type of narratives, consider them as inventions and they are jokes, laugh at them,” Trinidad added. He stressed that the military would continue conducting resupply missions, maritime patrols and surveillance flights regardless of China’s objections. “Let this be very clear, the AFP will keep performing its mandate not only doing the RoRe but our MDA flights, our maritime patrols, our air surveillance flights. This will continue long into the future,” he said. The Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) has maintained that the provisional understanding reached by Manila and Beijing in July 2024 for resupply missions to Ayungin Shoal does not require Chinese permission. During a House budget hearing in September, Foreign Affairs Secretary Ma. Theresa Lazaro clarified that the arrangement involved only an exchange of information between the two countries. Ayungin Shoal, located about 194 kilometers west of Palawan, lies within the Philippines’ exclusive economic zone. It is where the grounded BRP Sierra Madre serves as a military outpost. “谁信他们？他们每次都编造一套新说法，”西菲律宾海问题菲律宾军方发言人、海军少将罗伊·文森特·特立尼达在奎松市阿吉纳尔多营对记者说。“我们执行任务不需要任何外国势力的许可或批准，”他补充道。延伸阅读：特奥多罗：尽管中国干扰，阿云金运送补给任务仍将推进
周三在中国国防部网站发布的一份声明中，中国海警局发言人蒋璐声称，北京方面已允许菲律宾向阿云金浅滩（中国称仁爱礁）上的菲律宾海军巡逻舰“马德雷山脉”号运送补给。蒋璐还声称，中国海警局对参与此次运送任务的菲律宾船只进行了询问和核实，并监控了整个行动过程。
中国海警局声明称：“10月21日，经中方允许，菲律宾向其非法‘坐滩’于仁爱礁的船只运送了补给。中方海警对菲方船只所涉事件进行了询问和确认，并对全过程进行了监管。”
特立尼达证实，菲律宾武装部队成功完成了轮换和补给任务，但拒绝透露中国船只是否曾试图干扰此次行动。被追问中方可能存在的干扰行为时，他表示：“任务已经圆满完成。”
此次任务是继9月一次失败的补给尝试之后进行的。当时，出于安全考虑，加之中国船只在场，菲律宾军方中止了行动。
当被问及两次任务之间发生了什么变化时，特立尼达回答说：“上个月9月，没能完成；这次完成了。”他以作战需要为由拒绝进一步说明。
特立尼达还指责北京方面反复编造说法来为其领土和海洋主张辩护，并列举了其在帕纳塔格浅滩（即黄岩岛）和巴丹群岛问题上的立场。
“他们只是在编造叙事，没人会信他们，”他说。他还打趣道：“别大惊小怪，说不定他们连冥王星都要宣称是自己的了。”
特立尼达补充说：“这类说法，权当是编造和玩笑，一笑置之即可。”他强调，无论中方是否反对，菲律宾军方都将持续执行补给任务、海上巡逻和侦察飞行。
“请务必明确这一点：菲律宾武装部队不仅将继续完成轮换和补给任务，还将持续开展海上防卫飞行、海上巡逻和空中侦察飞行。这项行动将长期持续下去，”他表示。
菲律宾外交部坚持认为，2024年7月马尼拉与北京就阿云金浅滩补给任务达成的临时安排，并不要求获得中方许可。在9月举行的众议院预算听证会上，外交部长玛丽亚·特雷莎·拉扎罗澄清说，该安排仅涉及两国之间的信息交流。
阿云金浅滩位于巴拉望岛以西约194公里处，处于菲律宾专属经济区范围内，搁浅的“马德雷山脉”号巡逻舰即在该处充当军事前哨站。
此次行动发生在此前约一个月，9月份菲律宾武装部队因中国海警、海军和海上民兵船只在场、出于安全考虑，中止了向“马德雷山脉”号巡逻舰运送补给的行动。
在9月的任务中，菲律宾部队遭遇的中方船只比以往行动时距离阿云金浅滩更远，菲律宾军方为避免人员安全风险而中止了行动。/dl
